definition_zh: 有益的；有利的；有助益的
definition_en: producing a helpful or advantageous effect on someone or something
core_image: 一只手把好处递出去，接住的人因此变得更好
scene: The doctor told her that thirty minutes of walking a day would be beneficial to her heart.
sceneCN: 这里 beneficial 是「有益的」（第 3 个义项：对健康有好处）；句意：医生告诉她，每天走三十分钟对她的心脏有益。场景要点：诊室、处方笺、计步器、心脏模型、水杯。

pos.zh: 有益的；有利的；有助益的

collocations.zh: （法律）实际受益人；受益所有人

senses.title: Producing a good effect
senses.titleCN: 有益的：带来好效果
senses.definition: producing a good or useful effect on something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事物产生良好或有用效果的
senses.example: The new drainage system proved beneficial to the whole neighbourhood.
senses.exampleCN: 新的排水系统证明对整个街区都有益。
senses.why: Bene- means 'well' and -fic- means 'making, doing'; -ial makes the whole thing an adjective of relation. Literally 'doing well to' something. The word names the effect on the receiver, not the intention of the giver.
senses.whyCN: bene- 意为“好”，-fic- 意为“做、使”，-ial 使整个词成为关系形容词，字面即“对某物做好事”。这个词命名的是接受方所得到的效果，而不是给予方的意图。

senses.title: Advantageous to a party
senses.titleCN: 有利的：让某一方占到好处
senses.definition: giving a person or group an advantage or profit
senses.definitionCN: 给某个人或群体带来优势或收益的
senses.example: A lower exchange rate is beneficial to exporters.
senses.exampleCN: 较低的汇率对出口商有利。
senses.why: A good effect on a person can be counted: more money, a stronger position. The same 'do well' is now read as measurable advantage, which is why the word so often takes 'to' plus a beneficiary.
senses.whyCN: 对人的好效果可以计量：更多收入、更有利的地位。同一个“做好事”在这里被读成可衡量的优势，所以这个词常接 to 加受益方。

senses.title: Good for health
senses.titleCN: 有益健康的：对身体有好处
senses.definition: having a good effect on the body or on health
senses.definitionCN: 对身体或健康有良好作用的
senses.example: Regular sleep is beneficial for the immune system.
senses.exampleCN: 规律睡眠对免疫系统有益。
senses.why: Health is the most concrete good effect on a living body. The fixed phrase 'beneficial to health' froze this sense, so the adjective can now be used almost as a medical recommendation.
senses.whyCN: 健康是活着的身体上最具体的好效果。固定搭配 beneficial to health 把这个义项凝固下来，于是这个形容词几乎可以当作一条医学建议来用。

senses.title: Helpful in agriculture and ecology
senses.titleCN: 有益的（生物）：对作物或生态有帮助
senses.definition: of an organism: helpful to plants, crops, or an ecosystem rather than harmful
senses.definitionCN: （指生物）对植物、作物或生态系统有帮助而非有害的
senses.example: Ladybirds are beneficial insects in a garden.
senses.exampleCN: 瓢虫是花园里的益虫。
senses.why: In applied biology the receiver of the good effect is a crop or an ecosystem, and the doer is another organism. Beneficial then becomes a label for a species, opposed to pest.
senses.whyCN: 在应用生物学里，好效果的接受方是作物或生态系统，施加方是另一种生物。于是 beneficial 成了给物种贴的标签，与 pest（害虫）相对。

senses.title: Legal: entitled to the real benefit
senses.titleCN: 实际受益的：衡平法上的受益权
senses.definition: in law, having the right to enjoy property while another person holds the legal title
senses.definitionCN: （法律）享有实际利益的所有权，而法定名义由他人持有的
senses.example: The court asked who the beneficial owner of the account really was.
senses.exampleCN: 法院询问这个账户的实际受益人究竟是谁。
senses.why: Here beneficial does not mean 'nice'. It names the person who actually enjoys the benefit, as opposed to the nominal holder. The old sense 'pertaining to a favor or benefit' survives in this technical branch.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 beneficial 不是“善良”的意思，而是指真正享有利益的人，与名义上的持有人相对。古老的“与恩惠、利益有关”这一层意思就活在这个法律分支里。

senses.title: Mutually advantageous
senses.titleCN: 互利的：双方都得到好处
senses.definition: producing advantage for both sides of a relationship or agreement
senses.definitionCN: 对关系或协议的双方都产生优势的
senses.example: The two countries signed a mutually beneficial trade agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 两国签署了一项互利的贸易协定。
senses.why: When both sides receive the good effect, beneficial describes a relation rather than a one-way gift. The adjective can therefore attach to agreements, partnerships and exchanges, not only to acts of giving.
senses.whyCN: 当双方都得到好效果时，beneficial 描述的是一个关系，而不是单向的赠与。因此它可以修饰协定、伙伴关系和交换，而不只是“给予”这个动作。

senses.title: Therapeutic: good medical effect
senses.titleCN: 有疗效的：药物的有益作用
senses.definition: producing a good effect as a treatment or medicine
senses.definitionCN: 作为治疗或药物产生良好效果的
senses.example: The beneficial effects of the drug appeared after about a week.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药的有益效果大约一周后显现。
senses.why: Medicine speaks of effects rather than intentions. A drug is beneficial when its action leaves the body better, even if the same substance would be harmful in another dose.
senses.whyCN: 医学谈的是效果，不是意图。一种药之所以 beneficial，是因为它的作用让身体变好，哪怕同一物质在别的剂量下会有害。

senses.title: Good in the long run
senses.titleCN: 长远有益的：苦口良药
senses.definition: having a good final result even though the immediate experience is unpleasant
senses.definitionCN: 尽管当下体验不佳、但最终结果良好的
senses.example: The failure was a beneficial shock: it forced the team to rethink the design.
senses.exampleCN: 这次失败是一次有益的警醒：它迫使团队重新思考设计。
senses.why: Benefit can be delayed. When the immediate experience is bad but the later outcome is good, beneficial still applies, because the word measures the end state rather than the comfort of the moment.
senses.whyCN: 好处可以迟到。当当下体验很糟、而后来结果很好时，beneficial 仍然适用，因为这个词衡量的是终点状态，而不是此刻的舒适。

senses.title: A good influence on people
senses.titleCN: 有益的影响：作用于人心与社会
senses.definition: having a good moral or social influence on people
senses.definitionCN: 对人产生良好道德或社会影响的
senses.example: Her beneficial influence on the younger students was obvious.
senses.exampleCN: 她对低年级学生的有益影响显而易见。
senses.why: The receiver can be a mind or a community, not only a body or a purse. The 'good done' is then moral or social, which is the widest extension of the core image: the effect lands on character.
senses.whyCN: 接受方可以是心智或共同体，而不只是身体或钱包。这时“所做的善”是道德或社会层面的，这是核心意象最宽的延伸：效果落在品格上。

intro.en: Beneficial is a Latin adjective that reached English through French in the 15th century. Its two Latin pieces are still visible: bene- 'well' and -fic- 'making, doing'. The church word benefice is a cousin from the same noun, but it took a different branch.
intro.cn: beneficial 是一个拉丁形容词，15 世纪经由法语进入英语。它的两块拉丁成分至今可见：bene-“好”和 -fic-“做、使”。教会用语 benefice 出自同一个名词，但走的是另一条分支。

items.en: bene is an adverb meaning 'well, in the right way, honorably, properly'. It goes back to PIE *deu- 'to do, perform; show favor', and is also the source of Latin bonus 'good' and bellus 'fine, pretty'.
items.cn: bene 是副词，意为“好、以正确的方式、体面地、恰当地”。它追溯到原始印欧语 *deu-“做、执行；施恩”，也是拉丁语 bonus“好”和 bellus“漂亮、精致”的来源。

items.en: facere means 'to do, to make' (PIE *dhe- 'to set, put'). Its combining form -ficere, with the adjective ending -ficus 'making, doing', appears in beneficus, efficere and magnificus.
items.cn: facere 意为“做、制造”（原始印欧语 *dhe-“放置”）。它的组合形式 -ficere 与形容词词尾 -ficus“做……的、使……的”出现在 beneficus、efficere、magnificus 里。

items.en: beneficus 'generous, kind, obliging' literally means 'doing well'. The noun beneficium 'a favor, service, kindness' adds -ium. English draws two different words from this node: benefit, and the church benefice, where the 'benefit' is an ecclesiastical office with its income.
items.cn: beneficus“慷慨的、善良的、乐于助人的”字面就是“做好事”。名词 beneficium“恩惠、服务、善意”加上 -ium。英语从这个节点分出两个不同的词：benefit，以及教会用语 benefice——那里的“好处”是一份带收入的圣职。

items.en: Late Latin beneficialis 'pertaining to a favor' adds -alis, the relational adjective ending, to the stem beneficial-. English takes this stem whole, so beneficial is structurally 'of or belonging to a beneficium'.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 beneficialis“与恩惠有关的”在词干 beneficial- 上加 -alis（关系形容词词尾）。英语把整个词干接过来，所以 beneficial 在结构上就是“属于 beneficium 的”。

items.en: Mid-15c English beneficial came from Old French bénéficial and directly from Latin, with the first recorded sense 'helpful, advantageous, conferring benefit'. The adverb beneficially follows the same path.
items.cn: 15 世纪中期的英语 beneficial 来自古法语 bénéficial，并直接借自拉丁语，最早记录的义项是“有帮助的、有利的、带来好处的”。副词 beneficially 走同一条路径。

items.en: The sense moved from 'pertaining to a favor' to 'producing a good effect', because a favor is by definition something good for the receiver. Legal usage kept the older reading in beneficial owner, the person who actually enjoys the benefit. Beneficial is not the same derivative chain as beneficiary: -alis made a quality adjective, while -arius made a personal noun.
items.cn: 词义从“与恩惠有关”转向“产生好效果”，因为恩惠按定义就是对接受方好的东西。法律用法在 beneficial owner（实际受益人）里保留了较老的一层：真正享有利益的人。beneficial 与 beneficiary 不是同一条派生链：-alis 造的是性质形容词，-arius 造的是指人的名词。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin base bene- + facere but splits into different suffixes and different word classes; the second group contains adjectives that come close in meaning but measure different things.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁词基 bene- + facere，但分裂成不同的后缀和词性；第二组是意思接近、但衡量对象不同的形容词。

entries.definition: A person or organization that receives money or an advantage from a will, policy or trust. The -ary suffix marks the receiver, not the quality.
entries.definitionCN: 从遗嘱、保单或信托中获得钱财或好处的人或机构。-ary 后缀标记的是接受者，而不是性质。

entries.definition: Kind and generous by character. It describes the giver's disposition, while beneficial describes the effect on the receiver.
entries.definitionCN: 生性善良慷慨的。它描述给予者的品性，而 beneficial 描述接受方所得到的效果。

entries.definition: A church office together with its income. It comes from beneficium 'benefit granted', but the sense is an ecclesiastical post, not 'helpful'.
entries.definitionCN: 教会圣职及其附属收入。它来自 beneficium“授予的好处”，但词义是教会职位，与“有益的”无关。

entries.definition: The noun 'an advantage or profit' and the verb 'to help or to gain'. Beneficial is the adjective built on the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 名词“好处、利益”，动词“有益于；受益”。beneficial 就是同一词干上构成的形容词。

entries.definition: Giving a practical edge or profit. It is more competitive in tone than beneficial and usually implies someone gains relative to others.
entries.definitionCN: 带来实际优势或收益的。它比 beneficial 更带竞争意味，通常暗示某人相对于他人占了上风。

entries.definition: Giving practical help. Plainer and more about assistance than about a good final outcome.
entries.definitionCN: 提供实际帮助的。更朴素，侧重“帮上忙”，而不是最终的好结果。

entries.definition: Presenting conditions that help success; often used of weather, odds or circumstances rather than of effects on health.
entries.definitionCN: 呈现有利于成功的条件；常用于天气、胜算、环境，而不是对健康的作用。

entries.definition: Yielding financial gain. Narrower than beneficial, which need not involve money at all.
entries.definitionCN: 产生经济收益的。比 beneficial 窄，因为 beneficial 完全可以与金钱无关。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分和真实的同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: bene- 'well' + -fic- 'do, make' + -ial: beneficial is literally 'doing well to' someone.
normal.cn: bene-“好”+ -fic-“做”+ -ial：beneficial 字面就是“对某人做好事”。

normal.en: The same -fic- appears in efficient, sufficient and magnificent, all built on facere 'to do, make'.
normal.cn: 同一个 -fic- 还出现在 efficient、sufficient、magnificent 里，它们都建立在 facere“做、造”上。

normal.en: Benefit, benefactor, beneficence and beneficial share one stem; only the suffix changes the part of speech.
normal.cn: benefit、benefactor、beneficence、beneficial 共享一个词干，只有后缀在改变词性。

normal.en: Fixed pairs show where the word lives: beneficial to health, beneficial effect, mutually beneficial.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示这个词活跃在哪里：beneficial to health、beneficial effect、mutually beneficial。

normal.en: The legal phrase beneficial owner names the person who actually enjoys the benefit, even when the title stands in another name.
normal.cn: 法律短语 beneficial owner 指的是真正享有利益的人，即使产权名义写在别人名下。

abstract.en: Picture an arrow leaving a giver and ending at a receiver with a plus sign above it: that plus is beneficial.
abstract.cn: 想象一支箭头从给予者出发，落在接受者身上，上方有一个加号：那个加号就是 beneficial。

abstract.en: Picture a bitter pill and a stronger body a week later: the good is measured at the end, not at the swallow.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗苦药和一周后更强健的身体：好处在终点被衡量，而不是在吞下的那一刻。

abstract.en: Picture a balance with benefit on one pan and harm (mal-) on the other; beneficial names the side that pulls the beam down.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平，一端的秤盘是好处，另一端是害处（mal-）；beneficial 就是让横梁沉下去的那一边。

examples.en: Regular exercise is beneficial to both physical and mental health.
examples.cn: 规律运动对身心健康都有益。

examples.en: The new policy proved beneficial to small farmers in the region.
examples.cn: 新政策证明对该地区的小农有益。

examples.en: They reached a mutually beneficial agreement on sharing the river water.
examples.cn: 他们就河水分配达成了一项互利协议。

dict_mnemonic.text: 本尼（benefi）把好处舍（she）给你，你自然受益 → beneficial 有益的、有利的

root: 拉丁 bene“好、善”+ -fic-（facere“做”）+ -ial“与……有关的”：字面即“行好、带来好处的”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses share one gesture: something good is done to a receiver, and the receiver ends up better. The receiver can be a body, a purse, property, a crop, or a mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项共享同一个动作：有人对接受方做了一件好事，接受方因此变得更好。接受方可以是身体、钱包、财产、作物，也可以是一颗心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: good done to a receiver, so the receiver ends up better.
core.cn: 核心意象：对接受方做好事，接受方因此变得更好。

branches.en: GOOD EFFECT ON A BODY: the receiver is a living body, and the good appears as health.
branches.cn: 作用于身体的好效果：接受方是活体，好处表现为健康。

branches.en: ADVANTAGE BETWEEN PARTIES: the good effect is counted as profit, or shared fairly in an exchange.
branches.cn: 各方之间的优势：好效果被算成收益，或在交换中被公平分享。

branches.en: APPLIED FIELDS: agriculture labels helpful species; medicine labels helpful drug effects.
branches.cn: 应用领域：农业用它标记有益的物种；医学用它标记有益的疗效。

branches.en: LEGAL SURVIVAL: beneficial owner keeps the older sense of the person who actually enjoys the benefit.
branches.cn: 法律中的存留：beneficial owner 保留了较老的一层——真正享有利益的人。

branches.en: DELAYED AND MORAL GOOD: the good may arrive later, or act on minds and society instead of bodies.
branches.cn: 延迟的善与道德层面的善：好处可以后来才到，也可以作用于人心与社会而非身体。

intro.en: Beneficial is built entirely from Latin material: bene- + -fic- + -ial. For modern speakers only -ial and the -fic- combining form are transparent; bene- is a learned prefix, not a free word.
intro.cn: beneficial 完全由拉丁材料构成：bene- + -fic- + -ial。对现代使用者来说，只有 -ial 和组合形式 -fic- 是透明的；bene- 是学术前缀，不是自由词。

latinIntro.en: Latin bene 'well' and facere 'to make' supply a large family: benefit, benefactor, beneficence, beneficent, beneficial. The same -fic- appears in efficient, sufficient, magnificent, manufacture and factory.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 bene“好”和 facere“做”供应了一个大词族：benefit、benefactor、beneficence、beneficent、beneficial。同一个 -fic- 也出现在 efficient、sufficient、magnificent、manufacture、factory 里。

items.meaning: a good deed or advantage; to be useful to
items.meaningCN: 好处；善行；有益于（bene-“好”+ factum“所做之事”）
items.example: The new bus route is a benefit to commuters.
items.exampleCN: 新的公交线路对通勤者是一项福利。

items.meaning: producing a good effect
items.meaningCN: 有益的；产生良好效果的（bene-“好”+ -fic-“做”+ -ial“与……有关”）
items.example: Moderate exercise is beneficial to the heart.
items.exampleCN: 适度运动对心脏有益。

items.meaning: a person who gives help, especially money
items.meaningCN: 施惠者；捐助者（-tor 表示做动作的人）
items.example: An anonymous benefactor paid for the new library.
items.exampleCN: 一位匿名捐助者出资修建了新图书馆。

items.meaning: the quality of doing good; generosity
items.meaningCN: 善行；仁慈；施惠（-ence 构成性质或行为名词）
items.example: The hospital was founded through the beneficence of a local family.
items.exampleCN: 这家医院是靠当地一个家族的善举创办的。

items.meaning: kind and generous in action
items.meaningCN: 行善的；仁慈慷慨的（-ent 表示“正在做……的”）
items.example: A beneficent uncle paid her tuition.
items.exampleCN: 一位仁慈的叔叔为她付了学费。

items.meaning: a person who receives a benefit
items.meaningCN: 受益人；受惠者（-ary 表示“与……有关的人”）
items.example: She named her sister as the sole beneficiary.
items.exampleCN: 她指定妹妹为唯一受益人。

items.meaning: a church office with its income
items.meaningCN: 教会圣职及其俸禄（同一 beneficium 的另一条分支）
items.example: The priest was granted a benefice in the next parish.
items.exampleCN: 这位牧师获授邻教区的圣职俸禄。

items.meaning: doing harm; evil
items.meaningCN: 作恶的；有害的（male-“坏”+ -fic-“做”）
items.example: The story's maleficent queen curses the child.
items.exampleCN: 故事里的恶毒王后诅咒了这个孩子。

items.meaning: to make goods, originally by hand
items.meaningCN: 制造（原义“用手做”）
items.example: The company manufactures parts for wind turbines.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司制造风力涡轮机的零件。

items.meaning: a building where goods are made
items.meaningCN: 工厂（-ory 表示“做……的地方”）
items.example: The old factory is now a museum.
items.exampleCN: 那座旧工厂现在成了博物馆。

latinEntries.meaning: well, rightly, honorably
latinEntries.meaningCN: 好；正确地；体面地

latinEntries.meaning: to do, to make
latinEntries.meaningCN: 做；制造

latinEntries.meaning: a favor, service, kindness; also a granted office or benefice
latinEntries.meaningCN: 恩惠；服务；善意；也指授予的职位或圣职俸禄

latinEntries.meaning: generous, kind, obliging
latinEntries.meaningCN: 慷慨的；善良的；乐于助人的

definition_zh: 受益人；受惠者；（遗嘱、保险、信托等的）受益方
definition_en: a person or organization that receives money or an advantage under a will, policy, trust, or other arrangement
core_image: 一份文件的受益人栏上写着一个名字，箭头从文件指向这个人
scene: She named her sister as the sole beneficiary of her life insurance policy.
sceneCN: 这里 beneficiary 是「受益人」（第 2 个义项：保险金受益人）；句意：她指定妹妹作为她人寿保险的唯一受益人。场景要点：保单、受益人栏、签名、保险公司印章、信封。

pos.zh: 受益人；受惠者；（保险、遗嘱、信托的）受益方

senses.title: One named in a will
senses.titleCN: 遗嘱受益人：按遗嘱取得财产的人
senses.definition: a person named in a will to receive property or money from an estate
senses.definitionCN: 在遗嘱中被指定从遗产中获得财产或钱财的人
senses.example: Her three grandchildren were the beneficiaries of the estate.
senses.exampleCN: 她的三个孙辈是这笔遗产的受益人。
senses.why: beneficium is a favor or benefit, and -arius names the person connected with it; English -ary carries that personal sense. The first English use (1610s) was simply 'one who receives profits or advantages', and a will is the oldest concrete setting for that idea.
senses.whyCN: beneficium 是恩惠或好处，-arius 指与之相关的人，英语 -ary 承接了这个指人的含义。该词 1610 年代最早只是“获得利润或好处的人”，而遗嘱是这一观念最古老的落地场景。

senses.title: Insurance beneficiary
senses.titleCN: 保险金受益人：保单指定领钱的人
senses.definition: the person or party named in an insurance policy to receive its payout
senses.definitionCN: 在保险单中被指定领取保险金的人或方
senses.example: The policy pays the beneficiary directly, outside the estate.
senses.exampleCN: 保单直接向受益人赔付，不进入遗产程序。
senses.why: Insurance law lets a nomination do the work: the named person steps into the benefit at death. The general 'receiver of advantage' is narrowed to a named payee, which is why a beneficiary need not be an heir.
senses.whyCN: 保险法让“指定”本身发挥作用：被指定者在被保险人死亡时直接承接这笔利益。泛指的“好处接受者”在这里收窄为具名收款人，所以受益人未必是继承人。

senses.title: Trust beneficiary
senses.titleCN: 信托受益人：享有信托利益的人
senses.definition: a person entitled to income or capital from a trust, while a trustee holds the legal title
senses.definitionCN: 有权从信托中获得收益或本金、而由受托人持有法定所有权的人
senses.example: The trust's beneficiaries receive the income but do not control the capital.
senses.exampleCN: 信托受益人领取收益，但不控制本金。
senses.why: In a trust, legal title and enjoyment split: the trustee holds, the beneficiary enjoys. The word names the equitable side of that split, which is the same 'one who enjoys the benefit' idea in technical form.
senses.whyCN: 在信托中，法定所有权与享受权被拆开：受托人持有，受益人享有。这个词命名的正是这条裂缝中“享有”的那一侧，也就是“享有利益者”这一观念的技术形态。

senses.title: Charity or aid recipient
senses.titleCN: 慈善或援助的受助者
senses.definition: a person or household that receives help from a charity, welfare scheme, or aid programme
senses.definitionCN: 从慈善机构、福利计划或援助项目获得帮助的个人或家庭
senses.example: The programme asks each beneficiary to attend a training session.
senses.exampleCN: 该项目要求每位受助者参加一次培训。
senses.why: Aid language prefers beneficiary to 'poor person' because it frames the person as the rightful receiver of a benefit, not as an object of pity. The legal word supplies dignity as well as precision.
senses.whyCN: 援助话语更愿意用 beneficiary 而不是“穷人”，因为它把人框定为“有资格获得好处的人”，而不是被怜悯的对象。这个法律词同时提供了精确与尊严。

senses.title: Payment beneficiary in banking
senses.titleCN: 银行付款的收款人；信用证受益人
senses.definition: the party to whom a payment is to be made, especially under a transfer or letter of credit
senses.definitionCN: 应收款的一方，尤指汇款或信用证项下的收款人
senses.example: The bank released the funds once the beneficiary presented the shipping documents.
senses.exampleCN: 受益人一提交装运单据，银行就放款了。
senses.why: In banking the benefit is a payment, so the beneficiary is the party to whom money is owed or addressed. The word becomes a technical label printed on forms, and the 'benefit' is reduced to a sum of money.
senses.whyCN: 在银行业务中，好处就是一笔付款，所以 beneficiary 是应收款或被指定收款的一方。这个词成了印在单据上的技术标签，“好处”被压缩为一笔金额。

senses.title: Third-party beneficiary of a contract
senses.titleCN: 合同第三方受益人
senses.definition: a person outside a contract who is intended to receive its benefit and may enforce it
senses.definitionCN: 合同之外、被意图给予合同利益并可据此主张权利的人
senses.example: The subcontractor was a third-party beneficiary of the main contract.
senses.exampleCN: 分包商是主合同的第三方受益人。
senses.why: Contract law extends the will model: a person who never signed the agreement may still be its intended receiver. Beneficiary then means 'the one the promise was meant to benefit', not 'the one who made the promise'.
senses.whyCN: 合同法延伸了遗嘱模型：从未签过协议的人也可能是约定的受益对象。此时 beneficiary 指“承诺本想使之受益的人”，而不是“作出承诺的人”。

senses.title: Development beneficiary or country
senses.titleCN: 发展项目的受益群体；受援国
senses.definition: a community, household group, or country that receives development assistance
senses.definitionCN: 接受发展援助的社区、家庭群体或国家
senses.example: The report compared outcomes across five beneficiary countries.
senses.exampleCN: 报告比较了五个受援国的结果。
senses.why: When the receiver is a whole community or state, the noun becomes a policy category. The benefit is now development assistance rather than a private gift, so the word works at the scale of projects and governments.
senses.whyCN: 当接受方是整个社区或国家时，这个名词变成政策类别。此时的好处是发展援助而非私人赠与，于是这个词在项目与政府的尺度上运作。

senses.title: Anyone who gains from an event
senses.titleCN: 泛指受益者：从某事中得到好处的人
senses.definition: a person or group that profits from a change, event, or situation
senses.definitionCN: 从某种变化、事件或局势中获利的人或群体
senses.example: Small exporters were the main beneficiaries of the weaker currency.
senses.exampleCN: 小出口商是货币走弱的主要受益者。
senses.why: Once the legal senses are established, the word can be used loosely of anyone who profits from an event. The benefit need not come from a document at all; it can come from a policy, a storm, or a market move.
senses.whyCN: 法律义项确立之后，这个词可以宽松地指任何从事件中获利的人。好处完全不必来自文件，也可以来自政策、风暴或市场波动。

senses.title: Attributive: the receiving side
senses.titleCN: 受益方的：作定语指接受的一方
senses.definition: used before another noun to label the receiving side of a scheme or arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 置于另一名词前，标记某项计划或安排中接受的一方的
senses.example: Beneficiary families received the cash transfer at the start of each term.
senses.exampleCN: 受益家庭在每学期开始时收到现金补助。
senses.why: English often puts a noun before another noun instead of using an adjective, and beneficiary does this job in phrases such as beneficiary country and beneficiary family. It still names a person or party, but it now modifies rather than stands alone.
senses.whyCN: 英语常用名词而非形容词来修饰另一个名词，beneficiary 就在 beneficiary country、beneficiary family 这类短语里承担这个功能。它仍然指人或一方，但此时是修饰而非独立充当名词。

intro.en: Beneficiary and beneficial come from the same Latin noun beneficium, but they are not the same derivative. Beneficial goes through the adjective suffix -alis and names a quality; beneficiary goes through -arius and names a person. The noun reached English in the 1610s, probably through French.
intro.cn: beneficiary 和 beneficial 出自同一个拉丁名词 beneficium，但它们不是同一条派生。beneficial 走 -alis 这一形容词后缀，命名性质；beneficiary 走 -arius，命名人。这个名词在 17 世纪 10 年代进入英语，可能经由法语。

items.en: bene 'well' plus facere 'to do, make' produce beneficus 'generous, kind, obliging', literally 'doing well'. The pair is the common base of benefit, benefactor, beneficial and beneficiary.
items.cn: bene“好”加上 facere“做、造”产生 beneficus“慷慨的、善良的、乐于助人的”，字面即“做好事”。这一对成分是 benefit、benefactor、beneficial、beneficiary 的共同基础。

items.en: The noun beneficium 'a favor, service, kindness' adds -ium to the stem. It can mean a concrete benefit, a kindness done, and later a church office granted as a 'benefit' with its income.
items.cn: 名词 beneficium“恩惠、服务、善意”在词干上加 -ium。它可以指具体的好处、一次善举，后来也指作为“好处”授予的、带收入的教会圣职。

items.en: beneficiarius means 'enjoying a favor, privileged', built with -arius 'connected with, belonging to'. In Latin it describes a person attached to a benefit; the suffix is personal, not abstract.
items.cn: beneficiarius 意为“享有恩惠的、有特权的”，由 -arius“与……有关的、属于……的”构成。在拉丁语中它描述与好处相连的人；这个后缀是指人的，不是抽象性质的。

items.en: English beneficiary (1610s) probably came via French bénéficiaire, first as a noun 'one who receives profits or advantages', then in the 1620s as an adjective. The noun is now far more common than the adjective.
items.cn: 英语 beneficiary（17 世纪 10 年代）很可能经由法语 bénéficiaire 而来，先作名词“获得利润或好处的人”，17 世纪 20 年代再作形容词。如今名词用法远比形容词用法常见。

items.en: This is the key contrast with beneficial. beneficialis uses -alis to make 'pertaining to a benefit', a quality adjective. beneficiarius uses -arius to make 'the person who enjoys a benefit', a personal noun. Same base, different suffix, different word class.
items.cn: 这是它与 beneficial 的关键差别。beneficialis 用 -alis 构成“与好处有关的”性质形容词；beneficiarius 用 -arius 构成“享有好处的人”这一指人名词。同一词基，不同后缀，不同词性。

items.en: Modern English pushed the noun into law and finance: wills, life insurance, trusts, letters of credit, third-party contract rights. The old adjective use faded, and the attributive use in beneficiary country is a noun adjunct, not a revival of the adjective.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个名词推入法律与金融：遗嘱、人寿保险、信托、信用证、合同第三方权利。旧的形容词用法衰落了；beneficiary country 里的定语用法是名词作定语，并不是旧形容词的复活。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin base but differs in suffix and direction (giver or receiver); the second group contains words for receivers that differ in legal status and setting.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁词基，但后缀和方向不同（给予者还是接受者）；第二组都是“接受者”，但法律身份与场景不同。

entries.definition: Producing a good effect. It is an adjective, so it can never stand for the person who receives; -ial marks quality, not a person.
entries.definitionCN: 产生良好效果的。它是形容词，绝不能代替接受者本人；-ial 标记性质，不指人。

entries.definition: Kind and generous in character. It points at the person who does good, the opposite direction from beneficiary.
entries.definitionCN: 生性仁慈慷慨的。它指向行善的人，方向与 beneficiary 相反。

entries.definition: A church office with its income. It looks like beneficiary shortened, but it comes from the 'office granted' branch of beneficium.
entries.definitionCN: 带收入的教会圣职。它看起来像 beneficiary 的缩短形式，但来自 beneficium“授予的职位”这一分支。

entries.definition: A person who gives help or money. Benefactor gives; beneficiary receives; the -fact- of benefactor is the 'do' of facere.
entries.definitionCN: 提供帮助或金钱的人。benefactor 给，beneficiary 收；benefactor 里的 -fact- 就是 facere 的“做”。

entries.definition: Anyone who receives something. It is neutral and carries no legal entitlement, whereas beneficiary implies a recognized right to the benefit.
entries.definitionCN: 任何接受某物的人。它是中性的，不含法律权利；而 beneficiary 暗示对该利益有被承认的权利。

entries.definition: A person who inherits property by law or blood relationship, whether or not a will names them.
entries.definitionCN: 依法定或血缘继承财产的人，无论遗嘱是否点名。

entries.definition: A person who receives a legacy, usually money or movable property, under a will. Narrower than beneficiary, which also covers insurance and trusts.
entries.definitionCN: 依遗嘱接受遗赠（通常是钱或动产）的人。比 beneficiary 窄，后者还涵盖保险与信托。

entries.definition: The party to whom a payment is made, especially on a cheque or bill. It names only the receiving end of a payment.
entries.definitionCN: 收款的一方，尤指支票或票据上的收款人。它只命名付款的接收端。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real suffixes, real documents and real contrasts with the giver's word.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的后缀、真实的文书，以及和“给予者”一词的真实对比。

normal.en: -ary marks a person attached to something; in beneficiary that person is attached to a benefit, while -ial in beneficial marks a quality instead.
normal.cn: -ary 标记附着于某物的人；在 beneficiary 里此人与“好处”相连，而 beneficial 的 -ial 标记的是性质。

normal.en: Three documents always have a beneficiary line: a will, an insurance policy, and a trust deed.
normal.cn: 三种文书总有受益人栏：遗嘱、保单、信托契约。

normal.en: Direction test: benefactor gives, beneficiary receives. If the sentence is about giving, it is the wrong word.
normal.cn: 方向测试：benefactor 给，beneficiary 收。如果句子讲的是“给”，那就用错了词。

normal.en: Same stem as beneficial, different suffix: -ary makes a person, -ial makes a quality.
normal.cn: 与 beneficial 同词干、不同后缀：-ary 造人，-ial 造性质。

normal.en: In a letter of credit the form itself names the beneficiary, so banking gives the word a concrete place.
normal.cn: 在信用证里，表格本身就要填 beneficiary，银行业务给了这个词一个具体的位置。

abstract.en: Picture a document with an arrow leaving the page and landing on a person: the person at the arrow's end is the beneficiary.
abstract.cn: 想象一份文件，一支箭头离开纸面落在一个人身上：箭头末端的那个人就是 beneficiary。

abstract.en: Picture two chairs facing each other: the giver's chair is benefactor, the receiver's chair is beneficiary.
abstract.cn: 想象两把面对面的椅子：给予者的椅子是 benefactor，接受者的椅子是 beneficiary。

abstract.en: Picture a name written on a line: the line is the channel through which the benefit flows, and the name is the person at its end.
abstract.cn: 想象一条横线上写着一个名字：这条线是利益流动的通道，名字就是通道末端的人。

examples.en: She left the house to her nephew as the sole beneficiary of her will.
examples.cn: 她把房子留给侄子，作为她遗嘱的唯一受益人。

examples.en: The insurance company paid the beneficiary within thirty days.
examples.cn: 保险公司在三十天内向受益人支付了赔款。

examples.en: Rural households were the main beneficiaries of the electrification programme.
examples.cn: 农村家庭是电气化项目的主要受益者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 本（ben）来的好处（benefit）舍（she）给谁，谁就是 beneficiary 受益人

root: 拉丁 bene“好”+ facere“做” → beneficium“恩惠” → beneficiarius“受恩惠者、享有特权者”；-ary 表“与……有关的人”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses share one position: the person at the receiving end of a benefit. What changes is the document that assigns it — a will, a policy, a trust, a contract, a payment order — or, in the loosest sense, no document at all.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项共享同一个位置：处在利益接受端的那个人。变化的是分配利益的那份文书——遗嘱、保单、信托、合同、付款指令——或者在最宽松的义项里，根本没有文书。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a named person at the receiving end of a benefit written into a document.
core.cn: 核心意象：写在文书里的利益，末端是一个具名的接受者。

branches.en: PRIVATE AND CHARITABLE RECEIVERS: a will names an heir; a charity names the person it helps.
branches.cn: 私人与慈善接受者：遗嘱点名继承人；慈善机构点名它帮助的人。

branches.en: POLICY AND TRUST: the nomination or the trust deed assigns the benefit to a named party.
branches.cn: 保单与信托：指定或信托契据把利益分配给具名的一方。

branches.en: PAYMENT AND CONTRACT: banking and contract law make the beneficiary a technical party with a right to enforce.
branches.cn: 付款与合同：银行和合同法使 beneficiary 成为有主张权的技术性当事方。

branches.en: COLLECTIVE AND ATTRIBUTIVE: whole countries and households become the receiving side of a programme.
branches.cn: 集体与定语用法：整个国家与家庭成为项目的接受方。

branches.en: LOOSE EXTENSION: anyone who profits from an event, with no document at all.
branches.cn: 宽松延伸：任何从事件中获利的人，完全不需要文书。

intro.en: Beneficiary is bene- + -fic- + -ary, and each piece is still readable: 'well' + 'doing' + 'person connected with'. The -ary ending is the decisive one, because it turns a benefit into a person.
intro.cn: beneficiary 是 bene- + -fic- + -ary，每一块至今仍可读：“好”+“做”+“与之相连的人”。决定性的是 -ary，因为它把“好处”变成了“人”。

latinIntro.en: Latin bene and facere also produced beneficium, beneficus and beneficiarius. English keeps the -ary branch for people (beneficiary) and the -ial branch for qualities (beneficial), a split inherited from Latin suffix choice.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 bene 和 facere 还产生了 beneficium、beneficus、beneficiarius。英语把 -ary 那一支留给指人（beneficiary），把 -ial 那一支留给性质（beneficial），这一分裂承自拉丁语的后缀选择。

items.meaning: an advantage; to help or gain
items.meaningCN: 好处；利益；有益于；受益
items.example: The scholarship brought a real benefit to her family.
items.exampleCN: 这笔奖学金给她家带来了实实在在的好处。

items.meaning: producing a good effect
items.meaningCN: 有益的；有利的
items.example: The change was beneficial to the whole team.
items.exampleCN: 这一变化对整个团队都有益。

items.meaning: a person who receives a benefit
items.meaningCN: 受益人；受惠者
items.example: The beneficiary must show proof of identity.
items.exampleCN: 受益人必须出示身份证明。

items.meaning: one who gives help or money
items.meaningCN: 施惠者；捐助者
items.example: A benefactor funded the new laboratory.
items.exampleCN: 一位捐助者出资修建了新实验室。

items.meaning: generosity; the doing of good
items.meaningCN: 仁慈；善行
items.example: The clinic depends on the beneficence of donors.
items.exampleCN: 这家诊所依靠捐助者的善心维持。

items.meaning: kind and generous in action
items.meaningCN: 行善的；仁慈的
items.example: A beneficent stranger paid for the medicine.
items.exampleCN: 一位好心的陌生人付了药费。

items.meaning: a church office with its income
items.meaningCN: （教会）圣职及俸禄
items.example: The bishop granted him a benefice.
items.exampleCN: 主教授予他一处圣职俸禄。

items.meaning: the formal act of naming a beneficiary
items.meaningCN: 受益人指定（正式指定受益人的行为）
items.example: A beneficiary designation must be signed and dated.
items.exampleCN: 受益人指定必须签名并注明日期。

items.meaning: doing harm
items.meaningCN: 作恶的；有害的
items.example: The maleficent spell brought illness to the village.
items.exampleCN: 恶毒的咒语给村庄带来了疾病。

items.meaning: to make goods
items.meaningCN: 制造；生产
items.example: They manufacture medical devices in this plant.
items.exampleCN: 他们在这座工厂生产医疗器械。

latinEntries.meaning: well, rightly
latinEntries.meaningCN: 好；正确地

latinEntries.meaning: to do, to make
latinEntries.meaningCN: 做；制造

latinEntries.meaning: a favor, service, kindness; a granted office
latinEntries.meaningCN: 恩惠；服务；善意；授予的职位

latinEntries.meaning: enjoying a favor; privileged
latinEntries.meaningCN: 享有恩惠的；有特权的

definition_zh: 生物多样性；生物多样性水平
definition_en: the variety of living organisms and the ecological systems they form, measured at genetic, species, and ecosystem levels
core_image: 同一片森林里，每一层都长着不同的生命
scene: The island's isolation has produced remarkable biodiversity, with species found nowhere else on Earth.
sceneCN: 这里 biodiversity 是「生物多样性」（第 1 个义项：一个地区的物种多样性）；句意：这座岛屿的与世隔绝造就了非凡的生物多样性，有些物种在地球上别处都找不到。场景要点：海岛、多层的热带植被、不同种类的鸟与昆虫、记录表、望远镜。

pos.zh: 生物多样性；生物多样性水平

collocations.zh: 生物多样性补偿（生态补偿机制）

derivatives.zh: 生物多样性极高的（用于 megadiverse countries）

senses.title: Species diversity in a place
senses.titleCN: 物种多样性：一个地区有多少种生物
senses.definition: the variety and number of species living in a given area
senses.definitionCN: 某一地区内物种的多样程度和数量
senses.example: The island's isolation has produced remarkable biodiversity.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛屿的与世隔绝造就了非凡的生物多样性。
senses.why: bio- supplies 'life' and diversity supplies 'turned different ways'. The first sense counts how many kinds of living thing share a place: difference among organisms is the core of the word, and species are the easiest differences to see.
senses.whyCN: bio- 提供“生命”，diversity 提供“转向各方”。第一个义项数的是一个地方共享着多少种生物：生物之间的差异是这个词的核心，而物种是最容易看见的差异。

senses.title: Genetic diversity within a species
senses.titleCN: 遗传多样性：同一物种内部的基因差异
senses.definition: the variation in genes among individuals of the same species
senses.definitionCN: 同一物种个体之间的基因差异
senses.example: Small populations lose biodiversity at the genetic level even before species disappear.
senses.exampleCN: 小种群在物种消失之前，就已经在遗传层面失去生物多样性。
senses.why: The 1992 Convention on Biological Diversity defined the term at three levels, and the first extension went inward: variety does not stop between species, it continues among individuals and their genes. A species is itself a pool of differences.
senses.whyCN: 1992 年《生物多样性公约》把该词定义为三个层次，第一次延伸是向内走：多样性并不止于物种之间，它继续存在于个体及其基因之间。一个物种本身就是一池差异。

senses.title: Ecosystem and habitat diversity
senses.titleCN: 生态系统与生境多样性
senses.definition: the variety of ecosystems, habitats, and ecological communities in a region
senses.definitionCN: 一个地区内生态系统、生境与生态群落的多样程度
senses.example: Wetlands, forest and coral reef add ecosystem biodiversity to the same region.
senses.exampleCN: 湿地、森林与珊瑚礁为同一地区增加了生态系统多样性。
senses.why: The third level steps outward: not the organisms but the kinds of place and the communities they form. Difference now applies to habitats, so the same word covers a forest, a marsh and a reef.
senses.whyCN: 第三个层次向外走：不是生物本身，而是地方的类型以及它们形成的群落。差异这时适用于生境，于是同一个词覆盖森林、沼泽与珊瑚礁。

senses.title: The measured level: high or low
senses.titleCN: 多样性水平：可高可低的量
senses.definition: the measured degree of variety in a place, which can be high, low, or declining
senses.definitionCN: 一个地方多样性的可测程度，可高、可低或正在下降
senses.example: The survey recorded low biodiversity in the polluted stretch of the river.
senses.exampleCN: 调查记录到河流受污染河段的生物多样性很低。
senses.why: Once a quantity can be counted, it can be compared. Diversity stops being a bare fact and becomes a scale — high, low, rich, poor — which is what field surveys actually report.
senses.whyCN: 一旦可以计数，就可以比较。多样性不再是单纯的事实，而变成一把刻度——高、低、丰富、贫乏——这正是野外调查实际报告的内容。

senses.title: Loss of biodiversity
senses.titleCN: 生物多样性丧失
senses.definition: the decline or disappearance of biological variety, usually through human pressure
senses.definitionCN: 生物多样性程度的下降或消失，通常由人类压力造成
senses.example: Habitat clearance is the leading cause of biodiversity loss worldwide.
senses.exampleCN: 栖息地清除是世界范围内生物多样性丧失的首要原因。
senses.why: A scale that can fall invites the noun 'loss'. The word now names a public problem, not only a property of a place; conservation supplies the negative frame, and loss becomes the standard collocation.
senses.whyCN: 一个会下跌的刻度自然引出“丧失”这个名词。这个词现在命名的是一种公共问题，而不只是某地的属性；保护话语提供了负面框架，loss 于是成为标准搭配。

senses.title: Conservation hotspot
senses.titleCN: 保护热点：多样性极高又受威胁的地区
senses.definition: a region with exceptionally high biodiversity that is under serious threat
senses.definitionCN: 生物多样性异常高、同时面临严重威胁的地区
senses.example: The mountain range is recognised as a global biodiversity hotspot.
senses.exampleCN: 这条山脉被认定为全球生物多样性热点地区。
senses.why: Where diversity is high and threatened, attention concentrates. Hotspot is the spatial form of that concentration: a place worth naming, mapping and funding, so the word becomes an argument for protection.
senses.whyCN: 在多样性高又受威胁的地方，注意力会集中。hotspot 就是这种集中的空间形态：一个值得命名、绘图和投入资金的地方，于是这个词本身成了一种保护理由。

senses.title: Agricultural biodiversity
senses.titleCN: 农业生物多样性：作物与家畜品种的多样
senses.definition: the variety of crops, livestock breeds, and associated organisms used in farming
senses.definitionCN: 农业中使用的作物、家畜品种及相关生物的多样性
senses.example: Traditional farms preserve agricultural biodiversity that monocultures lose.
senses.exampleCN: 传统农场保存着单一种植所丧失的农业生物多样性。
senses.why: Humans select plants and animals, so variety also exists among breeds and crop varieties. The compound widens 'life' from wild organisms to cultivated ones, and the word becomes a measure of food-system resilience.
senses.whyCN: 人类对动植物进行选择，所以品种与作物之间也存在多样性。这个复合词把“生命”从野生生物扩展到栽培生物，于是该词成为衡量食物系统韧性的一项指标。

senses.title: Biodiversity as a global commons
senses.titleCN: 作为全球公共资源的生物多样性
senses.definition: biodiversity treated as a shared resource and a subject of international law and policy
senses.definitionCN: 被当作共享资源、并成为国际法与政策对象的生物多样性
senses.example: The treaty treats biodiversity as a common concern of humankind.
senses.exampleCN: 该条约把生物多样性视为人类的共同关切。
senses.why: Because genes, species and habitats cross borders, the noun was lifted from ecology into international law. The 1992 Convention made it the name of a shared resource, and the word acquired a political subject as well as an ecological one.
senses.whyCN: 由于基因、物种与生境都跨越国界，这个名词从生态学被提升到国际法。1992 年公约使它成为一种共享资源的名称，这个词于是既有生态学主体，也有政治主体。

senses.title: Diversity in managed or urban land
senses.titleCN: 城市与人工生境中的生物多样性
senses.definition: biological variety measured in cities, restored land, and other human-managed landscapes
senses.definitionCN: 在城市、修复地及其他人类管理景观中测得的生物多样性
senses.example: Green roofs and city parks can raise urban biodiversity.
senses.exampleCN: 绿色屋顶与城市公园可以提升城市生物多样性。
senses.why: The last extension drops the wilderness assumption: diversity is measured wherever life persists, including cities and restored land. The word becomes a planning target rather than a description of untouched nature.
senses.whyCN: 最后一次延伸丢掉了“荒野”预设：凡有生命存续之处都可测多样性，包括城市与修复地。这个词于是从“未受触及的自然之描述”变成一项规划目标。

intro.en: Biodiversity is not an inherited word. It is a 20th-century scientific compound, clipped from the phrase biological diversity: bio- is Greek, diversity is Latin, and the two were joined in modern English. The earliest written record is disputed.
intro.cn: biodiversity 不是承袭来的词，而是 20 世纪的科学复合词，由短语 biological diversity 截短而成：bio- 是希腊语，diversity 是拉丁语，两者在现代英语里被拼在一起。最早的书面记录存疑。

items.en: bios means 'one's life, course or way of living, lifetime', as opposed to zoē 'animal life'. It comes from PIE *gwei- 'to live'. In English bio- has been used in scientific compounds since about 1800 for 'organic life', though biography keeps the older 'life-story' sense.
items.cn: bios 意为“一个人的生命、生活历程、寿命”，与 zoē“动物生命”相对，来自原始印欧语 *gwei-“活”。英语自约 1800 年起用 bio- 构成科学复合词，表示“有机生命”，但 biography 仍保留更古老的“生平故事”义。

items.en: divertere 'to turn apart' is dis- 'apart' + vertere 'to turn'. Its past participle diversus means 'turned different ways', and diversitas gives 'difference, variety'. English diversity (mid-14c) came through Old French diversete.
items.cn: divertere“转开”是 dis-“分开”+ vertere“转”。其过去分词 diversus 意为“转向各方的”，名词 diversitas 表示“差异、多样”。英语 diversity（14 世纪中）经由古法语 diversete 而来。

items.en: The full phrase was used in ecology and conservation from the 1970s–80s for variety at genetic, species and ecosystem levels. It is a descriptive phrase built from existing words, not a classical term with an ancient pedigree.
items.cn: 完整短语 biological diversity 在 20 世纪 70—80 年代的生态学与保护生物学中用来指基因、物种、生态系统三个层次的多样性。它是由现有词构成的描述性短语，不是有古老传承的经典术语。

items.en: Etymonline dates biodiversity 'by 1988'. The clipped form is often credited to W. G. Rosen in conference material around 1985–86, later printed in 1988; the exact first written use and the first coiner are disputed, and sources differ. Treat the date as approximate.
items.cn: Etymonline 把 biodiversity 记作“by 1988”。这个截短形式常被归到 W. G. Rosen 在 1985—86 年前后的会议材料，后来于 1988 年付印；最早的书面使用与首创者都有争议，各家资料不一。年代只能作大致估计。

items.era: WHY IT IS NOT AN OLD WORD
items.en: There is no Latin biodiversitas and no Greek compound of this shape. The word was built from a living prefix and a living noun to fill a gap in ecology, so its structure stays transparent in a way inherited words are not.
items.cn: 并不存在拉丁语 biodiversitas，也没有这种形状的希腊语复合词。这个词是用活的前缀加活的名词造出来填补生态学的空缺，因此它的结构保持着承袭词所没有的透明性。

items.en: The 1992 Convention on Biological Diversity fixed the three-level definition and turned the word into a legal and policy term. Later compounds — hotspot, offset, agrobiodiversity — extend it outward from ecology into planning, finance and agriculture.
items.cn: 1992 年《生物多样性公约》确定了三层定义，把这个词变成法律与政策术语。后来的复合词——hotspot、offset、agrobiodiversity——又把它从生态学向外扩展到规划、金融与农业。

note.en: The first group contains the words and phrases most often mistaken for biodiversity itself; the second contains measures of living variety that differ in what they actually count.
note.cn: 第一组是最容易被误当成 biodiversity 本身的词与短语；第二组是衡量生命多样性的指标，但各自实际计数的对象不同。

entries.definition: Variety or difference in general. It can describe people, ideas, or tastes; only the bio- prefix makes it about living organisms.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指多样或差异，可指人、想法、口味；只有加上 bio- 才专指生物。

entries.definition: The longer, formal phrase from which biodiversity was clipped. It is the safer term in legal and scientific writing and covers the same three levels.
entries.definitionCN: biodiversity 由之截短而来的较长正式短语。在法律与科学写作中更稳妥，涵盖同样的三个层次。

entries.definition: The total mass of living matter. It shares bio- but measures amount, while biodiversity measures difference.
entries.definitionCN: 活物质的总质量。它共享 bio-，但衡量的是数量，而 biodiversity 衡量的是差异。

entries.definition: A written life of a person, from bio- + graphein 'to write'. It looks like a bio- word but has nothing to do with ecology.
entries.definitionCN: 人物传记，来自 bio- + graphein“书写”。它看起来像 bio- 词，却与生态学无关。

entries.definition: The quality of differing in form or type. Everyday and unmeasured, with no ecological definition behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 形式或类型上存在差异的性质。日常用语，不可量化，背后没有生态学定义。

entries.definition: The number of species in a place. It counts only species, whereas biodiversity also includes genetic and ecosystem variety.
entries.definitionCN: 一个地方的物种数目。它只数物种，而 biodiversity 还包括遗传与生态系统层面的多样。

entries.definition: The number of individuals of a species. More individuals is not more diversity; a field of one crop can have high abundance and low biodiversity.
entries.definitionCN: 某一物种的个体数量。个体多并不等于多样性高；一块单一种植的田可以个体数量很高而生物多样性很低。

entries.definition: Unevenness in composition or structure across space. It is a measurement of pattern, not the variety of life itself.
entries.definitionCN: 组成或结构在空间上的不均匀。它是格局的度量，而不是生命本身的多样。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek prefix, the real Latin noun, and the real three-level definition.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊前缀、真实的拉丁名词，以及真实的三层定义。

normal.en: bio- 'life' + diversity 'turned apart': life turned into many different forms.
normal.cn: bio-“生命”+ diversity“转向各方”：生命被分成许多不同的形态。

normal.en: Three levels: genes → species → ecosystems. The word covers all three, and most exam questions test only the first.
normal.cn: 三个层次：基因 → 物种 → 生态系统。这个词覆盖三层，而多数考题只考第一层。

normal.en: Contrast pair: biomass measures amount, biodiversity measures variety. The second half of each word tells you what is measured.
normal.cn: 对比记忆：biomass 量的是数量，biodiversity 量的是多样。两个词的后半部分告诉你衡量的对象。

normal.en: bio- means 'life story' in biography and 'life science' in biology; biodiversity belongs to the science side.
normal.cn: bio- 在 biography 里是“生平故事”，在 biology 里是“生命科学”；biodiversity 属于科学这一侧。

normal.en: The word usually travels with loss, hotspot and conservation, because it names something that can be measured, threatened and protected.
normal.cn: 这个词常与 loss、hotspot、conservation 同行，因为它命名的东西可以被测量、被威胁、被保护。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf with many different books; abundance would be many copies of one book, diversity is many different titles.
abstract.cn: 想象一个书架摆着许多不同的书；abundance 是同一本书有很多本，diversity 是有很多不同的书名。

abstract.en: Picture a forest where canopy, understory and soil each hold a different community of life.
abstract.cn: 想象一片森林，树冠层、林下层与土壤各自住着不同的生命群落。

abstract.en: Picture three nested circles: genes inside species, species inside ecosystems. Biodiversity is the whole set of circles, not just the middle one.
abstract.cn: 想象三个同心圆：基因在物种之内，物种在生态系统之内。biodiversity 是整套圆，而不只是中间那一圈。

examples.en: The rainforest supports biodiversity that no plantation can replace.
examples.cn: 雨林所支撑的生物多样性是任何单一林场都无法替代的。

examples.en: Scientists measure biodiversity at the genetic, species and ecosystem levels.
examples.cn: 科学家在遗传、物种和生态系统三个层次上测量生物多样性。

examples.en: The report links biodiversity loss to the draining of local wetlands.
examples.cn: 报告把生物多样性丧失与当地湿地被排干联系起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拜（bio）生命所赐，大（dai）家各有伟（ver）色，提（ti）供多样 → biodiversity 生物多样性

root: 希腊 bios“生命”+ 拉丁 diversus“转向各方”构成的 diversity“多样性”；20 世纪仿 biological diversity 截短而成的新造复合词。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses share one core: difference among living things. The word then widens inward to genes, outward to ecosystems, sideways to measurement and loss, and finally into law and city planning.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项共享同一个核心：生物之间的差异。这个词随后向内扩展到基因，向外扩展到生态系统，再横向扩展到测量与丧失，最后进入法律与城市规划。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: life turned into many different forms in one place.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一片土地上的生命分成许多不同的形态。

branches.en: LEVELS OF VARIETY: species differ from one another, and individuals differ genetically inside a species.
branches.cn: 多样的层次：物种之间彼此不同，个体在同一物种内部也有基因差异。

branches.en: PLACES AND CULTIVATION: habitats differ from one another, and farming adds human-selected varieties.
branches.cn: 生境与栽培：生境彼此不同，农业又加入人类选育的品种。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT AND DECLINE: variety becomes a scale with high and low values, and a falling scale becomes loss.
branches.cn: 测量与下降：多样性变成有高低值的刻度，而刻度下跌就成了丧失。

branches.en: PROTECTION AND LAW: threatened richness concentrates attention, and cross-border variety becomes a global commons.
branches.cn: 保护与法律：受威胁的丰富度集中注意力，跨国界的多样性成为全球公共资源。

branches.en: BEYOND WILDNESS: managed and urban land also count, so the word becomes a planning target.
branches.cn: 超越荒野：人工管理与城市土地也计入，于是这个词成为规划目标。

intro.en: Biodiversity is a transparent modern compound: bio- + diversity. Both parts are free-standing or semi-free in English, which is why the word feels self-explaining even to a reader who knows no Latin or Greek.
intro.cn: biodiversity 是一个透明的现代复合词：bio- + diversity。两部分在英语中都能独立或半独立使用，所以即使不懂拉丁语或希腊语，读者也觉得它自我解释。

latinIntro.en: There is no single Latin word behind biodiversity. The prefix is Greek bios; the noun is Latin diversitas, from diversus, past participle of divertere. The compound itself is modern, so its 'etymology' is a join, not an inheritance.
latinIntro.cn: biodiversity 背后没有单个拉丁词。前缀是希腊语 bios；名词是拉丁语 diversitas，出自 divertere 的过去分词 diversus。复合词本身是现代造物，所以它的“词源”是一次拼接，而不是承袭。

items.meaning: the science of life and living things
items.meaningCN: 生物学（bio-“生命”+ -logy“学科”）
items.example: She studied biology before turning to ecology.
items.exampleCN: 她在转向生态学之前学的是生物学。

items.meaning: the variety of life at several levels
items.meaningCN: 生物多样性（bio-“生命”+ diversity“多样”）
items.example: The survey mapped biodiversity across the valley.
items.exampleCN: 这项调查绘制了山谷各处的生物多样性。

items.meaning: having a high variety of living things
items.meaningCN: 生物多样的；生物种类丰富的
items.example: The delta is one of the most biodiverse regions in Asia.
items.exampleCN: 这片三角洲是亚洲生物多样性最丰富的地区之一。

items.meaning: the diversity of crops and livestock
items.meaningCN: 农业生物多样性（agro-“农田”+ biodiversity）
items.example: Seed banks protect agrobiodiversity.
items.exampleCN: 种子库保护农业生物多样性。

items.meaning: a place of intense activity or concentration
items.meaningCN: 热点（活动或集中程度极高的地点）
items.example: The region is a biodiversity hotspot.
items.exampleCN: 该地区是一个生物多样性热点。

items.meaning: the zone of life on Earth
items.meaningCN: 生物圈（bio-“生命”+ sphere“球体”）
items.example: Carbon moves through the biosphere.
items.exampleCN: 碳在生物圈中循环。

items.meaning: a large ecological community shaped by climate
items.meaningCN: 生物群系（bio-“生命”+ -ome“群体”）
items.example: Tundra is a cold biome.
items.exampleCN: 苔原是寒冷的生物群系。

items.meaning: the state of differing; variety
items.meaningCN: 多样性；差异（-ity 构成状态名词）
items.example: The region is known for its cultural diversity.
items.exampleCN: 该地区以文化多样性著称。

items.meaning: to make or become more varied
items.meaningCN: 使多样化；分散（-ify 表示“使……化”）
items.example: Farmers diversified their crops.
items.exampleCN: 农民使作物多样化。

items.meaning: compensation for damage to habitats, usually by restoring or protecting an equivalent area
items.meaningCN: 生物多样性补偿：通过修复或保护等面积生境来弥补损害
items.example: The company funded a biodiversity offset near the mine.
items.exampleCN: 公司出资在矿区附近实施生物多样性补偿。

latinEntries.meaning: life, lifetime, way of life
latinEntries.meaningCN: 生命；寿命；生活方式

latinEntries.meaning: to turn away, turn apart
latinEntries.meaningCN: 转开；转向别处

latinEntries.meaning: turned different ways; various
latinEntries.meaningCN: 转向各方的；各种各样的

definition_zh: 生物学家；研究生命现象的科学工作者
definition_en: a scientist who studies living organisms and the processes of life
core_image: 一个人俯身在显微镜与野外记录本之间，把活的东西写进知识
scene: A biologist took water samples from the lake every week for a year.
sceneCN: 这里 biologist 是「生物学家」（第 1 个义项：研究生命现象的科学工作者）；句意：一位生物学家在一年里每周都从湖里取水样。场景要点：湖泊、采样瓶、显微镜、记录本、防水靴。

pos.zh: 生物学家；生物学研究者

derivatives.zh: 生物学者（1865 年出现的旧式竞争说法，今罕用）

senses.title: A scientist of living things
senses.titleCN: 生物学家：研究生命现象的人
senses.definition: a scientist who studies living organisms and life processes
senses.definitionCN: 研究生物与生命过程的科学家
senses.example: A biologist took water samples from the lake every week.
senses.exampleCN: 一位生物学家每周从湖里取水样。
senses.why: bio- is 'life', -logy is 'study', and -ist is 'one who practises'. The suffix makes a person out of a discipline: the biologist is the human face of biology, and the object of study is anything alive.
senses.whyCN: bio- 是“生命”，-logy 是“学科”，-ist 是“从事者”。这个后缀把一门学科变成一个人：生物学家就是生物学的面孔，而研究对象是一切活的东西。

senses.title: The laboratory researcher
senses.titleCN: 实验室生物学家：在台前做实验的人
senses.definition: a biologist who works mainly in a laboratory, using experiments and instruments
senses.definitionCN: 主要在实验室工作、使用实验与仪器的生物学家
senses.example: The biologist spent the morning at the microscope, counting cells.
senses.exampleCN: 这位生物学家在显微镜前度过了一上午，数细胞。
senses.why: Modern biology is largely experimental, so the default picture of a biologist became a person at a bench. The word names the profession rather than the place, but bench work supplies its most familiar scene.
senses.whyCN: 现代生物学很大程度上是实验性的，所以生物学家的默认形象变成了实验台前的人。这个词命名的是职业而不是地点，但实验台提供了它最熟悉的场景。

senses.title: The field biologist
senses.titleCN: 野外生物学家：在自然中观察的人
senses.definition: a biologist who studies organisms in their natural habitats rather than in a lab
senses.definitionCN: 在自然栖息地而非实验室研究生物的科学家
senses.example: Field biologists camped in the valley to record bird calls at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 野外生物学家在山谷里扎营，记录黎明时的鸟鸣。
senses.why: The other half of the discipline works outdoors. The same title covers both because the object — living things — is the same; only the method and the setting change.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科的另一半在户外工作。同一个头衔覆盖两边，因为对象——活的东西——相同，变化的只是方法与场景。

senses.title: A branch specialist
senses.titleCN: 分支生物学家：海洋、分子、细胞等
senses.definition: a biologist identified by the branch of biology they specialize in
senses.definitionCN: 以所专攻的生物学分支来称呼的生物学家
senses.example: A marine biologist explained why the reef was bleaching.
senses.exampleCN: 一位海洋生物学家解释了珊瑚礁为何白化。
senses.why: Biology split into branches, and English simply puts the branch before biologist: marine biologist, molecular biologist. The head noun still marks the person, while the first word narrows the field.
senses.whyCN: 生物学分成许多分支，英语直接把分支放在 biologist 前面：marine biologist、molecular biologist。中心名词仍标记“人”，前面的词则缩小领域。

senses.title: The -ist pattern: practitioner of a discipline
senses.titleCN: -ist 构词：某学科的从业者
senses.definition: the general pattern by which -ist turns the name of a discipline into the name of the person who practises it
senses.definitionCN: -ist 把学科名称变成从业者名称的一般构词模式
senses.example: Botanists, zoologists and biologists all belong to the same -ist family.
senses.exampleCN: 植物学家、动物学家和生物学家都属于同一个 -ist 词族。
senses.why: -ist comes from Greek -istēs, an agent ending. Attaching it to -logy produces 'one who does the study'. The word therefore says what the person practises, not what they are like.
senses.whyCN: -ist 来自希腊语 -istēs，是施事词尾。把它加到 -logy 上就产生“从事这项研究的人”。所以这个词说的是“做什么”，而不是“是什么样的人”。

senses.title: The older sense: a student of life
senses.titleCN: 早期义：研究生命之学的人（1813）
senses.definition: the original English sense: a student of the science of life, with human life especially in view
senses.definitionCN: 英语最早的含义：研究生命之学的人，尤其着眼于人的生命
senses.example: The word biologist was first used in 1813 for a student of the science of life.
senses.exampleCN: biologist 一词在 1813 年最早用来指研究生命之学的人。
senses.why: The earliest English use (1813) still carried the Greek sense of bios as a person's life; the modern professional sense is recorded only by 1859. The word began as 'learner' and later became 'profession'.
senses.whyCN: 英语最早的使用（1813）仍带着希腊语 bios“一个人的生命”这层意思；现代职业义直到 1859 年才有记录。这个词从“学习者”开始，后来才成为“职业”。

senses.title: Conservation and applied biologist
senses.titleCN: 保护与应用生物学家：为管理生命而研究
senses.definition: a biologist whose work is directed at protecting or managing species and habitats
senses.definitionCN: 工作指向保护或管理物种与栖息地的生物学家
senses.example: Conservation biologists argue that protecting habitat protects species.
senses.exampleCN: 保护生物学家主张，保护栖息地就是保护物种。
senses.why: When biology is applied to managing species, the title gains a purpose: the biologist is not only describing life but defending it. The compound marks that applied role rather than a new kind of science.
senses.whyCN: 当生物学被用于管理物种时，这个头衔多了一层目的：生物学家不仅在描述生命，也在为生命辩护。这个复合词标记的是应用角色，而不是一门新科学。

senses.title: Biologists as a community
senses.titleCN: 生物学界：作为群体的生物学家
senses.definition: the profession or community of biologists, treated as a body of shared opinion
senses.definitionCN: 作为一个共享观点的群体的生物学家职业共同体
senses.example: Biologists generally agree that the warming ocean is shifting fish stocks.
senses.exampleCN: 生物学家普遍认为，海洋变暖正在改变鱼类种群分布。
senses.why: The plural without an article names a profession as a body of opinion. This is the collective sense: not one researcher but the discipline speaking, which is why news reports say 'biologists say'.
senses.whyCN: 不带冠词的复数把一种职业命名为一个观点共同体。这是集体义：说话的不是某位研究者，而是整个学科，所以新闻报道会说 biologists say。

senses.title: Attributive: a biologist's view
senses.titleCN: 生物学家的（视角/身份）
senses.definition: used before another noun or after 'as' to name the professional lens through which something is seen
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前或 as 之后，指看待某事物时所采用的生物学家视角
senses.example: As a biologist, she sees the garden as a web of interactions.
senses.exampleCN: 作为生物学家，她把花园看成一个相互作用的网络。
senses.why: Before another noun or after 'as', the word labels the lens through which something is seen. It is still a person, but the person now functions as a viewpoint rather than as the subject of the sentence.
senses.whyCN: 置于名词前或 as 之后时，这个词标记的是观察事物所用的镜头。它仍然指人，但此时的人作为“视角”起作用，而不是句子的主体。

intro.en: Biologist is biology + -ist. Biology itself is a modern Greek-Latin hybrid coined around 1800, so the whole family is scientific rather than inherited. The exact first coiner of biology is disputed; the date of biologist is better recorded.
intro.cn: biologist 是 biology + -ist。biology 本身是约 1800 年前后造出的希腊—拉丁混合词，所以整个词族是科学造词而非承袭词。biology 的确切首创者存疑，biologist 的年代记录则较清楚。

items.en: bios means 'life, lifetime, way of life' (PIE *gwei- 'to live'), as opposed to zoē 'animal life'. In modern scientific compounds bio- means 'life, living organisms'.
items.cn: bios 意为“生命、寿命、生活方式”（原始印欧语 *gwei-“活”），与 zoē“动物生命”相对。在现代科学复合词里，bio- 表示“生命、生物”。

items.en: logos means 'word, account, reason'. The derived -logia means 'the study of', and English -logy comes through Latin -logia. Biology is therefore 'the account or study of life'.
items.cn: logos 意为“词、叙述、理性”。派生的 -logia 表示“对……的研究”，英语 -logy 经由拉丁语 -logia 而来。因此 biology 就是“关于生命的论述或研究”。

items.en: The compound biology was suggested in 1802 by the German naturalist Gottfried Reinhold Treviranus and introduced in French that same year by Lamarck; the two seem to have hit on it independently. Who first coined it cannot be settled. English biology is recorded in 1819.
items.cn: 复合词 biology 由德国博物学家 Gottfried Reinhold Treviranus 于 1802 年提出，同年由拉马克在法语中引入；两人似乎是独立想到的。谁最先造出这个词无法确定。英语 biology 记录于 1819 年。

items.en: biologist is recorded from 1813, meaning 'a student of the science of life'. The earliest use refers to human life, in the Greek sense of bios; the modern sense 'one skilled in or a student of biology' is recorded by 1859.
items.cn: biologist 自 1813 年有记录，意为“研究生命之学的人”。最早用法指人的生命，取希腊语 bios 之义；现代义“精通或研究生物学的人”到 1859 年才有记录。

items.en: -ist 'one who does or makes' comes from French -iste and Latin -ista, from Greek -istēs, an agent ending built on verb stems. It makes biologist the person who practises what biology names.
items.cn: -ist“从事者”来自法语 -iste、拉丁语 -ista，再往上为希腊语 -istēs——建立在动词词干上的施事前缀。它使 biologist 成为“实践 biology 所示之事的人”。

items.en: Biography is bio- + graphein 'to write', literally 'life-writing', and its person is a biographer. Biology is bio- + -logy 'study', and its person is a biologist. The shared bio- is real, but the second element decides the word: writing versus studying.
items.cn: biography 是 bio- + graphein“书写”，字面“写生命”，其指人名词是 biographer。biology 是 bio- + -logy“研究”，其指人名词是 biologist。共享的 bio- 是真实的，但第二成分决定词义：书写还是研究。

note.en: The first group contains forms built on the same bio- prefix that are easily mistaken for the person; the second contains nearby professions that differ in scope or object.
note.cn: 第一组是同一 bio- 前缀构成、容易被误当成“指人”的形式；第二组是范围或对象不同的邻近职业。

entries.definition: The science of life. It ends in -logy 'study', so it names the field; biologist adds -ist to name the practitioner.
entries.definitionCN: 生命科学。它以 -logy“研究”结尾，命名的是领域；biologist 加 -ist 才命名从业者。

entries.definition: An account of a person's life, from bio- + graphein 'to write'. Its person is a biographer, never a biologist.
entries.definitionCN: 对一个人生平的记述，来自 bio- + graphein“书写”。其指人名词是 biographer，绝不是 biologist。

entries.definition: A rare 19th-century rival for biologist, recorded 1865 and now obsolete. It shows that -ist won the competition.
entries.definitionCN: 19 世纪与 biologist 竞争的罕见说法，1865 年有记录，今已废弃。它说明 -ist 赢下了这场竞争。

entries.definition: Relating to life or living things, from Greek biōtikos. It is an adjective, so it can never name the scientist.
entries.definitionCN: 与生命或生物有关的，来自希腊语 biōtikos。它是形容词，绝不能指科学家。

entries.definition: A researcher in any life science, including biomedicine and biochemistry. Broader than biologist, which usually points to organism-level study.
entries.definitionCN: 任何生命科学领域的研究者，包括生物医学与生物化学。比 biologist 宽，后者通常指生物体层面的研究。

entries.definition: A student of plants and animals through observation, often outside a university. It stresses watching nature rather than running experiments.
entries.definitionCN: 通过观察研究动植物的学者，常在大学之外。它强调观察自然，而不是做实验。

entries.definition: A specialist in animals. It is one branch of biology, so every zoologist is a biologist but not every biologist is a zoologist.
entries.definitionCN: 研究动物的专家。它是生物学的一个分支，所以动物学家都是生物学家，但生物学家不都是动物学家。

entries.definition: A scientist who studies the relations between organisms and their environment. The focus is the system, not the individual organism.
entries.definitionCN: 研究生物与环境之间关系的科学家。焦点在系统，而不在单个生物体。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real branch names, and the real biography contrast.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的分支名称，以及 biography 的真实对比。

normal.en: bio- 'life' + -logy 'study' + -ist 'practitioner': the person who does the study of life.
normal.cn: bio-“生命”+ -logy“研究”+ -ist“从业者”：从事生命研究的人。

normal.en: Test the ending: -logy is the field, -logist is the person. biology → biologist, geology → geologist.
normal.cn: 看词尾：-logy 是领域，-logist 是人。biology → biologist，geology → geologist。

normal.en: Branch names go before the person: marine, molecular, cell, evolutionary, conservation + biologist.
normal.cn: 分支名放在“人”前面：marine、molecular、cell、evolutionary、conservation + biologist。

normal.en: biography ends in -graphy 'writing', so its person is biographer. Never mix the two second elements.
normal.cn: biography 以 -graphy“书写”结尾，其指人名词是 biographer。不要把两个第二成分混在一起。

normal.en: The word began in 1813 as 'student of life' and only later meant a paid professional; that history explains why it sounds academic.
normal.cn: 这个词 1813 年起初是“研究生命的学生”，后来才指拿薪水的专业人士；这段历史解释了它为何带学术气。

abstract.en: Picture a person standing between a microscope and a muddy boot: lab and field are the two halves of one biologist.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人站在显微镜和沾泥的靴子之间：实验室与野外是同一个生物学家的两半。

abstract.en: Picture a tree of disciplines: biology is the trunk, and marine, cell, evolutionary biologists are branches bearing the same -ist label.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵学科树：biology 是树干，marine、cell、evolutionary 各支都挂着同一个 -ist 标签。

abstract.en: Picture the suffix as a badge: -ist is pinned on whoever practises the field, so the badge, not the field, makes the person.
abstract.cn: 把后缀想成一枚徽章：谁从事这门领域，-ist 就别在谁身上；造出“人”的是徽章，而不是领域。

examples.en: Biologists still disagree about how many species live in the deep ocean.
examples.cn: 生物学家对深海中有多少物种仍存在分歧。

examples.en: The marine biologist spent three months surveying the coral reef.
examples.cn: 这位海洋生物学家花了三个月调查珊瑚礁。

examples.en: As a biologist, she reads the forest as a set of relationships rather than a collection of trees.
examples.cn: 作为生物学家，她把森林读成一组关系，而不是一堆树。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拜（bio）生命，欧（o）罗（lo）辑（gi）知识，斯特（st）专门研究 → biologist 生物学家

root: 希腊 bios“生命”+ -logia“研究”构成的 biology（约 1802 年新造）+ -ist“从业者”；字面即“研究生命之学的人”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses share one person: someone who studies life. What changes is where they work, which branch they name, whether the word means learner or professional, and whether it speaks for one researcher or the whole discipline.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项共享同一个人：研究生命的人。变化的是工作地点、所属分支、词义是“学习者”还是“职业”，以及说话的是某位研究者还是整个学科。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person who turns living things into knowledge.
core.cn: 核心意象：把活的东西变成知识的人。

branches.en: THE MAKING OF THE WORD: life + study + agent suffix, which is the general -ist pattern.
branches.cn: 词的构成：生命 + 研究 + 施事后缀，也就是 -ist 的一般模式。

branches.en: TWO WORKPLACES: the bench and the field are the two halves of the same profession.
branches.cn: 两个工作场所：实验台与野外是同一职业的两半。

branches.en: SPECIALITY AND PURPOSE: branch names narrow the field, and applied names add a goal.
branches.cn: 分支与目的：分支名缩小领域，应用名增加目标。

branches.en: HISTORICAL LAYER: the earliest sense was 'student of life', not paid professional.
branches.cn: 历史层：最早的义项是“研究生命的学生”，而不是拿薪水的专业人士。

branches.en: COLLECTIVE AND LENS: the plural can speak for a discipline, and 'as a biologist' names a viewpoint.
branches.cn: 集体与视角：复数可以代表整个学科，as a biologist 则命名一种视角。

intro.en: Biologist is built from three live pieces: bio- (life), -logy (study), -ist (practitioner). Unlike an inherited Latin word, every joint is still visible to a modern reader.
intro.cn: biologist 由三个仍然能产的部分构成：bio-“生命”、-logy“研究”、-ist“从业者”。与承袭的拉丁词不同，每一处接缝对现代读者都仍然可见。

latinIntro.en: The elements come from Greek, not Latin: bios 'life', logos 'account, reason', and -istēs 'one who does'. They entered English through Latin and French forms (-logia, -ista), which is why the endings look Latin even though the roots are Greek.
latinIntro.cn: 这些成分来自希腊语而非拉丁语：bios“生命”、logos“叙述、理性”、-istēs“从事者”。它们经由拉丁语和法语形式（-logia、-ista）进入英语，所以词根虽是希腊语，词尾看起来却像拉丁语。

items.meaning: the science of life
items.meaningCN: 生物学
items.example: Biology was her favourite subject at school.
items.exampleCN: 生物学是她上学时最喜欢的科目。

items.meaning: a scientist who studies life
items.meaningCN: 生物学家
items.example: The biologist recorded the behaviour of the birds.
items.exampleCN: 这位生物学家记录了这些鸟的行为。

items.meaning: relating to biology or living things
items.meaningCN: 生物的；生物学的
items.example: The sample was sent for biological testing.
items.exampleCN: 样本被送去进行生物检测。

items.meaning: in biological terms
items.meaningCN: 从生物学角度；在生物层面
items.example: The two species are biologically distinct.
items.exampleCN: 这两个物种在生物学上是不同的。

items.meaning: the zone of life on Earth
items.meaningCN: 生物圈
items.example: Life is concentrated in the biosphere.
items.exampleCN: 生命集中在生物圈内。

items.meaning: a written account of a person's life
items.meaningCN: 传记（bio-“生命”+ -graphy“书写”，第二成分不同）
items.example: She wrote a biography of the chemist.
items.exampleCN: 她写了一部关于这位化学家的传记。

items.meaning: a person who writes lives
items.meaningCN: 传记作者（与 biologist 的指人后缀不同）
items.example: The biographer interviewed the family.
items.exampleCN: 传记作者采访了这家人。

items.meaning: a scientist who studies rocks and the earth
items.meaningCN: 地质学家（同 -logist 模式）
items.example: A geologist dated the rock layer.
items.exampleCN: 一位地质学家测定了岩层的年代。

items.meaning: a specialist in animals
items.meaningCN: 动物学家（生物学的一个分支）
items.example: The zoologist studied the migration route.
items.exampleCN: 这位动物学家研究了迁徙路线。

items.meaning: a specialist in plants
items.meaningCN: 植物学家（植物学分支）
items.example: The botanist identified the plant from its leaves.
items.exampleCN: 植物学家根据叶子辨认出这种植物。

latinEntries.meaning: life, lifetime, way of life
latinEntries.meaningCN: 生命；寿命；生活方式

latinEntries.meaning: word, account, reason
latinEntries.meaningCN: 词；叙述；理性

latinEntries.meaning: the study of, an account of
latinEntries.meaningCN: 对……的研究；关于……的论述

latinEntries.meaning: agent ending: one who does or practises
latinEntries.meaningCN: 施事后缀：从事、实践某事的人

definition_zh: 生物量；生物质；生物质燃料
definition_en: the total mass of living matter in a given area, or living material used as fuel
core_image: 一整个生态系统被放上秤，读数就是活物的总重量
scene: The researchers weighed every plant in the plot to estimate the biomass of the meadow.
sceneCN: 这里 biomass 是「生物量」（第 1 个义项：一个地区的活物质总质量）；句意：研究人员称量了样方里的每一株植物，以估算这片草甸的生物量。场景要点：样方框、电子秤、割下的草、记录板、烘干箱。

pos.zh: 生物量；（可作燃料的）生物质

senses.title: Total mass of living matter
senses.titleCN: 生物量：一个地区的活物质总量
senses.definition: the total mass of living organisms in a given area or volume
senses.definitionCN: 某一区域或体积内全部活物质的总质量
senses.example: The researchers weighed every plant in the plot to estimate biomass.
senses.exampleCN: 研究人员称量了样方里的每一株植物来估算生物量。
senses.why: bio- is 'life' and mass is 'a lump, a quantity of matter'. The compound simply asks how much living stuff there is, measured as mass rather than counted as individuals. The core image is a scale under an entire ecosystem.
senses.whyCN: bio- 是“生命”，mass 是“一团、一定量的物质”。这个复合词只问“活的东西有多少”，用质量来衡量，而不是数个体。核心意象是在整个生态系统下面放一台秤。

senses.title: Biomass of a species or population
senses.titleCN: 种群生物量：某一个物种的总重量
senses.definition: the total mass of one species or population in a given area
senses.definitionCN: 某一物种或种群在特定区域内的总质量
senses.example: The fish population's biomass fell by half in a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 这个鱼类种群的生物量十年间减少了一半。
senses.why: The total can be restricted to one group. The same measure is applied to a species, so biomass becomes a stock estimate rather than a whole-ecosystem figure, and fisheries use it to decide catch limits.
senses.whyCN: 总量可以被限定在一个群体上。同一把尺子用在一个物种上，biomass 就从“整个生态系统的数字”变成“资源存量估计”，渔业用它来定捕捞上限。

senses.title: Biomass at a trophic level
senses.titleCN: 营养级生物量：食物链每一层的重量
senses.definition: the mass of living matter grouped by trophic level in a food chain
senses.definitionCN: 按食物链营养级分组的活物质质量
senses.example: A pyramid of biomass shows less living matter at each higher level.
senses.exampleCN: 生物量金字塔显示，每高一层，活物质就越少。
senses.why: Ecologists arrange species by what they eat. Grouping biomass by trophic level turns a total into a structure, and the pyramid is the standard picture of that structure: producers below, predators above.
senses.whyCN: 生态学家按“吃什么”把物种排成层。把生物量按营养级分组，就把一个总数变成一种结构，而金字塔是这种结构的标准图像：生产者在下，捕食者在上。

senses.title: Plant or crop biomass
senses.titleCN: 植物与作物生物量：可收获的植物物质
senses.definition: the mass of plants or crops grown in a field, often measured to predict yield
senses.definitionCN: 田地里生长的植物或作物的质量，常用来预测产量
senses.example: Farmers measure above-ground biomass to predict the harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 农民测量地上生物量来预测收成。
senses.why: Plants are the entry point of energy into an ecosystem, and their mass is what agriculture harvests. The compound therefore becomes a yield measure in agronomy, often qualified as above-ground or below-ground.
senses.whyCN: 植物是能量进入生态系统的入口，而农业收获的正是它们的质量。于是这个复合词在农学里成为产量指标，常以“地上／地下”来限定。

senses.title: Soil microbial biomass
senses.titleCN: 土壤微生物生物量
senses.definition: the mass of microorganisms living in soil, used as an indicator of soil health
senses.definitionCN: 土壤中微生物的质量，用作土壤健康的指标
senses.example: Soil microbial biomass is a sensitive indicator of soil health.
senses.exampleCN: 土壤微生物生物量是土壤健康的一项敏感指标。
senses.why: Most living mass is invisible and below ground. Extending the word to microbes makes it a soil-health indicator, because microbes respond quickly to disturbance, fertilization and contamination.
senses.whyCN: 大部分活物质是看不见的，而且在地下。把词扩展到微生物，它就变成土壤健康指标，因为微生物对扰动、施肥和污染反应很快。

senses.title: Forest biomass and carbon stock
senses.titleCN: 森林生物量与碳储量
senses.definition: the mass of forest vegetation, especially as a measure of stored carbon
senses.definitionCN: 森林植被的质量，尤用作储存碳的度量
senses.example: The map estimates forest biomass to calculate stored carbon.
senses.exampleCN: 这张地图估算森林生物量，以计算储存的碳。
senses.why: About half of dry biomass is carbon, so weighing a forest also measures a carbon store. Climate policy made this technical equivalence central, and biomass became a number in carbon accounting.
senses.whyCN: 干生物量中约有一半是碳，所以给森林称重同时也在测量碳库。气候政策使这一技术等价关系变得关键，biomass 于是成为碳核算里的一个数字。

senses.title: Biomass as fuel feedstock
senses.titleCN: 生物质原料：可作燃料的生物材料
senses.definition: living or recently living material used as a source of fuel
senses.definitionCN: 用作燃料来源的活体或刚死去的生物材料
senses.example: The plant burns crop residues and wood chips as biomass.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂把作物残余和木屑作为生物质燃烧。
senses.why: The word shifts from a measure to a material: what was counted as living mass becomes a stock of fuel. The physical substance, not the ecological total, is now the referent, and the word behaves like 'coal'.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从“度量”转成“材料”：原本被计为活物质总量的东西，变成一堆燃料库存。此时指称的是实物，而不是生态总量，这个词在句中就像 coal 一样使用。

senses.title: Biomass power generation
senses.titleCN: 生物质发电：以生物质为燃料的技术
senses.definition: the use of biomass as fuel in boilers or power plants to produce heat and electricity
senses.definitionCN: 在锅炉或电厂中以生物质为燃料生产热与电
senses.example: A biomass plant supplies heat to the nearby town.
senses.exampleCN: 一座生物质电厂为附近的城镇供热。
senses.why: Once biomass is a fuel, it can be burned in a plant. The compound names the technology, and the word now belongs to engineering vocabulary as much as to ecology.
senses.whyCN: 一旦生物质成为燃料，就可以在电厂里燃烧。这个复合词命名的是一项技术，此时它既属于生态学词汇，也同样属于工程词汇。

senses.title: Biomass as a policy category
senses.titleCN: 政策口径中的生物质能
senses.definition: biomass counted as a renewable energy source in statistics and regulation
senses.definitionCN: 在统计与法规中被计为可再生能源的生物质
senses.example: Biomass counts as renewable in the national energy statistics.
senses.exampleCN: 在国家能源统计中，生物质被算作可再生能源。
senses.why: Policy needs categories. Biomass becomes an accounting box defined by origin rather than by ecology, and the word now answers a regulatory question: does this fuel count as renewable?
senses.whyCN: 政策需要分类。生物质于是变成一个按“来源”而非按“生态”定义的统计格子；这个词此时回答的是一个监管问题：这种燃料算不算可再生能源？

intro.en: Biomass is a 20th-century compound: Greek bio- 'life' joined to the Latin-derived English mass. It is not an inherited word, and the exact first coinage is uncertain; only the date by which it was in use is fairly well recorded.
intro.cn: biomass 是 20 世纪复合词：希腊语 bio-“生命”接上源自拉丁语的英语 mass。它不是承袭词，确切的首创情况存疑；只有“已在使用”的年代记录比较可靠。

items.en: bios means 'life, lifetime, way of life' (PIE *gwei- 'to live'). In scientific compounds bio- has meant 'organic life' since about 1800, and it is the first element of biomass.
items.cn: bios 意为“生命、寿命、生活方式”（原始印欧语 *gwei-“活”）。在科学复合词中，bio- 自约 1800 年起表示“有机生命”，是 biomass 的第一成分。

items.en: Latin massa means 'kneaded dough, lump, that which adheres together like dough', probably from Greek maza 'barley cake', related to massein 'to knead' (PIE *mag- 'to knead, fashion, fit').
items.cn: 拉丁 massa 意为“揉好的面团、团块、像面团那样黏在一起的东西”，可能来自希腊语 maza“大麦饼”，与 massein“揉”相关（原始印欧语 *mag-“揉、塑造、使合适”）。

items.en: English mass (late 14c) came from Old French masse and directly from Latin. It extended to 'a large quantity' in the 1580s, to 'bulk' about 1600, and to the physics sense 'quantity of matter' in 1704 — the sense biomass needs.
items.cn: 英语 mass（14 世纪晚期）来自古法语 masse，并直接借自拉丁语。16 世纪 80 年代扩展为“大量”，约 1600 年扩展为“体积、主体”，1704 年获得物理学义“物质的量”——正是 biomass 所需的那一层。

items.en: Etymonline records bio-mass 'by 1969' for 'the total weight of the organic substance or organisms in a given area'. Earlier uses may exist in mid-20th-century ecology and fisheries; the exact first coinage and first printed use are uncertain.
items.cn: Etymonline 把 bio-mass 记作“by 1969”，义为“某一区域内有机物质或生物的总重量”。20 世纪中期的生态学与渔业文献中可能有更早用法；确切首创与最早印刷记录存疑。

items.en: The modern energy sense moves from a measure to a commodity: what was counted as living mass becomes a stock of fuel. The link is practical — fuel is bought and sold by weight, so the measured mass turns into the traded substance.
items.cn: 现代能源义从“度量”转向“商品”：原本被计为活物质总量的东西，变成一堆燃料库存。联系是实用性的——燃料按重量买卖，于是被测量的质量变成了被交易的物质。

items.en: After the oil shocks of the 1970s, biomass entered energy policy as a renewable category alongside solar and wind. It is now standard in carbon accounting, bioenergy statistics and assessments of forest carbon stocks.
items.cn: 1970 年代石油危机之后，biomass 作为可再生能源类别与太阳能、风能并列进入能源政策。如今它已是碳核算、生物能源统计和森林碳储量评估中的标准词。

note.en: The first group contains bio- compounds and the base noun mass, which are easy to swap; the second contains ecological quantities that are often confused with biomass in measurement.
note.cn: 第一组是容易互换的 bio- 复合词与基础名词 mass；第二组是测量中常与 biomass 混淆的生态量。

entries.definition: A lump, a large quantity, or (in physics) the quantity of matter. Biomass adds bio- to restrict the mass to living material.
entries.definitionCN: 团块、大量，或物理学上的“物质的量”。biomass 加 bio- 把质量限定为活物质。

entries.definition: Gas produced by the breakdown of organic matter, mainly methane. It is a fuel made from biomass, not biomass itself.
entries.definitionCN: 有机物分解产生的气体，主要是甲烷。它是由生物质制成的燃料，而不是生物质本身。

entries.definition: Fuel made from living or recently living material. Biomass is the raw material; biofuel is the refined product.
entries.definitionCN: 由活体或刚死去的生物材料制成的燃料。biomass 是原料，biofuel 是加工后的产品。

entries.definition: The zone of life on Earth. It names a region, whereas biomass names a quantity within that region.
entries.definitionCN: 地球上的生命圈层。它命名一个区域，而 biomass 命名该区域内的一个量。

entries.definition: The amount of living matter present at a given moment. It is the actual measurement that a biomass estimate tries to represent.
entries.definitionCN: 某一时刻实际存在的活物量。它是 biomass 估计所试图表达的实际测量值。

entries.definition: The living organisms of a region as a group. It names the set of organisms, not their weight.
entries.definitionCN: 一个区域内作为整体的全部生物。它命名生物集合，而不是它们的重量。

entries.definition: Carbon-based material in soil or water, including dead and dissolved matter. Broader than biomass, which usually means living or recently living material.
entries.definitionCN: 土壤或水中含碳的物质，包括死亡与溶解的部分。比 biomass 宽，后者通常指活的或刚死去的材料。

entries.definition: The amount harvested or produced, usually for human use. It measures what is taken, while biomass measures what is there.
entries.definitionCN: 收获或产出的量，通常供人使用。它衡量被取走的部分，而 biomass 衡量现存的部分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, the real mass family, and real measurement contrasts.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的 mass 词族，以及真实的测量对比。

normal.en: bio- 'life' + mass 'lump of matter': life put on a scale and weighed.
normal.cn: bio-“生命”+ mass“一团物质”：把生命放上秤称重。

normal.en: mass has been in English since the late 14th century; the physics sense 'quantity of matter' dates from 1704 and is the one biomass uses.
normal.cn: mass 自 14 世纪晚期就在英语里；物理学义“物质的量”始于 1704 年，正是 biomass 所用的那一层。

normal.en: Contrast pair: biomass measures amount, biodiversity measures variety. Same prefix, different question.
normal.cn: 对比记忆：biomass 量数量，biodiversity 量多样。同一个前缀，不同的问题。

normal.en: Field convention: above-ground biomass and below-ground biomass are counted separately, so the word always needs a boundary.
normal.cn: 野外惯例：地上生物量与地下生物量分开计，所以这个词总需要一条边界。

normal.en: Energy chain: biomass (raw material) → biofuel or biogas (product) → bioenergy (the category).
normal.cn: 能源链：biomass（原料）→ biofuel 或 biogas（产品）→ bioenergy（类别）。

abstract.en: Picture an entire forest lifted onto an industrial scale; the number on the dial is biomass.
abstract.cn: 想象整片森林被抬上一台工业秤；表盘上的数字就是 biomass。

abstract.en: Picture a pyramid of trays, each holding less grain as you go up: that is the biomass pyramid.
abstract.cn: 想象一摞托盘堆成金字塔，越往上每一层的谷物越少：那就是生物量金字塔。

abstract.en: Picture a sack of wood chips beside a coal sack: both are fuel sold by weight, which is why 'mass' became 'biomass'.
abstract.cn: 想象一袋木屑放在一袋煤旁边：两者都是按重量卖的燃料，这正是“质量”变成“生物质”的原因。

examples.en: Tropical forests hold a large share of the world's living biomass.
examples.cn: 热带森林拥有全球活生物量的很大一部分。

examples.en: The village burns agricultural biomass instead of coal in winter.
examples.cn: 这个村子冬天烧农业生物质而不是煤。

examples.en: Satellites can estimate forest biomass from the height and density of the canopy.
examples.cn: 卫星可以根据树冠的高度和密度估算森林生物量。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拜（bio）生命，欧（o）麦（m）斯（ss）——把生命放到秤上称重 → biomass 生物量、生物质

root: 希腊 bios“生命”+ 拉丁 massa“面团、团块”演变来的 mass“质量”；20 世纪新造复合词，先指生态总量，后指可作燃料的生物质。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses share one measure: how much living matter there is. It is applied to a whole area, one species, one trophic level, one part of a plant, soil, or a forest; then the measured matter becomes a fuel, a technology, and a policy category.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项共享同一把尺子：活物质有多少。它被用于整片区域、一个物种、一个营养级、植物的一部分、土壤或森林；随后被测量之物又变成燃料、技术和政策类别。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: living matter put on a scale.
core.cn: 核心意象：把活物质放上秤。

branches.en: WHAT IS WEIGHED: the whole community, or one species singled out as a stock.
branches.cn: 称的是什么：整个群落，或被单独拿出作为存量的一个物种。
