branches.en: STRUCTURE: grouping by trophic level turns the total into a pyramid.
branches.cn: 结构：按营养级分组，把总量变成一个金字塔。

branches.en: POOLS: crops, soil microbes and forests are separate measured pools, and each has its own method.
branches.cn: 库：作物、土壤微生物与森林是各自独立的测量库，各有自己的方法。

branches.en: CONVERSION: measured matter becomes feedstock, then heat and electricity.
branches.cn: 转化：被测量的物质变成原料，再变成热与电。

branches.en: ACCOUNTING: policy turns biomass into a renewable category with rules.
branches.cn: 核算：政策把生物质变成一个带规则的可再生类别。

intro.en: Biomass is a two-part modern compound: bio- + mass. Both halves are productive in English, so the word can be understood without knowing Latin or Greek; its compound status, not its age, is what makes it transparent.
intro.cn: biomass 是两段式现代复合词：bio- + mass。两半在英语里都能产，所以不懂拉丁语或希腊语也能理解；使它透明的，是复合词的身份，而不是年代。

latinIntro.en: Only the second element is Latin: massa 'kneaded dough, lump', probably from Greek maza. The first element is Greek bios. The compound was assembled in English, which is why no single Latin word corresponds to biomass.
latinIntro.cn: 只有第二成分是拉丁语：massa“面团、团块”，可能来自希腊语 maza。第一成分是希腊语 bios。这个复合词是在英语里拼合的，所以没有单个拉丁词与 biomass 对应。

items.structure: Latin massa (lump, dough) → Old French masse
items.meaning: a lump; a large quantity; (physics) quantity of matter
items.meaningCN: 团块；大量；（物理）质量
items.example: The stone has a mass of about two kilograms.
items.exampleCN: 这块石头的质量约为两公斤。

items.meaning: total living matter; living material used as fuel
items.meaningCN: 生物量；（可作燃料的）生物质
items.example: The meadow's biomass doubles each spring.
items.exampleCN: 这片草甸的生物量每年春天翻倍。

items.meaning: energy produced from living material
items.meaningCN: 生物能源
items.example: Bioenergy supplies a small but growing share of electricity.
items.exampleCN: 生物能源在电力中占一小部分，但正在增长。

items.meaning: fuel made from living or recently living material
items.meaningCN: 生物燃料
items.example: The buses run on a biofuel blend.
items.exampleCN: 这些公交车使用混合生物燃料。

items.meaning: gas, mainly methane, produced by decomposing organic matter
items.meaningCN: 沼气；生物气
items.example: The farm produces biogas from manure.
items.exampleCN: 这个农场用粪便生产沼气。

items.meaning: the zone of life on Earth
items.meaningCN: 生物圈
items.example: Forests are a major part of the biosphere.
items.exampleCN: 森林是生物圈的重要组成部分。

items.meaning: the variety of life
items.meaningCN: 生物多样性
items.example: Biomass and biodiversity are measured differently.
items.exampleCN: 生物量与生物多样性的测量方式不同。

items.meaning: very large and heavy
items.meaningCN: 巨大的；厚重的
items.example: A massive oak stood at the edge of the field.
items.exampleCN: 田野边矗立着一棵巨大的橡树。

items.meaning: making goods in large quantities
items.meaningCN: 大批量生产
items.example: Mass production lowered the price of the device.
items.exampleCN: 大批量生产降低了这种设备的价格。

items.meaning: made from biomass
items.meaningCN: 生物质衍生的
items.example: The factory makes biomass-derived plastics.
items.exampleCN: 这家工厂生产生物质衍生塑料。

latinEntries.meaning: kneaded dough, lump, mass
latinEntries.meaningCN: 揉好的面团；团块；一堆

latinEntries.meaning: barley cake, lump
latinEntries.meaningCN: 大麦饼；团块

latinEntries.meaning: life, lifetime
latinEntries.meaningCN: 生命；寿命

definition_zh: 植物的；植物学的；植物提取的
definition_en: relating to plants as living things, to the science that studies them, or to substances obtained from them
core_image: 标本夹里一片压平的叶子，旁边贴着写有拉丁学名的小标签
scene: The field team pressed a fern into the specimen folder and wrote its botanical name on the label.
sceneCN: 这里 botanical name 中的 botanical 是「植物学名的；与正式拉丁学名有关的」（第 5 个义项：与正式拉丁学名有关）；句意：野外考察队把一株蕨类压进植物标本夹，并在标签上写下它的植物学名。场景要点：标本夹、压平的蕨叶、拉丁学名标签、采集标签。

pos.zh: 植物的；植物学的；植物提取的

derivatives.zh: 植物学上；从植物学角度
植物的；植物学的（多用于机构名称）

senses.title: Relating to living plants
senses.titleCN: 与活体植物有关
senses.definition: relating to plants as living organisms, especially their structure, growth, and kinds
senses.definitionCN: 与作为活体生物的植物有关，尤指其结构、生长与种类
senses.example: The botanical survey recorded 240 species along the ridge.
senses.exampleCN: 这次植物调查在山脊沿线记录了 240 个物种。
senses.why: The family chain runs botany → botanic → botanical, but -al does not add the meaning 'plant'. Latin -alis means 'pertaining to', so it turns botanic 'of plants' into an adjective of relation; the plant meaning sits in the Greek-derived stem botan-.
senses.whyCN: 这个词族的关系链是 botany → botanic → botanical，但 -al 并不添加“植物”这个意义。拉丁 -alis 意为“与……有关”，它把 botanic“植物的”变成表关系的形容词；植物义始终在希腊来源的词干 botan- 里。

senses.title: Belonging to the science of botany
senses.titleCN: 属于植物学这门学科
senses.definition: belonging to botany as a scientific discipline, including its methods, names, and classifications
senses.definitionCN: 属于作为学科的植物学，包括其方法、命名与分类
senses.example: Botanical nomenclature follows strict international rules.
senses.exampleCN: 植物学命名遵循严格的国际规则。
senses.why: Because botanic already meant 'pertaining to the science of plants', adding -al lets the adjective describe the discipline itself. The reference shifts from the organism to the organized body of knowledge about it.
senses.whyCN: 由于 botanic 本已表示“与植物研究有关的”，再加 -al 就让形容词可以描述这门学科本身。指称对象从植物体转向关于植物的系统知识。

senses.title: Made from or obtained from plants
senses.titleCN: 由植物制成或提取
senses.definition: made from or obtained from plants, especially in medicine, cosmetics, or agriculture
senses.definitionCN: 由植物制成或从植物中提取，尤用于医药、化妆品或农业
senses.example: The cream contains botanical extracts rather than synthetic oils.
senses.exampleCN: 这款乳霜含有植物提取物，而不是合成油脂。
senses.why: This is metonymy: the source stands for the product. The adjective still names plant origin, but the noun it modifies is now an extract or ingredient, so the plant has been reduced to material.
senses.whyCN: 这是转喻：来源代替了产品。形容词仍命名植物来源，但它修饰的名词已变成提取物或成分，于是植物被压缩成了材料。

senses.title: Relating to a garden or collection
senses.titleCN: 植物园的；植物收藏的
senses.definition: relating to a place or collection where plants are grown, labelled, and shown for study or display
senses.definitionCN: 与种植、标注并展示植物以供研究或观赏的场所或收藏有关
senses.example: The botanical garden keeps a glasshouse for tropical species.
senses.exampleCN: 这座植物园为热带物种保留了一间温室。
senses.why: A botanical garden is a living archive: plants are arranged and labelled like research material. The adjective marks the place as scientific rather than merely ornamental, so the garden becomes an instrument of botany.
senses.whyCN: 植物园是一座活的档案库：植物被排列、标注，像研究材料。这个形容词标记该场所是科学性的，而不只是观赏性的，于是园圃成了植物学的工具。

senses.title: Relating to the formal Latin name
senses.titleCN: 与正式拉丁学名有关
senses.definition: relating to the formal Latin name or taxonomic placing of a plant
senses.definitionCN: 与植物的正式拉丁学名或分类位置有关
senses.example: The botanical name for the common oak is Quercus robur.
senses.exampleCN: 普通橡树的植物学名是 Quercus robur。
senses.why: Naming is the most precise layer of botany. A botanical name is not a local label but a fixed Latin address that places the plant in a genus and species, so the adjective signals taxonomic exactness.
senses.whyCN: 命名是植物学中最精确的一层。botanical name 不是地方俗称，而是把植物固定在属与种中的拉丁地址，因此这个形容词标记的是分类学上的精确性。

senses.title: Noun: plant-derived substances
senses.titleCN: 名词：植物提取物
senses.definition: in the plural, substances or ingredients obtained from plants, used in cosmetics, supplements, or pesticides
senses.definitionCN: 复数形式指从植物取得的物质或成分，用于化妆品、补充剂或杀虫剂
senses.example: Regulators require proof that botanicals are free of contaminants.
senses.exampleCN: 监管机构要求证明植物提取物不含污染物。
senses.why: This is a zero conversion: the phrase 'botanical ingredients' drops its head noun, and the adjective remains as the class name. The plural botanicals then names the category of such substances.
senses.whyCN: 这是零派生：短语 botanical ingredients 省略中心名词，形容词留下来充当类别名。复数 botanicals 于是指这一类物质。

senses.title: Relating to scientific plant drawing
senses.titleCN: 植物科学绘图的
senses.definition: relating to accurate drawings or prints that record a plant's form so that it can be identified
senses.definitionCN: 与准确记录植物形态、以便识别之用的绘图或版画有关
senses.example: The herbarium keeps a botanical illustration of every type specimen.
senses.exampleCN: 标本馆为每一份模式标本保存一幅植物学插图。
senses.why: An identification drawing must show veins, hairs, and flower parts rather than a pleasing view. Botanical therefore marks the image as a diagnostic record, extending the adjective from the plant to the way it is documented.
senses.whyCN: 用于识别的绘图必须画出叶脉、毛被与花部，而不是一幅好看的景。botanical 因此标记这幅图是诊断性记录，把形容词从植物本身延伸到记录植物的方式。

senses.title: Usage boundary: botanical versus botanic
senses.titleCN: 用法边界：botanical 与 botanic
senses.definition: both mean 'of plants'; botanical is the default modern adjective, while botanic survives mainly in fixed institutional names
senses.definitionCN: 两者都表示“植物的”；botanical 是现代默认形容词，botanic 主要残留在固定的机构名称中
senses.example: The Royal Botanic Gardens use botanic in their title, though the work done there is botanical.
senses.exampleCN: 英国皇家植物园在名称里用 botanic，但那里做的工作是 botanical 的。
senses.why: -ic and -ical are twin adjective endings built on the same stem. English specialised them: botanic stayed in older names such as botanic garden, while botanical took over general and technical use.
senses.whyCN: -ic 与 -ical 是同一词干上的成对形容词后缀。英语把它们分工了：botanic 留在 botanic garden 等较老名称里，而 botanical 接管了一般与技术用法。

senses.title: Usage boundary: botanical versus herbal
senses.titleCN: 用法边界：botanical 与 herbal
senses.definition: botanical describes plant origin neutrally; herbal implies the traditional use of whole plants as medicine
senses.definitionCN: botanical 中性描述植物来源；herbal 暗示把整株植物作传统药用的做法
senses.example: A herbal tea is brewed from leaves; a botanical blend may be any plant-derived mixture.
senses.exampleCN: herbal tea 是用叶子冲泡的；botanical blend 则可以是任何植物来源的混合物。
senses.why: Herbal carries the older craft of gathering and brewing herbs. Botanical is the laboratory-neutral term, which is why a cosmetics firm prefers it: it claims a plant source without claiming medical action.
senses.whyCN: herbal 带着采集、煎煮草药的旧手艺色彩。botanical 是实验室式的中性词，因此化妆品公司更爱用它：它只声称植物来源，不声称医疗功效。

intro.en: Botanical is a derived adjective, not a root word. The Greek-derived stem names plants and pasturage; botanic entered English first, and -al made botanical from it. The modern family chain is often given as botany → botanic → botanical, but that is a chain of meaning and word formation, not a single line of descent.
intro.cn: botanical 是派生形容词，不是词根词。希腊来源的词干先表示植物与牧草；botanic 先进入英语，-al 再由它构成 botanical。现代常把词族链记作 botany → botanic → botanical，但那是意义与构词的链条，不是一条单向血统。

items.en: Greek botanē meant 'plant, grass, pasture, fodder', and botanikos meant 'of herbs'. Etymonline notes that the Greek words seem to have more to do with pasturage than with plants; related forms include botamia 'pastures, meadows', boter 'herdsman', and boton 'grazing beast'. The deeper origin of the family is not established.
items.cn: 希腊语 botanē 意为“植物、草、牧场、牧草”，botanikos 意为“草本的”。etymonline 指出这些希腊词更多与放牧有关，而非与植物学有关；相关形式有 botamia“牧场、草地”、boter“牧人”、boton“吃草的牲畜”。这个词族的更深来源尚未确定。

items.en: Medieval Latin botanicus 'of plants' carried the Greek adjective into learned Latin, and French botanique (17c.) passed it into English. Latin had no native name for plant science, so this borrowed stem did the work.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 botanicus“植物的”把这个希腊形容词带入学术拉丁语，法语 botanique（17 世纪）再把它传入英语。拉丁语没有本土的植物科学名称，于是由这个借来的词干承担。

items.en: English botanic is recorded from the 1650s, meaning 'pertaining to the science or study of plants'. It came from French botanique or directly from Medieval Latin botanicus, and it is the shorter of the two English adjectives.
items.cn: 英语 botanic 于 17 世纪 50 年代有记录，意为“与植物研究有关的”。它来自法语 botanique，或直接来自中世纪拉丁语 botanicus，是两个英语形容词中较短的一个。

items.en: Botanical is recorded from the same decade, formed as botanic + -al. Latin -alis (through French -al) means 'of, like, pertaining to', so -al adds relation, not plant meaning. Morphologically botanical is botanic + -al; it is not built directly from botany with -ical.
items.cn: botanical 在同一时期有记录，由 botanic + -al 构成。拉丁 -alis（经法语 -al）意为“属于、像、与……有关”，所以 -al 添加的是关系，不是植物义。形态上 botanical 是 botanic + -al，并不是由 botany 直接加 -ical。

items.en: Botany, the name of the discipline, is recorded from the 1690s, formed from botanic with -y on the model of astronomy. Botanist is recorded from the 1680s as botany + -ist. Etymonline's dates make the person word appear slightly earlier than the field noun; that apparent contradiction means the exact derivation order is uncertain.
items.cn: 表示学科的 botany 于 17 世纪 90 年代有记录，由 botanic 加 -y、仿 astronomy 构成。botanist 于 17 世纪 80 年代有记录，按 botany + -ist 解释。etymonline 的年代让人这个词略早于学科名词；这一表面矛盾说明确切的派生先后存疑。

items.en: Modern usage extends the adjective from living plants to extracts, gardens, Latin names, drawings, and products. The 'plant-derived' sense is a later narrowing whose exact first date is not recorded. Botanical is now the neutral default, while botanic survives chiefly in institution names.
items.cn: 现代用法把这个形容词从活体植物延伸到提取物、园圃、拉丁学名、绘图与产品。“植物提取的”义是后来收窄出来的，其确切最早年代未见记录。botanical 现为中性默认词，botanic 主要残留在机构名称中。

note.en: The first group shares the botan- stem with different endings; the second separates plant-related adjectives by domain and by what part of the plant they stress.
note.cn: 第一组共享 botan- 词干而后缀不同；第二组按领域以及所强调的植物部位来区分与植物相关的形容词。

entries.definition: The older adjective from the same stem, now mostly fixed in names such as botanic garden. It lacks the general 'plant-derived' use of botanical.
entries.definitionCN: 由同一词干构成的较老形容词，现多固定在 botanic garden 等名称中。它没有 botanical 那种一般的“植物提取的”用法。

entries.definition: The science that studies plants. It is the field itself, while botanical is the adjective of relation built on botanic.
entries.definitionCN: 研究植物的科学。它是学科本身，而 botanical 是建立在 botanic 上的关系形容词。

entries.definition: A person who studies plants. It shares botan- with botanical but adds -ist, so it names a practitioner rather than a quality.
entries.definitionCN: 研究植物的人。它与 botanical 共享 botan-，但加上 -ist，因此命名的是从业者，而不是性质。

entries.definition: In botanical terms; from the viewpoint of plant science. The -ly ending makes it modify a verb or a whole statement, not a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 从植物学角度；以植物学的说法。后缀 -ly 使它修饰动词或整句，而不是名词。

entries.definition: Relating to herbs used as medicine or flavouring. It stresses traditional preparation, while botanical merely states a plant origin.
entries.definitionCN: 与作药用或调味用的草药有关。它强调传统制法，而 botanical 只陈述植物来源。

entries.definition: Relating to flowers, not to plants in general. A floral scent comes from blossoms; a botanical survey covers mosses and ferns too.
entries.definitionCN: 与花有关，而非笼统与植物有关。floral scent 来自花朵；植物调查则连苔藓和蕨类也包含。

entries.definition: Relating to the cultivation of gardens. It names the growing practice, while botanical names the scientific study of the plants themselves.
entries.definitionCN: 与园圃栽培有关。它命名的是种植实践，而 botanical 命名的是对植物本身的科学研究。

entries.definition: Relating to plants as opposed to animals or minerals. It is a technical contrast word and rarely appears where botanical would do.
entries.definitionCN: 与植物有关，以区别于动物或矿物。它是技术性的对比词，很少出现在本可用 botanical 的地方。

normalIntro.en: Real associations: the Greek 'plant, fodder' stem, the twin endings -ic and -ical, and the living collocations botanical name and botanical garden.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联想：希腊语“植物、牧草”词干、成对后缀 -ic 与 -ical，以及真实搭配 botanical name、botanical garden。

normal.en: botanic + -al = botanical. The -al only adds 'pertaining to'; the plant meaning comes from the Greek-derived stem.
normal.cn: botanic + -al = botanical。-al 只添加“与……有关”；植物义来自希腊来源的词干。

normal.en: Greek botanē was fodder and pasture before it was a science; the same word fed animals and later fed scholars.
normal.cn: 希腊语 botanē 先是牧草与牧场，后来才成为科学；同一个词先喂养牲畜，后来喂养学者。

normal.en: botanic and botanical are twins from one stem. Older institutions kept the short twin; everyday English took the long one.
normal.cn: botanic 与 botanical 是同一词干生出的双胞胎。较老的机构留下短的那个，日常英语取了长的那个。

normal.en: A botanical name is a Latin address: genus first, species second, and the plant can be found from that address anywhere.
normal.cn: botanical name 是一个拉丁地址：先属后种，凭这个地址在任何地方都能找到这株植物。

normal.en: Botanicals in a cream are the plant parts reduced to ingredients; the adjective has become the noun for the material itself.
normal.cn: 乳霜里的 botanicals 是被还原成成分的植物部分；形容词已经变成指材料本身的名词。

abstract.en: A pressed leaf with a label: the moment a living thing becomes an object of knowledge is the moment botanical begins.
abstract.cn: 一片压平的叶子加一张标签：活物变成知识对象的那一刻，就是 botanical 开始的地方。

abstract.en: A herbarium drawer is an archive where plants are filed like documents, and botanical is the stamp on the folder.
abstract.cn: 标本馆的抽屉是一座档案库，植物像文件一样被归档，botanical 就是文件夹上的那枚印章。

abstract.en: A garden bed and a laboratory bench use one word because both arrange plants so that someone can look closely and name what is there.
abstract.cn: 花圃与实验台共用一个词，因为两者都把植物安排妥当，好让人靠近观察并说出那是什么。

examples.en: The botanical garden holds one of the oldest collections of alpine plants.
examples.cn: 这座植物园收藏着最古老的高山植物标本之一。

examples.en: Botanical extracts are listed separately from synthetic fragrance oils.
examples.cn: 植物提取物与合成香精油分开列示。

examples.en: Students learn to write a botanical description of a single leaf.
examples.cn: 学生学着为一片叶子写出植物学描述。

dict_mnemonic.text: “博坦尼克”——博物学家在植物园里给每片叶子贴标签 → botanical 植物的、植物学的

root: botanic（植物的）+ -al（拉丁 -alis，“与……有关”）；botanic 来自法语 botanique 或中世纪拉丁语 botanicus，再上溯希腊语 botanikos“草本的”、botanē“植物、牧场、牧草”；更早的联系存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of botanical follow one movement: take a living plant, press and label it, then let that label travel to extracts, gardens, Latin names, drawings, and products.
sensesIntro.cn: botanical 的九个义项沿着一条动作链展开：把活体植物压平、贴标签，再让这张标签延伸到提取物、园圃、拉丁学名、绘图与产品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plant is pressed, labelled, and named, so a living thing becomes an object of knowledge.
core.cn: 核心意象：植物被压平、贴标签、命名，于是一个活物变成了知识对象。

branches.en: PLANT LIFE AND DISCIPLINE: the adjective points first at the organism, then at the organized science that studies it.
branches.cn: 植物生命与学科：形容词先指向植物体，再指向研究它的系统科学。

branches.en: MATERIAL: the plant is reduced to an extract, and the adjective becomes the plural noun for such substances.
branches.cn: 材料：植物被还原为提取物，形容词又变成指这类物质的复数名词。

branches.en: PLACE AND NAME: a labelled garden and a Latin binomial are the plant turned into an addressable record.
branches.cn: 场所与名称：标注过的园圃和拉丁双名，都是植物被变成可检索的记录。

branches.en: RECORD AND TWIN: scientific drawing is documentation, and botanic marks the older institutional twin of botanical.
branches.cn: 记录与孪生词：科学绘图是文档化，而 botanic 标记 botanical 较老的机构用孪生形式。

branches.en: BOUNDARY: herbal marks the traditional medicinal edge that botanical avoids by staying neutral.
branches.cn: 边界：herbal 标出传统药用的边缘，而 botanical 以中性立场避开它。

intro.en: Botanical has no live English prefix. It is botanic + -al; the Greek and Latin material sits frozen inside the stem, and English can still add -ly to the finished adjective.
intro.cn: botanical 没有活的英语前缀。它是 botanic + -al；希腊语与拉丁语材料凝固在词干内部，英语还能在成品形容词后加 -ly。

latinIntro.en: One Greek stem botan- runs through botany, botanic, botanical, and botanist. Greek botanē meant 'plant, pasture, fodder' and botanikos meant 'of herbs'; Medieval Latin botanicus carried both into the schools.
latinIntro.cn: 一个希腊词干 botan- 贯穿 botany、botanic、botanical 与 botanist。希腊语 botanē 意为“植物、牧场、牧草”，botanikos 意为“草本的”；中世纪拉丁语 botanicus 把两者带入学术。

items.structure: botan- (plant stem) + -y (name of a field, on the model of astronomy)
items.meaning: the science of plants; the suffix names a domain of knowledge, not a person or quality
items.meaningCN: 植物学；后缀 -y 命名一个知识领域，而不是人或性质
items.example: Botany began as the description and naming of useful plants.
items.exampleCN: 植物学最初是对有用植物的描述与命名。

items.meaning: pertaining to the science or study of plants; the shorter adjective
items.meaningCN: 与植物研究有关的；较短的那个形容词
items.example: The botanic collection was catalogued by species.
items.exampleCN: 这批植物收藏按物种编目。

items.meaning: relating to plants or botany; the longer and now default adjective
items.meaningCN: 植物的；植物学的；较长且现为默认的形容词
items.example: The botanical survey listed every fern in the valley.
items.exampleCN: 这次植物调查列出了山谷里的每一种蕨类。

items.meaning: a person who studies plants; the shift is from a field to its practitioner
items.meaningCN: 研究植物的人；语义从学科转到从业者
items.example: A botanist identified the moss as a new species.
items.exampleCN: 一位植物学家鉴定出这种苔藓是新物种。

items.meaning: in botanical terms; the adjective becomes an adverb of viewpoint
items.meaningCN: 从植物学角度；形容词变成表视角的副词
items.example: Botanically, the tomato is a fruit.
items.exampleCN: 从植物学上说，番茄是一种果实。

items.structure: botan- + -ize (to act in a particular way)
items.meaning: to collect or study plants in the field; the suffix turns the field into an activity
items.meaningCN: 在野外采集或研究植物；后缀把学科变成活动
items.example: They botanized along the stream for the whole morning.
items.exampleCN: 他们整个上午沿溪采集植物。

items.meaning: plant-derived ingredients; the adjective has become a class noun
items.meaningCN: 植物提取物；形容词已变成类别名词
items.example: The label lists three botanicals and no synthetic perfume.
items.exampleCN: 标签列出三种植物成分，不含合成香精。

items.meaning: relating to how a particular people use plants
items.meaningCN: 与某一族群如何使用植物有关
items.example: Ethnobotanical fieldwork records which plants a village uses for medicine.
items.exampleCN: 民族植物学田野工作记录一个村庄用哪些植物作药。

items.meaning: the study of fossil plants
items.meaningCN: 研究化石植物的古植物学
items.example: Paleobotany reconstructs ancient forests from fossil leaves.
items.exampleCN: 古植物学根据化石叶片重建远古森林。

latinEntries.meaning: plant, grass, pasture, fodder
latinEntries.meaningCN: 植物；草；牧场；牧草

latinEntries.meaning: of herbs or plants
latinEntries.meaningCN: 草本的；植物的

latinEntries.meaning: relating to plants; the immediate source of botanic
latinEntries.meaningCN: 与植物有关的；botanic 的直接来源

latinEntries.meaning: of, like, pertaining to; the ancestor of English -al
latinEntries.meaningCN: 属于、像、与……有关的；英语 -al 的前身

definition_zh: 植物学家；研究植物的专家
definition_en: a person who studies plants scientifically, or who collects, identifies, and classifies them
core_image: 一个人蹲在草丛里，用放大镜看花蕊，笔记本上写满拉丁学名
scene: In the glasshouse, the botanist used tweezers to take a stamen and wrote the family, genus, species, and collection number in her notebook.
sceneCN: 这里 botanist 是「植物学家」（第 1 个义项：以研究植物为专业的人）；句意：温室里，植物学家用镊子取下一枚花蕊，在记录本上写下科、属、种和采集编号。场景要点：镊子、花蕊、记录本、拉丁学名、采集编号、温室植株。

pos.zh: 植物学家；植物学工作者

collocations.zh: 经济植物学家（研究有用植物）
这位植物学家的采集品

derivatives.zh: 植物学上；从植物学角度
采集植物；进行植物考察

senses.title: A scientist who studies plants
senses.titleCN: 研究植物的科学家
senses.definition: a person who studies plants as a profession, usually with formal training in botany
senses.definitionCN: 以研究植物为职业的人，通常受过正式的植物学训练
senses.example: She became a botanist after finishing her doctorate on alpine mosses.
senses.exampleCN: 她完成关于高山苔藓的博士研究后成为植物学家。
senses.why: Botanist is botan- plus -ist, the agent suffix. The stem names the field and -ist names the person, so the word begins as 'one who practises botany' rather than as a description of a quality.
senses.whyCN: botanist 是 botan- 加施动后缀 -ist。词干命名领域，-ist 命名人，因此这个词的起点是“从事植物学的人”，而不是描述某种性质。

senses.title: Field botanist: the collector outdoors
senses.titleCN: 野外植物学家：在户外采集的人
senses.definition: a botanist who works in the field, finding, pressing, and recording plants where they grow
senses.definitionCN: 在野外工作的植物学家，在植物生长地寻找、压制并记录植物
senses.example: A field botanist spent three weeks surveying the valley's orchids.
senses.exampleCN: 一位野外植物学家花了三周调查这个山谷的兰科植物。
senses.why: The suffix identifies the person, while 'field' identifies where the practice happens. Collecting is the oldest form of the job: the specimen comes before the theory, so the agent noun is narrowed by its workplace.
senses.whyCN: 后缀标识人，field 标识实践发生的地点。采集是这份工作最古老的形式：标本先于理论，因此这个施动名词被工作场所所收窄。

senses.title: Taxonomist: the namer and classifier
senses.titleCN: 分类学家：命名与归类的人
senses.definition: a botanist who describes, names, and places plants in the taxonomic system
senses.definitionCN: 描述、命名并把植物放入分类系统的植物学家
senses.example: The botanist published a revision of the genus in a taxonomic journal.
senses.exampleCN: 这位植物学家在分类学期刊上发表了对该属的修订。
senses.why: Naming is the part of botany that turns a plant into a retrievable record. A taxonomic botanist is therefore the keeper of the Latin labels, a role rather than a new word.
senses.whyCN: 命名是把植物变成可检索记录的那部分植物学。因此分类植物学家就是拉丁标签的保管人；这是一种角色，而不是另一个新词。

senses.title: Specialist branches of the profession
senses.titleCN: 职业内部的专门分支
senses.definition: a botanist may also be a plant physiologist, ecologist, geneticist, or molecular botanist, depending on the layer of the plant studied
senses.definitionCN: 植物学家也可以是植物生理学家、生态学家、遗传学家或分子植物学家，取决于研究植物的哪一层
senses.example: A molecular botanist studies the genes that control flowering time.
senses.exampleCN: 一位分子植物学家研究控制开花时间的基因。
senses.why: The same agent noun covers every subfield because all of them study plants. The modifier names the layer of study, not a different kind of person, so the core sense stays intact.
senses.whyCN: 同一个施动名词覆盖所有子领域，因为它们都在研究植物。修饰语命名的是研究层次，而不是另一种人，因此核心义保持不变。

senses.title: Historical: herbalist and plant collector
senses.titleCN: 历史义：草药师与植物采集者
senses.definition: before botany became a university science, a botanist was often a herbalist or an amateur collector of medicinal plants
senses.definitionCN: 在植物学成为大学科学之前，botanist 常指草药师或采集药用植物的业余爱好者
senses.example: In the 17th century a botanist might keep both a herb garden and a dried collection.
senses.exampleCN: 在 17 世纪，一位 botanist 可能既经营药草园，又保存干燥标本。
senses.why: The word is recorded from the 17th century, when plant knowledge was still tied to medicine. The modern professional sense grew out of that older practical role, so the agent noun widened before it narrowed.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从 17 世纪起有记录，当时植物知识仍与医药相连。现代的职业义正是从那更早的实用角色中长出来的：这个施动名词先变宽，后又收窄。

senses.title: Applied botanists outside academia
senses.titleCN: 学术界之外的应用植物学家
senses.definition: a botanist employed in agriculture, forestry, conservation, or industry, applying plant science to practical problems
senses.definitionCN: 受雇于农业、林业、保护或工业，把植物科学用于实际问题的植物学家
senses.example: An economic botanist searches for wild relatives of crop plants.
senses.exampleCN: 一位经济植物学家寻找农作物的野生近缘种。
senses.why: The suffix says what the person knows, not where they work. Applied fields therefore use the same noun and add a modifier for the sector, which is how the profession extends beyond the university.
senses.whyCN: 后缀说明这个人懂什么，而不是在哪里工作。因此应用领域用同一个名词，只添加标明行业的修饰语；职业范围就这样延伸到大学之外。

senses.title: Everyday: the knowledgeable plant lover
senses.titleCN: 日常用法：懂植物的爱好者
senses.definition: in informal use, a very knowledgeable plant enthusiast may be called a botanist, though not a professional one
senses.definitionCN: 非正式用法中，非常懂植物的爱好者也可被称为 botanist，但并非职业人士
senses.example: My neighbour is a botanist of sorts; she can name every weed in the lane.
senses.exampleCN: 我邻居算得上半个植物学家，巷子里每种野草她都叫得出名字。
senses.why: The word can be used loosely because the boundary of the profession is knowledge, not a licence. The hedge 'of sorts' keeps the informal use honest while borrowing the prestige of the agent noun.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以宽松使用，因为这一职业的边界是知识，而不是执照。of sorts 这样的限定语让非正式用法保持诚实，同时借用了这个施动名词的声望。

senses.title: Usage boundary: botanist versus horticulturist
senses.titleCN: 用法边界：botanist 与 horticulturist
senses.definition: a botanist studies plants; a horticulturist grows and cultivates them for gardens, food, or sale
senses.definitionCN: botanist 研究植物；horticulturist 为园艺、食用或销售而栽培植物
senses.example: The botanist identified the species; the horticulturist worked out how to propagate it.
senses.exampleCN: 植物学家鉴定了物种；园艺师则研究出如何繁殖它。
senses.why: Both work with plants, but one produces knowledge and the other produces plants. The suffixes differ as -ist of a science versus -ist of a cultivation practice, so the two agent nouns are not interchangeable.
senses.whyCN: 两者都跟植物打交道，但一个产出知识，另一个产出植株。后缀同样都是 -ist，区别在于一个是科学，一个是栽培实践，因此两个施动名词不能互换。

senses.title: Usage boundary: botanist versus biologist
senses.titleCN: 用法边界：botanist 与 biologist
senses.definition: a botanist is a kind of biologist; biologist is the wider term for anyone who studies living things
senses.definitionCN: botanist 是 biologist 的一种；biologist 是研究生物者的更宽泛称呼
senses.example: As a biologist she works on fungi; as a botanist she would have to exclude them.
senses.exampleCN: 作为生物学家她研究真菌；若作为植物学家，她就得把真菌排除在外。
senses.why: The stem restricts the field to plants, while -ist only marks the practitioner. Botanist is therefore narrower than biologist, not a synonym of it, because the stem does the restricting.
senses.whyCN: 词干把领域限制在植物，而 -ist 只标记从业者。因此 botanist 比 biologist 窄，不是它的同义词，收窄工作由词干完成。

intro.en: Botanist is the same stem as botany with a different suffix: botan- names the field and -ist names the person. The stem is Greek in origin and reached English through medieval Latin; the suffix is a general agent ending, not a plant word. The recorded dates for botanist and botany are slightly inconsistent, so the exact order of formation is uncertain.
intro.cn: botanist 与 botany 词干相同，后缀不同：botan- 命名领域，-ist 命名人。词干源自希腊语，经中世纪拉丁语进入英语；后缀是一般的施动者词尾，本身不是植物词。botanist 与 botany 的记录年代略有矛盾，因此确切的构词先后存疑。

items.en: Greek botanē meant 'plant, grass, pasture, fodder', and botanikos meant 'of herbs'. Etymonline notes that these words seem to have more to do with pasturage than with plant science; related forms include botamia 'pastures' and boter 'herdsman'. The deeper origin of the family is not established.
items.cn: 希腊语 botanē 意为“植物、草、牧场、牧草”，botanikos 意为“草本的”。etymonline 指出这些词更多与放牧有关，而非与植物科学有关；相关形式有 botamia“牧场”、boter“牧人”。这个词族的更深来源尚未确定。

items.en: Medieval Latin botanicus 'of plants' carried the Greek adjective into learned Latin, and French botanique (17c.) passed the same stem into English as botanic.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 botanicus“植物的”把这个希腊形容词带入学术拉丁语，法语 botanique（17 世纪）又把同一词干以 botanic 的形式传入英语。

items.en: English botanic is recorded from the 1650s, botany from the 1690s, and botanist from the 1680s. Etymonline derives botany from botanic, adding -y on the model of astronomy, and botanist from botany + -ist. The dates leave botanist apparently earlier than botany; that contradiction means the exact derivation order is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 botanic 于 17 世纪 50 年代有记录，botany 于 17 世纪 90 年代有记录，botanist 于 17 世纪 80 年代有记录。etymonline 认为 botany 来自 botanic，仿 astronomy 加 -y；botanist 来自 botany + -ist。这些年代使 botanist 表面上早于 botany；这一矛盾说明确切的派生先后存疑。

items.en: -ist comes from Greek -istēs through Latin -ista and French -iste. It is built from the stem ending of verbs in -izein plus the agent suffix -tēs, and it forms nouns meaning 'one who practises or believes', as in artist, scientist, and botanist. It adds no plant meaning of its own.
items.cn: -ist 经拉丁语 -ista、法语 -iste 上溯希腊语 -istēs。它由 -izein 动词词干的结尾加施动后缀 -tēs 构成，形成表示“从事者或信奉者”的名词，如 artist、scientist、botanist。它本身不添加任何植物含义。

items.en: Herbaria, overseas expeditions, and Linnaean taxonomy turned plant study into a paid profession. Botanist then settled into its modern sense of a trained plant scientist, while the older overlap with herbalists and gardeners faded. The exact period of this shift is not fixed.
items.cn: 标本馆、海外考察与林奈分类学把植物研究变成有薪职业。botanist 由此固定为“受过训练的植物科学家”这一现代义，而与草药师、园艺者的旧重叠逐渐消退。这一转变的确切时期并无定论。

items.en: Modern usage adds modifiers for molecular, ecological, and conservation specialties but keeps one noun. The word stays narrower than biologist because its stem names plants, not life in general.
items.cn: 现代用法为分子、生态与保护等方向添加修饰语，却保留同一个名词。由于词干命名的是植物而非一切生命，这个词始终比 biologist 窄。

note.en: The first group is the same botan- stem with three different endings; the second separates the plant scientist from the gardener, the herbalist, the ecologist, and the wider life scientist.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个 botan- 词干配三种不同后缀；第二组把植物学家与园艺者、草药师、生态学家及更宽泛的生命科学家区分开。

entries.definition: The science of plants. It is the field itself, while botanist is the person who practises it.
entries.definitionCN: 研究植物的科学。它是学科本身，而 botanist 是从事这门学科的人。

entries.definition: Relating to plants or botany. It describes a quality or relation, while botanist names a person.
entries.definitionCN: 植物的；植物学的。它描述性质或关系，而 botanist 命名人。

entries.definition: In botanical terms; from the viewpoint of plant science. The -ly ending makes it modify a verb or statement, not a person.
entries.definitionCN: 从植物学角度；以植物学的说法。-ly 结尾使它修饰动词或陈述，而不是人。

entries.definition: To collect or study plants in the field. The -ize suffix turns the field into an activity, so it names what a botanist does, not who they are.
entries.definitionCN: 在野外采集或研究植物。-ize 后缀把学科变成活动，因此它命名植物学家做什么，而不是他们是谁。

entries.definition: A person who studies living things. Botanist is a narrower kind of biologist, limited to plants.
entries.definitionCN: 研究生物的人。botanist 是 biologist 中较窄的一类，限于植物。

entries.definition: A person who grows and cultivates plants for gardens, food, or sale. The focus is on producing plants, not on producing knowledge about them.
entries.definitionCN: 为园艺、食用或销售而栽培植物的人。重点在产出植株，而不是产出关于植物的知识。

entries.definition: A person who uses plants as medicine, often in a traditional practice. Botanist studies plants scientifically rather than treating patients with them.
entries.definitionCN: 用植物治病、常从事传统实践的人。botanist 以科学方式研究植物，而不是用植物治疗病人。

entries.definition: A person who studies how organisms relate to their environment. A botanist may study a plant's ecology, but the ecologist's unit is the whole system.
entries.definitionCN: 研究生物与环境关系的人。植物学家可能研究某种植物的生态，但生态学家的单位是整个系统。

normalIntro.en: Real associations: the agent suffix -ist, the field noun botany, and the working verbs botanize and botanically describe.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联想：施动后缀 -ist、学科名词 botany，以及实际使用的动词 botanize 与副词 botanically。

normal.en: botany + -ist = botanist: the field first, the person second. The suffix adds 'one who practises', not 'plant'.
normal.cn: botany + -ist = botanist：先有学科，再有人。后缀添加的是“从事者”，不是“植物”。

normal.en: The -ist in botanist is the same -ist as in artist and scientist: a person who does the work.
normal.cn: botanist 里的 -ist 与 artist、scientist 里的 -ist 相同：做这项工作的人。

normal.en: A field botanist carries a press and a notebook; the specimen is the first document of the science.
normal.cn: 野外植物学家带着标本夹和记录本；标本是这门科学的第一份文档。

normal.en: A taxonomic botanist owns the Latin names: genus and species are the addresses that make a plant findable.
normal.cn: 分类植物学家掌管拉丁名：属与种是让植物可被找到的地址。

normal.en: Botanist is narrower than biologist because botan- names plants, while bio- names life in general.
normal.cn: botanist 比 biologist 窄，因为 botan- 命名植物，而 bio- 命名一般生命。

abstract.en: A person bent over a flower with a lens: the whole profession is the act of looking closely and writing down what is seen.
abstract.cn: 一个人俯身用放大镜看花：整个职业就是靠近观察并把所见写下来。

abstract.en: A herbarium sheet is a passport: the plant travels through time because someone signed it with a Latin name.
abstract.cn: 一份腊叶标本就是一本护照：因为有人在上面签了拉丁名，这株植物得以穿越时间。

abstract.en: The botanist stands between the wild plant and the written record, turning a living thing into a repeatable observation.
abstract.cn: 植物学家站在野生植物与书面记录之间，把一个活物变成可重复的观察。

examples.en: The botanist spent the morning pressing specimens for the herbarium.
examples.cn: 这位植物学家花了一上午为标本馆压制标本。

examples.en: A botanist and a horticulturist worked together to save the rare orchid.
examples.cn: 一位植物学家和一位园艺师合作拯救这种稀有兰花。

examples.en: As a botanist, she is careful to distinguish mosses from lichens.
examples.cn: 作为植物学家，她谨慎地把苔藓与地衣区分开来。

dict_mnemonic.text: “博坦尼斯特”——博物（博）学家在园里蹲（tan）下，拿着放大镜研究植物 → botanist 植物学家

root: botan-（植物、牧草，希腊 botanē / botanikos，经中世纪拉丁语 botanicus 入英语）+ -ist（施动后缀，希腊 -istēs，经拉丁 -ista、法语 -iste）；-ist 表示从业者，不表示植物。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of botanist all name the same person from different angles: a trained plant scientist, a field collector, a namer, a specialist, a historical herbalist, an applied worker, a keen amateur, and two boundary cases.
sensesIntro.cn: botanist 的九个义项从不同角度命名同一种人：受过训练的植物科学家、野外采集者、命名者、专门方向研究者、历史中的草药师、应用工作者、热心的业余爱好者，以及两个边界情形。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person who looks closely at plants, collects them, and turns them into named records.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人靠近观察植物、采集它们，并把它们变成有名字的记录。

branches.en: CORE: the agent noun itself, 'one who practises botany'.
branches.cn: 核心：施动名词本身，即“从事植物学的人”。

branches.en: FIELD AND NAME: collecting outdoors and naming in the herbarium are the two oldest halves of the job.
branches.cn: 野外与命名：户外采集与标本馆命名，是这份工作最古老的两半。

branches.en: SPECIALTY AND APPLICATION: the same noun takes modifiers for the layer studied or the sector worked in.
branches.cn: 专门方向与应用：同一个名词接受修饰语，标明研究层次或工作行业。

branches.en: HISTORY AND EVERYDAY: the old herbalist role and the knowledgeable amateur both stretch the word beyond the licensed profession.
branches.cn: 历史与日常：旧时的草药师角色与懂行的业余爱好者，都把词义拉到执照职业之外。

branches.en: BOUNDARIES: horticulturist produces plants, biologist studies all life; botanist sits between them.
branches.cn: 边界：horticulturist 产出植株，biologist 研究一切生命；botanist 位于两者之间。

intro.en: Botanist has one live suffix, -ist, on a borrowed Greek stem. The suffix is productive and can be added to other fields, while botan- stays fixed and supplies the plant meaning.
intro.cn: botanist 在借来的希腊词干上只有一个活后缀 -ist。这个后缀能产，可加在其他领域上；botan- 则固定不变，提供植物义。

latinIntro.en: The botan- stem is Greek, carried into English through Medieval Latin botanicus and French botanique. The agent suffix -ist also has a Latin stage, -ista, before it reached French and English.
latinIntro.cn: botan- 词干是希腊语，经中世纪拉丁语 botanicus 与法语 botanique 进入英语。施动后缀 -ist 也有拉丁阶段 -ista，之后才到法语和英语。

items.meaning: a person who studies plants; the shift is from a field to its practitioner
items.meaningCN: 研究植物的人；语义从学科转到从业者
items.example: The botanist recorded the plant's habitat and date.
items.exampleCN: 这位植物学家记录了该植物的生境与日期。

items.structure: botan- + -y (name of a field, on the model of astronomy)
items.meaning: the science of plants; the noun that supplies the profession's field
items.meaningCN: 植物学；为这一职业提供学科名的名词
items.example: Botany and zoology were once taught together as natural history.
items.exampleCN: 植物学与动物学曾作为博物学一起教授。

items.meaning: pertaining to plants; the shorter adjective
items.meaningCN: 植物的；较短的那个形容词
items.example: The botanic garden dates from the eighteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 这座植物园可追溯到 18 世纪。

items.meaning: relating to plants or botany; the default adjective
items.meaningCN: 植物的；植物学的；默认形容词
items.example: The botanical description notes the leaf's hairs and veins.
items.exampleCN: 植物学描述记录了叶片的毛被与叶脉。

items.meaning: in botanical terms
items.meaningCN: 从植物学角度
items.example: Botanically, the tomato is a berry.
items.exampleCN: 从植物学上说，番茄是一种浆果。

items.structure: botan- + -ize (to act in a particular way)
items.meaning: to collect or study plants in the field
items.meaningCN: 在野外采集或研究植物
items.example: They botanized the coastal dunes at low tide.
items.exampleCN: 他们在退潮时考察了海岸沙丘的植物。

items.meaning: a person who studies how a culture uses plants
items.meaningCN: 研究某一文化如何使用植物的人
items.example: An ethnobotanist documented the village's medicinal plants.
items.exampleCN: 一位民族植物学家记录了该村的药用植物。

items.meaning: a person who studies fossil plants
items.meaningCN: 研究化石植物的人
items.example: The paleobotanist identified a fern from the Jurassic.
items.exampleCN: 这位古植物学家鉴定出一株侏罗纪蕨类。

items.meaning: the activity of collecting or studying plants in the field
items.meaningCN: 野外采集或研究植物的活动
items.example: A morning of botanizing produced forty pressed specimens.
items.exampleCN: 一个上午的植物考察采得四十份压制标本。

latinEntries.meaning: plant, grass, pasture, fodder
latinEntries.meaningCN: 植物；草；牧场；牧草

latinEntries.meaning: of herbs or plants
latinEntries.meaningCN: 草本的；植物的

latinEntries.meaning: relating to plants; the source of the English stem
latinEntries.meaningCN: 与植物有关的；英语词干的来源

latinEntries.meaning: agent suffix 'one who practises'; the ancestor of English -ist
latinEntries.meaningCN: 施动后缀“从事者”；英语 -ist 的前身

definition_zh: 突破；重大进展；突破性成果；（军事）突破防线
definition_en: a sudden important advance that gets past a barrier, especially in science, medicine, technology, or the military
core_image: 一堵墙上被撞开的第一道缺口，后面的人由此穿过去
scene: On the lab screen the long-unsolved structure finally resolved, and the team leader said, This is the breakthrough we needed.
sceneCN: 这里 breakthrough 是「重大突破、突破性进展」（第 2 个义项：科研上越过长期障碍）；句意：实验室屏幕上多年无解的结构终于显出清晰轮廓，团队负责人说，这就是他们需要的突破。场景要点：屏幕上的结构图、实验台、团队、记录板。

pos.zh: 突破；重大进展；突破性成果；军事突破

derivatives.zh: 爆发痛（慢性疼痛治疗中突然发作的剧痛）
突破性感染（接种或服药后仍发生的感染）
突破性技术（名词作定语）

senses.title: Military: a hole forced in a defensive line
senses.titleCN: 军事：在防线中强行打开缺口
senses.definition: a successful advance through an enemy's defensive line, opening a gap for the rest of the force
senses.definitionCN: 成功穿过敌方防线，为其余部队打开缺口
senses.example: The armoured division made a breakthrough at dawn and pushed into open ground.
senses.exampleCN: 装甲师在黎明时突破防线，向开阔地推进。
senses.why: Breakthrough began as a noun from the phrase break through: a line is broken and the force passes through the hole. The earliest recorded modern noun use is military, from the trench warfare of the late 1910s.
senses.whyCN: breakthrough 最初是短语 break through 名词化的结果：防线被打破，部队从缺口穿过去。最早有记录的现代名词用法是军事义，来自 1910 年代后期的堑壕战。

senses.title: Science and technology: an advance past a long barrier
senses.titleCN: 科研与技术：越过长期障碍的进展
senses.definition: a sudden, important advance that solves a problem or removes an obstacle that had blocked work for a long time
senses.definitionCN: 突然而重要的进展，解决了一个问题或清除了长期阻碍工作的障碍
senses.example: The team's breakthrough came when they could finally image the protein's active site.
senses.exampleCN: 当团队终于能成像该蛋白的活性位点时，他们的突破到来了。
senses.why: The military gap becomes an intellectual gap. Something long closed is suddenly open, and work that was stuck can move forward; this transfer is recorded from the 1930s, on the notion of a successful attack.
senses.whyCN: 军事上的缺口变成了知识上的缺口。长期封闭的东西突然打开，卡住的工作得以推进；这一转移自 1930 年代有记录，依托的是“进攻成功”的意象。

senses.title: Medicine: a treatment that changes the outcome
senses.titleCN: 医学：改变结局的治疗
senses.definition: a new drug, test, or procedure that greatly improves the treatment of a disease
senses.definitionCN: 极大改善某种疾病治疗的新药、检测或疗法
senses.example: The drug was hailed as a breakthrough for patients who had run out of options.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药被赞为那些已无其他选择的患者的突破。
senses.why: The barrier here is disease or a failed treatment, and the advance passes through it. Medical writing adopts the word because it captures both the obstacle and the sudden release, keeping the battlefield shape intact.
senses.whyCN: 这里的障碍是疾病或失效的疗法，而进展穿过了它。医学写作采用这个词，因为它同时抓住障碍与突然的解除，并保持战场的形状不变。

senses.title: Personal: breaking a deadlock or limit
senses.titleCN: 个人：打破僵局或极限
senses.definition: a moment when a person gets past a mental block, a deadlock, or a limit that had held them back
senses.definitionCN: 一个人越过心理障碍、僵局或长期限制自己的极限的时刻
senses.example: Learning to speak in public was a personal breakthrough for him.
senses.exampleCN: 学会公开演讲对他而言是一次个人突破。
senses.why: The wall is now inside the person: fear, habit, or a fixed limit. The same shape holds — a barrier is met and passed — which is why the word feels natural outside science and warfare.
senses.whyCN: 墙现在在人的内心：恐惧、习惯或固定极限。形状不变——遇到障碍并越过去——因此这个词用在科学与战争之外也很自然。

senses.title: Business and market: opening a closed door
senses.titleCN: 商业与市场：打开一扇关着的门
senses.definition: a product, deal, or strategy that lets a company enter a new market or reach a new level
senses.definitionCN: 让公司进入新市场或达到新水平的产品、交易或策略
senses.example: The low-cost model was the company's breakthrough into emerging markets.
senses.exampleCN: 低成本模式是这家公司进入新兴市场的突破。
senses.why: A closed market is treated as a wall, and a successful entry as the hole through it. Business English borrows the military image and keeps its force, so entering a market becomes a passage through a barrier.
senses.whyCN: 封闭的市场被当作一堵墙，成功进入就是墙上打开的洞。商业英语借用了军事意象并保留其力度，于是进入市场变成了穿过障碍。

senses.title: Attributive use: breakthrough drug, technology, year
senses.titleCN: 定语用法：突破性药物、技术、年份
senses.definition: used before a noun to mark the thing as the one that produced the advance, as in breakthrough technology
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，标记该事物就是产生突破的那一个，如 breakthrough technology
senses.example: The breakthrough technology cut the cost of sequencing by half.
senses.exampleCN: 这项突破性技术把测序成本降低了一半。
senses.why: The noun is placed before another noun without a suffix, a zero-derived modifier. It names not a general quality but the specific advance that opened the way, so the modifier keeps the concrete event.
senses.whyCN: 名词不加后缀直接放在另一个名词前，构成零派生修饰语。它命名的不是一般性质，而是打开道路的那次具体突破，因此修饰语保留具体事件。

senses.title: Usage boundary: breakthrough versus discovery
senses.titleCN: 用法边界：breakthrough 与 discovery
senses.definition: a discovery is something found; a breakthrough is a discovery or advance that passes a barrier and changes what can be done next
senses.definitionCN: discovery 是被发现的东西；breakthrough 是越过障碍、改变接下来能做之事的新发现或进展
senses.example: The discovery of the fossil was interesting, but the dating method was the breakthrough.
senses.exampleCN: 发现化石本身很有意思，但真正突破的是测年方法。
senses.why: Discovery names the find; breakthrough adds the wall and the passage. A discovery can be small and still be a discovery, but a breakthrough must change the situation, because the break is part of its meaning.
senses.whyCN: discovery 命名“找到的东西”；breakthrough 额外包含“墙”与“穿过”。发现可以很小仍是发现，而突破必须改变局面，因为“打破”是它意义的一部分。

senses.title: Usage boundary: breakthrough versus advance and progress
senses.titleCN: 用法边界：breakthrough 与 advance、progress
senses.definition: advance and progress can be gradual; breakthrough implies a sudden, decisive jump past an obstacle
senses.definitionCN: advance 与 progress 可以是渐进的；breakthrough 暗示突然而决定性地越过障碍
senses.example: Years of steady progress led to one breakthrough.
senses.exampleCN: 多年稳步进展最终带来一次突破。
senses.why: The compound contains break, a sudden verb, so it cannot describe slow improvement. This is why journalists reserve it for the moment the wall gives way, while progress can continue for years.
senses.whyCN: 这个词组含有 break 这个表示突然动作的动词，因此不能描述缓慢改善。这也是记者只把它留给墙崩塌那一刻的原因，而 progress 可以持续多年。

senses.title: Specialized: breakthrough infection and breakthrough pain
senses.titleCN: 专业用法：突破性感染与爆发痛
senses.definition: in medical compounds, breakthrough describes something that gets past a defence, such as a vaccine or a painkiller
senses.definitionCN: 在医学复合词中，breakthrough 描述越过某种防御的东西，如疫苗或止痛药
senses.example: A breakthrough infection occurred in a few vaccinated patients.
senses.exampleCN: 少数已接种患者发生了突破性感染。
senses.why: These compounds use the oldest literal sense: the pathogen or the pain breaks through the defence that was supposed to hold it. The barrier is medical, but the image is unchanged, so the noun keeps its military geometry.
senses.whyCN: 这些复合词用的是最古老的字面义：病原体或疼痛突破了本应拦住它的防线。障碍是医学的，但意象没有变，因此名词保留了军事几何。

intro.en: Breakthrough is not a Latin derivative. It is the English phrase break through turned into a noun: two native Old English words, a verb of breaking and a word of passing through, welded into one compound. Etymonline dates the noun to 1918 in a military sense; the exact first occurrence is uncertain.
intro.cn: breakthrough 不是拉丁派生词。它是英语短语 break through 名词化的结果：两个本土古英语词——表示“打破”的动词与表示“穿过”的词——焊合为一个复合词。etymonline 把名词的军事义定在 1918 年；确切的最早出现存疑。

items.en: Break goes back to Old English brecan 'to divide solid matter violently, to burst, to break', from Proto-Germanic *brekanan and PIE root *bhreg- 'to break'. Through goes back to Old English þurh, from Proto-Germanic *thurx and PIE *tere- 'to cross over, pass through, overcome'. Neither word is Latin or Greek.
items.cn: break 上溯古英语 brecan“猛烈分开固体、爆裂、打破”，来自原始日耳曼语 *brekanan 与原始印欧语词根 *bhreg-“打破”。through 上溯古英语 þurh，来自原始日耳曼语 *thurx 与原始印欧语 *tere-“越过、穿过、克服”。两者都不是拉丁语或希腊语。

items.en: The verbal phrase break through is attested from about 1400 in the sense 'overcome or penetrate a barrier'. The verb keeps its sudden force, and the later noun inherits that suddenness.
items.cn: 短语动词 break through 约自 1400 年起有记录，意为“克服或穿透障碍”。动词保留突然的力度，后来的名词继承了这种突然性。

items.en: Etymonline records the noun breakthrough (also written break-through) from 1918, meaning a 'significant or sudden advance', in a military sense. The date fits the trench warfare of the First World War, but the exact first written occurrence is uncertain and may be slightly earlier.
items.cn: etymonline 记录名词 breakthrough（也写作 break-through）自 1918 年起表示军事上的“重大或突然的推进”。这个年代与第一次世界大战的堑壕战相符，但确切的最早书面出现存疑，可能略早。

items.en: The meaning 'abrupt solution or progress' is recorded from the 1930s, on the notion of a successful attack. The wall becomes a research problem, a disease, or a personal limit, and the passage through it becomes a decisive advance.
items.cn: “突然的解决或进展”义自 1930 年代有记录，依托的是“进攻成功”的意象。墙变成研究难题、疾病或个人极限，而穿过墙的通道变成决定性的进展。

items.en: Medicine applied the word to drugs and procedures that change outcomes, and business to products that open new markets. The attributive use, as in breakthrough technology, is a zero-derived modifier with no suffix.
items.cn: 医学把这个词用于改变结局的药物与疗法，商业把它用于打开新市场的产品。breakthrough technology 这类定语用法是零派生修饰语，不加后缀。

items.en: Journalism has inflated the word, so it is often used for any good news. Technical compounds such as breakthrough infection and breakthrough pain keep the strict literal sense of something passing a defence. The noun remains a native English compound, not a borrowed root.
items.cn: 新闻写作把这个词用滥了，常用来指任何好消息。breakthrough infection、breakthrough pain 等技术复合词则保留“某物越过防御”的严格字面义。这个名词始终是本土英语复合词，而不是借来的词根。

note.en: The first group is the same break + particle pattern with different particles and different results; the second separates a breakthrough from a find, a gradual gain, a jump, and a new method.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个 break + 小品词的构词模式，但小品词与结果不同；第二组把突破与发现、渐进增益、跃升及新方法区分开。

entries.definition: The end of a relationship or the splitting of a group. Up here means apart, so the compound is about separation, not passage.
entries.definitionCN: 关系结束或团体分裂。这里的 up 表示“分开”，因此复合词说的是分离，而不是穿过。

entries.definition: An escape from a place or a sudden success that escapes a limited category. Out stresses leaving a container, not crossing a line.
entries.definitionCN: 从某处逃出，或突然脱离某一局限类别的成功。out 强调离开容器，而不是越过一条线。

entries.definition: A failure of a machine, system, or person, or an analysis into parts. Down marks collapse or division, the opposite direction from through.
entries.definitionCN: 机器、系统或人的崩溃，或分解为部分。down 标记崩塌或分解，与 through 的方向相反。

entries.definition: A separation or departure from a group, as in a breakaway faction. Away marks distance from the source, not a passage to the other side.
entries.definitionCN: 从群体中分离或脱离，如 breakaway faction。away 标记远离源头，而不是穿到另一边。

entries.definition: The act of finding something that was already there but unknown. It names the find, while breakthrough names the barrier passed.
entries.definitionCN: 发现原本存在却未知之物的行为。它命名“找到”，而 breakthrough 命名“越过的障碍”。

entries.definition: A forward movement or improvement, often gradual. It lacks the sudden break that breakthrough requires.
entries.definitionCN: 向前的移动或改善，常为渐进。它没有 breakthrough 所要求的突然断裂。

entries.definition: A very large and sudden change, as in a leap in technology. It stresses distance jumped rather than a wall broken.
entries.definitionCN: 巨大而突然的变化，如技术上的 leap。它强调跳过的距离，而不是打破一堵墙。

entries.definition: A new idea, method, or product actually put into use. It stresses novelty and application, not the overcoming of an obstacle.
entries.definitionCN: 被实际采用的新想法、方法或产品。它强调新颖与应用，而不是克服障碍。

normalIntro.en: Real associations: break + through, the military gap, and real medical compounds such as breakthrough infection.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联想：break + through 的构词、军事缺口，以及 breakthrough infection 等真实医学复合词。

normal.en: break + through: first a wall is broken, then people pass through the hole. The noun keeps both halves of that action.
normal.cn: break + through：先打破一堵墙，再有人从洞里穿过去。名词同时保留这一动作的两半。

normal.en: The word grew in the trenches: a breakthrough was a hole in the enemy line, not a clever idea.
normal.cn: 这个词在堑壕里长大：breakthrough 是敌军防线上的一个缺口，而不是一个聪明点子。

normal.en: When a lab says breakthrough, it borrows the trench image: the problem was a wall, and now there is a way through.
normal.cn: 实验室说 breakthrough 时借用了堑壕的意象：问题是一堵墙，现在有路可过了。

normal.en: breakthrough technology is the technology that made the hole; the modifier names the specific advance, not a general quality.
normal.cn: breakthrough technology 就是打出缺口的那个技术；修饰语命名的是具体那次突破，不是一般性质。

normal.en: breakthrough infection is literal: the germ breaks through the vaccine's defence. The old image survives in the clinic.
normal.cn: breakthrough infection 是字面义：病原体突破了疫苗的防线。旧意象在诊室里活了下来。

abstract.en: A wall is not removed; a hole is made. A breakthrough does not erase the obstacle, it creates a passage through it.
abstract.cn: 墙没有被移走，只是被打开一个洞。突破并不消除障碍，而是在障碍上开出一条通路。

abstract.en: Before the break, every step is blocked; after it, the same energy moves freely. The word marks the single instant when the direction changes.
abstract.cn: 在断裂之前，每一步都被挡住；之后，同样的力气自由流动。这个词标记方向改变的那一瞬。

abstract.en: A breakthrough is a door that was not there yesterday: the room behind it was always there, but no one could enter.
abstract.cn: 突破是昨天还不存在的一扇门：门后的房间一直都在，只是没人进得去。

examples.en: The vaccine was the first real breakthrough in the fight against the disease.
examples.cn: 这种疫苗是对抗该疾病的第一项真正突破。

examples.en: Years of failed experiments made the final breakthrough feel sudden.
examples.cn: 多年失败的实验让最后的突破显得很突然。

examples.en: The company's breakthrough into the Japanese market came through a local partner.
examples.cn: 这家公司借本地伙伴实现了进入日本市场的突破。

dict_mnemonic.text: “布雷克思如”——先把墙 break（打破），再 through（穿过去）→ breakthrough 突破

root: 英语本土短语 break through 的名词化；break 来自古英语 brecan“打破”，through 来自古英语 þurh“穿过”。不是拉丁派生，而是“动词 + 方位小品词”的复合。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of breakthrough share one shape: a barrier is broken and something passes through it. The barrier may be a trench line, a research problem, a disease, a personal limit, a closed market, or a vaccine defence.
sensesIntro.cn: breakthrough 的九个义项形状相同：障碍被打破，某物穿过去。障碍可以是战壕防线、研究难题、疾病、个人极限、封闭市场，或疫苗防线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wall is broken at one point, and what was blocked can now pass through.
core.cn: 核心意象：墙在某一点被打破，原本被挡住的东西现在可以通过。

branches.en: BATTLE: the literal gap in a defensive line, the historical seed of the word.
branches.cn: 战场：防线上字面的缺口，这个词的历史种子。

branches.en: KNOWLEDGE AND CURE: a research problem or a disease becomes the wall that is passed.
branches.cn: 知识与治疗：研究难题或疾病变成被越过的墙。

branches.en: SELF: the barrier moves inside a person, as fear or a fixed limit.
branches.cn: 自我：障碍移到人的内心，成为恐惧或固定极限。

branches.en: MARKET AND MODIFIER: a closed market is a wall, and the breakthrough product is the thing that made the hole.
branches.cn: 市场与定语：封闭市场是一堵墙，而突破性产品就是打出缺口的那个东西。

branches.en: BOUNDARIES: discovery names the find, advance names a gradual step, and medical compounds keep the literal defence.
branches.cn: 边界：discovery 命名发现，advance 命名渐进一步，医学复合词则保留字面的防御义。

intro.en: Breakthrough has no affixes at all. It is a compound of break and through, both native English words; the noun is a zero-derivation from the phrasal verb, with no suffix added.
intro.cn: breakthrough 没有任何词缀。它是 break 与 through 两个本土英语词的复合；名词由短语动词零派生而来，没有添加后缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin layer here. The word is native English, so the Latin entries below are not ancestors but Latin-derived counterparts that English already had for a forward step or a find.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语层次。这个词是本土英语，因此下面的拉丁条目不是祖先，而是英语中原本就有的、表示“向前一步”或“发现”的拉丁来源对应词。

items.structure: break (to break) + through (from one side to the other)
items.meaning: to force a way through an obstacle; the source phrase, later compressed into a noun
items.meaningCN: 强行穿过障碍；这是源短语，后来压缩成名词
items.example: The water broke through the dam at midnight.
items.exampleCN: 水在午夜冲破了堤坝。

items.meaning: the gap and the passage through it; no suffix marks the change of word class
items.meaningCN: 缺口以及穿过缺口的通道；词性变化不靠后缀标记
items.example: The breakthrough came after ten years of work.
items.exampleCN: 这项突破在十年工作之后到来。

items.meaning: sudden pain that breaks through painkillers; the old literal sense applied to medicine
items.meaningCN: 突破止痛药控制的突发疼痛；旧字面义用于医学
items.example: She described the breakthrough pain as sharp and brief.
items.exampleCN: 她描述那种爆发痛尖锐而短暂。

items.meaning: an infection that gets past a vaccine or drug defence
items.meaningCN: 越过疫苗或药物防线的感染
items.example: Breakthrough infections are expected when a virus changes.
items.exampleCN: 病毒变异时，出现突破性感染是意料之中的。

items.meaning: the technology that produced the decisive advance
items.meaningCN: 产生决定性进展的技术
items.example: The breakthrough technology halved the cost of sequencing.
items.exampleCN: 这项突破性技术把测序成本降低了一半。

items.meaning: an escape or a sudden success beyond a former limit
items.meaningCN: 逃脱；突破原有局限的突然成功
items.example: The band had a breakout year after the album.
items.exampleCN: 这张专辑之后，乐队迎来了突破性的一年。

items.meaning: a collapse or a division into parts
items.meaningCN: 崩溃；分解为部分
items.example: The breakdown of the talks surprised both sides.
items.exampleCN: 谈判破裂让双方都感到意外。

items.meaning: the ending of a relationship or the splitting of a group
items.meaningCN: 关系结束；团体分裂
items.example: The breakup of the partnership left both firms weaker.
items.exampleCN: 合作关系解体后，两家公司都变弱了。

items.meaning: a separation or departure from a larger group
items.meaningCN: 从较大群体中分离或脱离
items.example: A breakaway faction formed a new party.
items.exampleCN: 一个脱离出来的派系组成了新政党。

latinEntries.meaning: a forward step; a Latin-derived counterpart, not the source of breakthrough
latinEntries.meaningCN: 前进一步；拉丁来源的对应词，并非 breakthrough 的来源

latinEntries.structure: Old French avancer, ultimately from Latin abante 'from before'
latinEntries.meaning: to move forward; again a counterpart rather than an ancestor
latinEntries.meaningCN: 向前移动；同样是对应词而非祖先

latinEntries.meaning: the introduction of something new; it stresses novelty, not a broken barrier
latinEntries.meaningCN: 引入新事物；强调新颖，而不是被打破的障碍

latinEntries.meaning: an uncovering, hence a find; it names the thing found, not the passage through a wall
latinEntries.meaningCN: 揭开覆盖，故为发现；它命名被找到之物，而不是穿墙而过

definition_zh: 加宽；使变宽；扩大；拓宽（范围、视野、兴趣等）
definition_en: to make something wider, or to increase its range, scope, variety, or inclusiveness
core_image: 把一条窄路的两侧各向外推一寸，路面随之变宽
scene: The teacher broadened the course from European history alone to include Asia and Africa, and the students' view opened with it.
sceneCN: 这里 broaden 是「拓宽、扩大」（第 2 个义项：扩大范围）；句意：老师把课程范围从只讲欧洲史拓宽到包含亚洲与非洲，学生的视野也随之打开。场景要点：课程大纲、世界地图、欧洲与亚非区域标注、学生笔记。

senses.title: Make physically wider
senses.titleCN: 把实物加宽
senses.definition: to make a road, river, opening, or surface wider from side to side
senses.definitionCN: 把道路、河流、开口或表面从一侧到另一侧加宽
senses.example: The council broadened the path so that two bicycles could pass.
senses.exampleCN: 市政会把小路加宽，好让两辆自行车并行。
senses.why: Broaden is broad plus the verb suffix -en, the same pattern as widen and deepen. The suffix here has a causative force: an agent makes the object broad, so the first sense is purely physical, with the distance between two edges increasing.
senses.whyCN: broaden 是 broad 加动词后缀 -en，与 widen、deepen 同一模式。这里的后缀带使役意味：施动者使宾语变宽，因此第一个义项纯粹是物理的，两条边之间的距离变大。

senses.title: Widen the range or scope
senses.titleCN: 扩大范围或覆盖面
senses.definition: to increase the range of a study, inquiry, rule, or discussion so that it covers more
senses.definitionCN: 扩大研究、调查、规则或讨论的范围，使其覆盖更多内容
senses.example: The committee broadened the inquiry to include earlier failures.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会扩大了调查范围，把更早的失败也纳入其中。
senses.why: The physical edges become the boundaries of a subject. To broaden an inquiry is to move both limits outward, so that more cases fall inside; the same causative suffix now applies to an abstract object.
senses.whyCN: 物理的边变成主题的边界。扩大调查就是把两端的界限向外移，让更多案例落进范围内；同一个使役后缀现在作用于抽象宾语。

senses.title: Broaden the mind: knowledge and experience
senses.titleCN: 开阔心智：知识与经验
senses.definition: to make a person's knowledge, interests, or experience more varied and less narrow
senses.definitionCN: 使一个人的知识、兴趣或经验更多样、更不狭窄
senses.example: A year abroad broadened her understanding of her own country.
senses.exampleCN: 在国外的一年拓宽了她对自己国家的理解。
senses.why: A narrow mind is imagined as a narrow space. Travel and study push the walls outward, which is why the fixed phrase is broaden someone's horizons: the horizon is the far edge of what can be seen.
senses.whyCN: 狭窄的心智被想象成一个狭窄的空间。旅行与学习把墙向外推，因此固定说法是 broaden someone's horizons：地平线就是所能看见的远边界。

senses.title: Widen the audience or appeal
senses.titleCN: 扩大受众或吸引力
senses.definition: to make something attractive or understandable to more people, not only to a small group
senses.definitionCN: 使某物对更多人具有吸引力或可理解，而不只面向小圈子
senses.example: The museum broadened its appeal by adding evening openings.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆增加夜间开放，扩大了它的吸引力。
senses.why: The audience is the area covered. Broadening it means reaching groups that were outside the old edge, without changing the core of what is offered, so the edge metaphor extends from space to social reach.
senses.whyCN: 受众就是被覆盖的面积。扩大它就是触及旧边界之外的群体，而不改变所提供的核心内容，因此边界隐喻从空间延伸到社会触达。

senses.title: Make more inclusive
senses.titleCN: 使更具包容性
senses.definition: to increase who is included, admitted, or represented in an activity or institution
senses.definitionCN: 增加某项活动或机构所包含、接纳或代表的人群
senses.example: The programme was broadened to include students from rural schools.
senses.exampleCN: 该项目扩大到纳入乡村学校的学生。
senses.why: This is the scope sense applied to people. The boundary of the group moves outward, so broadening becomes a word for inclusion rather than for width, and the abstract sense gains a social value.
senses.whyCN: 这是范围义用在人身上。群体的边界向外移，于是 broaden 从“宽度”变成了“包容”，抽象义由此带上社会价值。

senses.title: Phrasal: broaden out into a wider form
senses.titleCN: 短语：broaden out 展开变宽
senses.definition: of a river, road, or shape, to become wider as it continues, often opening into a larger area
senses.definitionCN: 指河流、道路或形状在延伸中变宽，常展开成更大的区域
senses.example: Below the bridge, the river broadens out into a shallow lake.
senses.exampleCN: 桥下游，河流展开成一片浅湖。
senses.why: Out adds the idea of spreading open. The verb is intransitive here: nothing is being widened by an outside hand; the thing itself opens. This shows the inchoative side of -en, 'become broad' rather than 'make broad'.
senses.whyCN: out 添加“展开”的意思。这里动词是不及物的：没有外来的手把它加宽，而是事物自身展开。这体现了 -en 的起始义，即“变得宽”，而不是“使宽”。

senses.title: Usage boundary: broaden versus widen
senses.titleCN: 用法边界：broaden 与 widen
senses.definition: widen is the usual verb for physical width; broaden is preferred for scope, knowledge, appeal, and inclusion
senses.definitionCN: widen 是物理宽度的常用动词；broaden 更常用于范围、知识、吸引力与包容性
senses.example: They widened the doorway, but broadened the discussion.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把门洞加宽，却把讨论拓宽了。
senses.why: Both mean 'make wide', but broad has long been the adjective for abstract extent, as in a broad view. That abstract life carried over to broaden and left widen with the concrete job.
senses.whyCN: 两者都表示“使宽”，但 broad 长期是表示抽象广度的形容词，如 a broad view。这种抽象生命延续到 broaden，把具体工作留给了 widen。

senses.title: Usage boundary: broaden versus expand and extend
senses.titleCN: 用法边界：broaden 与 expand、extend
senses.definition: expand stresses growth in size or volume in all directions; extend stresses length or duration; broaden stresses the widening of a range
senses.definitionCN: expand 强调体积或规模向各方向增长；extend 强调长度或时间的延伸；broaden 强调范围的加宽
senses.example: The firm expanded abroad, extended its contract, and broadened its product range.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司向海外扩张，延长了合同，并拓宽了产品范围。
senses.why: Each verb keeps its own spatial image: a balloon expands, a line extends, and a range is broadened by pushing its side limits outward. The suffixes differ, so the verbs are not interchangeable.
senses.whyCN: 每个动词保留自己的空间意象：气球膨胀（expand），线延长（extend），而范围是靠把两侧界限外推来拓宽（broaden）。后缀不同，因此这些动词不能互换。

senses.title: Grammar boundary: transitive and intransitive
senses.titleCN: 语法边界：及物与不及物
senses.definition: broaden takes an object when someone widens something, and stands alone when something becomes wider by itself
senses.definitionCN: 有人把某物加宽时 broaden 带宾语；某物自行变宽时则单独使用
senses.example: They broadened the road; farther on, the road broadens.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把路加宽了；再往前，路自己变宽了。
senses.why: The -en suffix makes both readings possible: it can mean 'make wide' with an object, or 'become wide' without one. The context decides whether an agent is present.
senses.whyCN: -en 后缀让两种读法都成立：带宾语时表示“使宽”，不带宾语时表示“变宽”。语境决定是否存在施动者。

intro.en: Broaden is broad plus the native verb suffix -en, the same pattern that gives widen, deepen, and strengthen. Broad is an Old English adjective; the suffix is Germanic; the deeper prehistoric root of broad is not known with certainty. The earliest recorded dates are 1726 for the transitive and 1727 for the intransitive.
intro.cn: broaden 是 broad 加本土动词后缀 -en，与 widen、deepen、strengthen 同一模式。broad 是古英语形容词，后缀属日耳曼语；broad 更深的史前词源并不确定。最早记录年代为及物用法 1726 年、不及物用法 1727 年。

items.en: Old English brād meant 'wide, not narrow', and also 'flat, open, extended'. It covered physical width and open space from the start; the senses of daylight and of speech or accent developed later, in the late 14th and mid-15th centuries.
items.cn: 古英语 brād 意为“宽的、不窄的”，也表示“平坦的、敞开的、延展的”。它从一开始就覆盖物理宽度与开阔空间；白昼义与口音义则较晚，分别见于 14 世纪晚期与 15 世纪中期。

items.en: The adjective goes back to Proto-Germanic *braidi-, the source of Old Frisian bred, Old Norse breiðr, Dutch breed, German breit, and Gothic brouþs. Etymonline says its origin is unknown and it is not found outside Germanic; it also notes no clear distinction in sense from wide.
items.cn: 这个形容词上溯原始日耳曼语 *braidi-，也是古弗里斯语 bred、古诺斯语 breiðr、荷兰语 breed、德语 breit、哥特语 brouþs 的来源。etymonline 称其来源不明，且不见于日耳曼语族之外；它还指出 broad 与 wide 在意义上没有清晰区分。

items.en: -en is a native verb-forming suffix from Old English -nian, from Proto-Germanic *-inojan and a PIE adjectival suffix *-no-. It makes verbs from adjectives or nouns, usually with the sense 'make or become', as in darken, weaken, widen, and deepen. It was most active in Middle and early modern English.
items.cn: -en 是本土动词构词后缀，来自古英语 -nian，上溯原始日耳曼语 *-inojan 与原始印欧语形容词后缀 *-no-。它把形容词或名词变成动词，通常表示“使……或变得……”，如 darken、weaken、widen、deepen。它在古英语中较沉寂，在中古英语与早期现代英语中最活跃。

items.en: Etymonline dates broaden to 1726 for 'make broad' and 1727 for 'grow broad'. It says the word seems no older than this and was cited by Johnson in one of James Thomson's Seasons poems; broadened is also first found in the same poet. These are earliest recorded uses, not necessarily the coinage date.
items.cn: etymonline 把 broaden 的“使宽”义定在 1726 年，“变宽”义定在 1727 年。它称这个词似乎不会更早，约翰逊曾在詹姆斯·汤姆森的《四季》诗作中引用过；broadened 也最早见于同一位诗人。这些是最早记录用法，不一定是造词年代。

items.en: In the 19th century the verb spread from roads and rivers to scope, knowledge, sympathy, and audience, giving phrases such as broaden the mind and broaden one's horizons. The exact dates of these figurative extensions are not recorded, so the century is only an approximate frame.
items.cn: 19 世纪，这个动词从道路、河流扩展到范围、知识、同情心与受众，产生 broaden the mind、broaden one's horizons 等短语。这些比喻扩展的确切年代未见记录，因此该世纪只是大致框架。

items.en: Modern institutional English uses broaden for access, participation, appeal, and debate. The physical image remains underneath: two side limits are pushed outward. The verb keeps both the causative 'make broad' and the inchoative 'become broad'.
items.cn: 现代机构英语用 broaden 谈获取机会、参与、吸引力与讨论。底下的物理意象仍在：两条侧边界限被向外推。这个动词同时保留使役的“使宽”与起始的“变宽”。

note.en: The first group shares the broad root in adjective, adverb, and noun form; the second separates widening by range, by volume, by length, and by overall size.
note.cn: 第一组共享 broad 词根，分别为形容词、副词与名词形式；第二组按范围、体积、长度与整体规模区分“加宽”。

entries.definition: Wide, or large in range. It is the base adjective; broaden is the action of making something broad or becoming broad.
entries.definitionCN: 宽的，或范围广的。它是基础形容词；broaden 是使之变宽或变宽的动作。

entries.definition: In general terms, or over a wide range. It describes how something is meant, while broaden describes a change.
entries.definitionCN: 大体上，或广泛地。它描述某话是在什么意义上说的，而 broaden 描述变化。

entries.definition: The measurable width of something, or the range of a person's knowledge. It is the noun of broad, with a vowel change and the suffix -th.
entries.definitionCN: 可测量的宽度，或一个人知识的广度。它是 broad 的名词，伴随元音变化与后缀 -th。

entries.definition: The quality of being broad. It is the regular noun from the adjective, while breadth is the older irregular noun.
entries.definitionCN: 宽的性质。它是由形容词规则构成的名词，而 breadth 是更古老的不规则名词。

entries.definition: To make or become wider, especially in physical space. It is the default verb for roads, gaps, and openings.
entries.definitionCN: 使变宽，尤指物理空间。它是道路、缺口与开口的默认动词。

entries.definition: To grow larger in size, volume, or number. It suggests growth in all directions, like a balloon, not the pushing of two edges.
entries.definitionCN: 在尺寸、体积或数量上变大。它暗示像气球一样向各方向增长，而不是推两条边。

entries.definition: To make something longer in space or time. It stretches a line, while broaden pushes a range sideways.
entries.definitionCN: 在空间或时间上使更长。它拉长一条线，而 broaden 把范围向两侧推。

entries.definition: To make something larger overall, as in enlarge a photograph. It stresses total size rather than the width of a range.
entries.definitionCN: 使整体变大，如放大照片。它强调总体尺寸，而不是范围的宽度。

normalIntro.en: Real word parts: broad + -en, the same native pattern as widen, deepen, and strengthen; broad itself goes back to Old English brād.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词：broad + -en，与 widen、deepen、strengthen 同一本土模式；broad 本身上溯古英语 brād。

normal.en: broad + -en = broaden, exactly like wide + -en = widen and deep + -en = deepen. The suffix means 'make or become'.
normal.cn: broad + -en = broaden，正如 wide + -en = widen、deep + -en = deepen。后缀意为“使……或变得……”。

normal.en: To broaden the scope is to push both side limits of an inquiry outward, so that more cases fit inside.
normal.cn: 扩大范围（broaden the scope）就是把调查的两侧界限向外推，让更多案例装进去。

normal.en: Horizons are the far edge of what you can see; broadening them moves that edge farther away.
normal.cn: horizons 是你能看见的远边界；把它拓宽，就是把那条边界推得更远。

normal.en: A river broadens out where it opens into a lake: the verb can be intransitive, with no one doing the widening.
normal.cn: 河流展开成湖时会 broaden out：这个动词可以不及物，并没有谁在加宽它。

normal.en: Broaden is the action, broad is the quality, broadly is the viewpoint, and breadth is the measured result: four jobs from one root.
normal.cn: broaden 是动作，broad 是性质，broadly 是视角，breadth 是量出的结果：同一个词根承担四种职能。

abstract.en: A narrow beam turned into a floodlight: the same light, spread over more area, so more of the room is lit.
abstract.cn: 一束窄光变成泛光灯：同样的光铺在更大面积上，于是房间被照亮的范围更大。

abstract.en: A picture frame stretched at both ends: the scene inside does not change, but more of the world now fits in the frame.
abstract.cn: 一个相框两端被拉宽：框里的景象没有变，但能装进框里的世界更多了。

abstract.en: A road given shoulders: the destination stays the same, yet the passage can carry more traffic without becoming a different road.
abstract.cn: 一条路加上了路肩：目的地不变，但这条通道能承载更多往来，而不会变成另一条路。

examples.en: Reading foreign novels broadened her sense of what a family can be.
examples.cn: 读外国小说拓宽了她对“家庭可以是什么”的理解。

examples.en: The new policy broadens access to free screening.
examples.cn: 新政策扩大了免费筛查的获取机会。

examples.en: The valley broadens out into farmland beyond the last bridge.
examples.cn: 过了最后一座桥，山谷展开成农田。

dict_mnemonic.text: “布若等”——把一块布（broad）向两边再拉宽一点 → broaden 加宽、扩大

root: broad（古英语 brād“宽的”，原始日耳曼语 *braidi-）+ -en（本土动词后缀，古英语 -nian，原始日耳曼语 *-inojan，表示“使……、变得……”）；更深的原始印欧语来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of broaden share one motion: push two limits outward. The limits may belong to a road, an inquiry, a mind, an audience, a group, or a river mouth.
sensesIntro.cn: broaden 的九个义项是一个动作：把两条界限向外推。这两条界限可以属于道路、调查、心智、受众、群体或河口。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two side limits are pushed outward, so the space between them becomes larger.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条侧边界限被向外推，于是它们之间的空间变大。

branches.en: PHYSICAL: a road or opening gains width, the literal starting point of the verb.
branches.cn: 物理：道路或开口增加宽度，这是动词的字面起点。

branches.en: SCOPE: the edges become the limits of a study or rule, and both are moved outward.
branches.cn: 范围：边变成研究或规则的界限，两端都被向外移。

branches.en: MIND: the narrow space is inside a person, and experience pushes its walls back.
branches.cn: 心智：狭窄空间在人的内部，经验把它的墙往后推。

branches.en: PEOPLE: an audience or a group is the covered area, so widening becomes inclusion.
branches.cn: 人群：受众或群体就是被覆盖的面积，因此加宽变成包容。

branches.en: FORM AND BOUNDARIES: broaden out opens by itself, widen takes physical width, expand grows in volume, and the verb can be transitive or not.
branches.cn: 形态与边界：broaden out 自行展开，widen 承担物理宽度，expand 是体积增长，而动词可及物也可不及物。

intro.en: Broaden is a clean two-part word: the adjective broad plus the native verb suffix -en. There is no prefix, and the suffix is the same one seen in widen, deepen, and strengthen.
intro.cn: broaden 是干净的两段式：形容词 broad 加本土动词后缀 -en。它没有前缀，这个后缀也见于 widen、deepen、strengthen。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestry in broaden. Its suffix is native Old English, and the Latin-derived verbs below (extend, expand, enlarge, amplify) are separate words that English borrowed for overlapping ideas, not relatives of broaden.
latinIntro.cn: broaden 没有拉丁语血统。它的后缀是本土古英语；下面的 extend、expand、enlarge、amplify 都是英语为相近概念另借来的拉丁词，不是 broaden 的亲属。

items.meaning: to make or become broad; the suffix changes an adjective of width into a verb of widening
items.meaningCN: 使变宽或变宽；后缀把表宽度的形容词变成表加宽的动词
items.example: They broadened the track to take larger vehicles.
items.exampleCN: 他们把车道加宽，以容纳更大的车辆。

items.meaning: wide in space or large in range; the base that supplies all the meaning of width
items.meaningCN: 空间上宽的，或范围广的；提供全部“宽度”语义的基础词
items.example: A broad street runs through the old town.
items.exampleCN: 一条宽阔的街道穿过老城。

items.meaning: in general terms or over a wide range; the adjective becomes an adverb of manner or viewpoint
items.meaningCN: 大体上，或广泛地；形容词变成表方式或视角的副词
items.example: Broadly speaking, the two accounts agree.
items.exampleCN: 大体而言，两种说法是一致的。

items.structure: broad + -th (noun of a quality), with a vowel change
items.meaning: width, or range of knowledge; the suffix turns the adjective into the measurable quality itself
items.meaningCN: 宽度，或知识广度；后缀把形容词变成可测量的性质本身
items.example: The breadth of her reading impressed the panel.
items.exampleCN: 她阅读的广度让评审小组印象深刻。

items.meaning: the quality of being broad; the regular alternative to breadth
items.meaningCN: 宽的性质；breadth 的规则替代形式
items.example: The broadness of the valley surprised the walkers.
items.exampleCN: 山谷的宽阔让步行者感到惊讶。

items.meaning: to make or become wide; the same suffix applied to a near-synonym of broad
items.meaningCN: 使变宽或变宽；同一后缀加在 broad 的近义词上
items.example: They widened the bridge to ease traffic.
items.exampleCN: 他们把桥加宽以缓解交通。

items.meaning: to make or become deep; another verb of the same native pattern
items.meaningCN: 使变深或变深；同一本土模式的另一个动词
items.example: The channel was deepened to admit larger ships.
items.exampleCN: 航道被加深，以容纳更大的船只。

items.meaning: to make or become strong; the suffix works on a noun here
items.meaningCN: 使变强或变强；这里后缀加在名词上
items.example: The new evidence strengthened their case.
items.exampleCN: 新证据加强了他们的论证。

items.structure: broad + -minded (having a mind of that kind)
items.meaning: willing to accept views different from one's own; the abstract sense of broad in a compound
items.meaningCN: 愿意接受不同观点的；broad 的抽象义用于复合词
items.example: Her broad-minded approach won over the committee.
items.exampleCN: 她开明的态度赢得了委员会的支持。

latinEntries.meaning: to stretch out or lengthen; a Latin-derived counterpart stressing length, not width
latinEntries.meaningCN: 向外伸展或延长；拉丁来源的对应词，强调长度而非宽度

latinEntries.meaning: to spread out and grow larger; a counterpart stressing volume in all directions
latinEntries.meaningCN: 铺开并变大；对应词，强调各方向的体积增长

latinEntries.structure: en- (make) + large, from Latin largus 'abundant, generous'
latinEntries.meaning: to make larger overall; a counterpart stressing total size
latinEntries.meaningCN: 使整体变大；对应词，强调总体尺寸

latinEntries.meaning: to make larger, stronger, or fuller; a counterpart often used for sound and signals
latinEntries.meaningCN: 使更大、更强或更充分；对应词，常用于声音与信号

definition_zh: 更宽的；更广阔的；更概括的；更广泛的（broad 的比较级）
definition_en: the comparative of broad: wider in physical extent, or larger in range, generality, or inclusiveness
core_image: 两只手把同一块布向两边再拉开一截，比原来更宽
scene: At the review, the editor asked for a broader view that placed the single case inside the whole industry.
sceneCN: 这里 broader 是「更广阔的、更概括的」（第 3 个义项：更概括而非局限于一点）；句意：评审会上，编辑要求作者给出更广阔的视角，不只盯一个案例，而要放进整个行业的背景。场景要点：评审桌、论文稿、行业图表、放大的取景框。

pos.zh: 更宽的；更广阔的；更概括的（broad 的比较级）

senses.title: Wider in physical extent
senses.titleCN: 物理上更宽
senses.definition: comparative of broad: having a greater distance from side to side than something else
senses.definitionCN: broad 的比较级：从一侧到另一侧的距离比另一物更大
senses.example: The new bridge is broader than the old one by two lanes.
senses.exampleCN: 新桥比旧桥宽出两条车道。
senses.why: Broader is not a separate word with its own meaning; it is broad plus the comparative suffix -er. The first sense simply compares two physical widths, so the base adjective supplies all the content and -er supplies the comparison.
senses.whyCN: broader 不是有独立词义的词，而是 broad 加比较级后缀 -er。第一个义项只是比较两个物理宽度，因此基础形容词提供全部内容，-er 提供比较。

senses.title: Larger in range or scope
senses.titleCN: 范围更大
senses.definition: covering a larger range of things, cases, or activities than another range
senses.definitionCN: 比另一范围覆盖更多事物、案例或活动
senses.example: The second study uses a broader range of sources.
senses.exampleCN: 第二项研究使用了范围更广的资料。
senses.why: The comparison moves from space to scope: one range extends farther at both ends than another. The comparative suffix does the comparing, and broad supplies the range image, so no new root is created.
senses.whyCN: 比较从空间转到范围：一个范围的两端都比另一个伸得更远。比较级后缀负责比较，broad 提供范围的意象，因此没有产生新词根。

senses.title: More general, less specific
senses.titleCN: 更概括、更不具体
senses.definition: belonging to a higher or more general category, as in the broader sense of a word
senses.definitionCN: 属于更高或更概括的类别，如某词的 broader sense
senses.example: In the broader sense, 'tool' includes software as well as hammers.
senses.exampleCN: 在更宽泛的意义上，tool 既包括锤子，也包括软件。
senses.why: A category is imagined as an area: the broader category covers the narrower one. Saying 'in the broader sense' moves up one level of generality, losing detail as it gains coverage; the comparative is doing the movement.
senses.whyCN: 类别被想象成一块面积：更宽的类别覆盖更窄的类别。说 in the broader sense 就是上升一层概括，覆盖变多而细节变少；这个移动由比较级完成。

senses.title: More inclusive: audience and participation
senses.titleCN: 更具包容性：受众与参与
senses.definition: reaching or including more people than a previous audience, group, or arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 比先前的受众、群体或安排触及或包含更多人
senses.example: The podcast found a broader audience than the original radio show.
senses.exampleCN: 这档播客找到了比原广播节目更广泛的受众。
senses.why: The circle of people is treated as an area. A broader audience means the circle's edge has moved outward, so more people are inside it; the same spatial comparison now measures social reach.
senses.whyCN: 人群的圈子被当作一块面积。更广泛的受众意味着圈的边缘向外移，因此更多人在圈内；同一个空间比较现在量的是社会触达。

senses.title: More open or tolerant in outlook
senses.titleCN: 眼界更开阔、更宽容
senses.definition: of a person or view, more willing to accept differences and less limited by one narrow standpoint
senses.definitionCN: 指人或观点更愿意接受差异，较少受单一狭隘立场限制
senses.example: She came back with a broader view of what counts as success.
senses.exampleCN: 她回来时对什么算成功有了更开阔的看法。
senses.why: This is the mind-as-space metaphor again, now comparative: an outlook with wider walls admits more kinds of life and opinion without rejecting them first. The comparison turns width into tolerance.
senses.whyCN: 这仍是“心智即空间”的比喻，只是变成比较级：墙更宽的眼界能容纳更多生活方式与意见，而不先排斥它们。比较把宽度变成了宽容。

senses.title: Discourse: the broader picture and context
senses.titleCN: 篇章用法：更大的图景与背景
senses.definition: used in writing and speech to call for the larger setting around a case, as in the broader context
senses.definitionCN: 用于书面与口语，要求把个案放回更大的背景中，如 the broader context
senses.example: Before judging the decision, consider the broader context of the shortage.
senses.exampleCN: 在评判这一决定前，先考虑短缺这一更大的背景。
senses.why: The comparative asks the reader to step back until more of the scene is visible. It is a framing move, not a new sense of broad: the same adjective is simply placed in a comparison of visible scope.
