senses.whyCN: 这个比较级要求读者后退，直到看见更多场景。它是一种取景动作，而不是 broad 的新义项：同一个形容词只是被放进可见范围的比较。

senses.title: Usage boundary: broader versus wider
senses.titleCN: 用法边界：broader 与 wider
senses.definition: both compare width; wider is usual for physical gaps, while broader is usual for scope, meaning, and outlook
senses.definitionCN: 两者都比较宽度；wider 常用于物理缺口，broader 常用于范围、意义与眼界
senses.example: The river is wider here, but the argument is broader there.
senses.exampleCN: 河在这里更宽，而论点在那里更广。
senses.why: Broad and wide overlap physically, but broad developed a strong abstract life. Broader therefore follows broad into abstract comparisons, and wider stays closer to measured space; the difference is in the base adjective, not the comparative ending.
senses.whyCN: broad 与 wide 在物理上有重叠，但 broad 发展出很强的抽象用法。因此 broader 跟随 broad 进入抽象比较，而 wider 更贴近可测量的空间；差别在基础形容词，不在比较级词尾。

senses.title: Usage boundary: broader versus larger and greater
senses.titleCN: 用法边界：broader 与 larger、greater
senses.definition: larger compares size or number; greater compares amount or importance; broader compares the width of a range
senses.definitionCN: larger 比较尺寸或数量；greater 比较数量或重要性；broader 比较范围的宽度
senses.example: A larger sample may still not give a broader picture.
senses.exampleCN: 更大的样本未必能给出更广的图景。
senses.why: The three comparatives measure different things: size, amount, and breadth. A sample can grow in number without covering more kinds of cases, which is why the adjectives cannot be swapped.
senses.whyCN: 这三个比较级量的是不同东西：尺寸、数量与广度。样本数量可以变大，却未必覆盖更多种类的案例，因此这些形容词不能互换。

senses.title: Grammar boundary: comparison without an independent meaning
senses.titleCN: 语法边界：没有独立词义的比较级
senses.definition: broader exists only as the comparative of broad; it cannot be used as a base adjective or paired with 'more'
senses.definitionCN: broader 只作为 broad 的比较级存在；不能当原级形容词用，也不能与 more 搭配
senses.example: Say 'broader', not 'more broader'; the comparison is already inside the word.
senses.exampleCN: 说 broader，不说 more broader；比较意义已经在词内。
senses.why: The suffix -er is the comparative marker, so the word has no lexical entry of its own. Every sense it shows is simply one sense of broad placed in a comparison, which is why no new etymology is needed.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -er 就是比较级标记，因此这个词没有自己的词条。它显示的每个义项，都只是 broad 的某个义项被放进比较，因此不需要新的词源。

intro.en: Broader is not a borrowed word and has no independent history. It is broad plus the native comparative suffix -er, formed by rule whenever two things are compared; its meaning is entirely the meaning of broad under comparison. Etymonline has no separate broader entry.
intro.cn: broader 不是借词，也没有独立的历史。它是 broad 加本土比较级后缀 -er，凡比较两物时按规则构成；它的意义完全是 broad 的意义被放进比较。etymonline 没有单独的 broader 词条。

items.en: The base is Old English brād 'wide, not narrow', also 'flat, open, extended'. It already covered physical width and open space; the abstract senses of daylight and of speech developed later.
items.cn: 基础词是古英语 brād“宽的、不窄的”，也表示“平坦的、敞开的、延展的”。它已覆盖物理宽度与开阔空间；白昼与言语的抽象义后来才发展出来。

items.en: Brād goes back to Proto-Germanic *braidi-, also the source of German breit and Dutch breed. Etymonline says the origin is unknown and the word is not found outside Germanic; the deeper PIE source should not be invented.
items.cn: brād 上溯原始日耳曼语 *braidi-，也是德语 breit、荷兰语 breed 的来源。etymonline 称其来源不明，且不见于日耳曼语族之外；更深的原始印欧语来源不应硬造。

items.en: The suffix -er is the native comparative ending, from Old English -ra and Germanic *-izô. It is the regular marker for short adjectives, as in wider, deeper, and broader. It adds comparison, not a new lexical root.
items.cn: 后缀 -er 是本土比较级词尾，来自古英语 -ra 与日耳曼语 *-izô。它是短形容词的规则标记，如 wider、deeper、broader。它添加的是比较，不是新的词根。

items.en: Broader is produced by rule, not recorded as a separate coinage. It has no dictionary history of its own; the same form would appear whenever broad is compared. This is why its etymology is the etymology of broad plus the comparative ending.
items.cn: broader 按规则生成，不是单独铸造的词。它没有自己的词典史；只要 broad 参与比较，就会出现这个形式。因此它的词源就是 broad 的词源加比较级词尾。

items.en: As broad grew common in abstract phrases such as broad view and broad sense, the comparative followed: broader view, broader sense, broader context. The exact first dates of these phrases are not recorded, so the century is only an approximate frame.
items.cn: 随着 broad 在 broad view、broad sense 等抽象短语中普及，比较级也随之跟进：broader view、broader sense、broader context。这些短语的确切最早年代未见记录，因此该世纪只是大致框架。

items.en: Modern academic and journalistic English uses broader before nouns to frame a discussion: broader implications, broader picture, broader debate. The comparative still carries every sense of broad, and it is still an inflected form rather than a new word.
items.cn: 现代学术与新闻英语把 broader 放在名词前，用来给讨论取景：broader implications、broader picture、broader debate。这个比较级仍承载 broad 的所有义项，也仍是屈折形式，而不是一个新词。

note.en: The first group is broad in its positive, superlative, adverbial, and verb forms; the second separates comparisons of width, size, amount, and coverage.
note.cn: 第一组是 broad 的原级、最高级、副词与动词形式；第二组区分宽度、尺寸、数量与覆盖范围这几种比较。

entries.definition: Wide or large in range. It is the base form; broader is only this adjective under comparison.
entries.definitionCN: 宽的，或范围广的。它是原级；broader 只是这个形容词被放进比较。

entries.definition: The most broad of a group. It uses the superlative -est, where broader uses the comparative -er.
entries.definitionCN: 一群中最宽的。它用最高级 -est，而 broader 用比较级 -er。

entries.definition: In general terms or widely. It modifies a verb or sentence, while broader modifies a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 大体上或广泛地。它修饰动词或句子，而 broader 修饰名词。

entries.definition: To make or become broad. It names the action, while broader only compares two degrees of the quality.
entries.definitionCN: 使变宽或变宽。它命名动作，而 broader 只比较同一性质的两个程度。

entries.definition: Comparative of wide: measuring more from side to side. It is the usual choice for physical gaps, roads, and openings.
entries.definitionCN: wide 的比较级：两侧之间量得更多。它是物理缺口、道路与开口的常用选择。

entries.definition: Comparative of large: greater in size or number. It measures overall magnitude, not the width of a range.
entries.definitionCN: large 的比较级：尺寸或数量更大。它量的是总体规模，而不是范围的宽度。

entries.definition: Comparative of great: larger in amount, degree, or importance. It often compares abstract value rather than extent.
entries.definitionCN: great 的比较级：数量、程度或重要性更大。它常比较抽象价值，而不是范围。

entries.definition: Covering much or nearly everything. It stresses completeness of coverage, while broader only compares two degrees of width.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖很多或几乎全部的。它强调覆盖的完整性，而 broader 只比较宽度的两个程度。

normalIntro.en: Real associations: broad + the comparative -er, the same adjective-and-suffix pattern as wider and deeper; broader has no separate root to memorise.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联想：broad + 比较级 -er，与 wider、deeper 同一“形容词加后缀”模式；broader 没有可单独记的词根。

normal.en: broad + -er = broader, exactly like wide + -er = wider and deep + -er = deeper. The suffix means 'more', and it needs no new root.
normal.cn: broad + -er = broader，正如 wide + -er = wider、deep + -er = deeper。后缀表示“更”，不需要新词根。

normal.en: broader is not a base adjective: you say broader, never more broader. The comparison is already inside the word.
normal.cn: broader 不是原级形容词：说 broader，绝不说 more broader。比较意义已经在词内。

normal.en: In the broader sense, you climb one step up the category ladder: more coverage, less detail.
normal.cn: in the broader sense 就是沿类别阶梯上升一级：覆盖更多，细节更少。

normal.en: A broader audience is a circle with its edge pushed outward, so more people are inside.
normal.cn: 更广泛的受众就是一个边缘被向外推的圈，因此更多人在圈内。

normal.en: The broader picture is a wider camera angle: the same scene, but more of it is visible.
normal.cn: the broader picture 就是一个更广的镜头：场景不变，但看见的部分更多。

abstract.en: Two roads side by side: broader is the one whose two edges stand farther apart, though both lead to the same destination.
abstract.cn: 两条并排的路：broader 是两边距离更远的那条，尽管两者通向同一目的地。

abstract.en: A lens zooming out: nothing in the scene changes, but the frame now holds more of the world, and that is broader.
abstract.cn: 镜头拉远：场景里没有任何东西改变，但取景框现在装下更多世界，这就是 broader。

abstract.en: A hand opening from a fist to a flat palm: the same hand, a wider span, more things it can hold.
abstract.cn: 一只手从拳头张开成掌心：同一只手，跨度更大，能握住的东西更多。

examples.en: The new report takes a broader view of the problem than the earlier one.
examples.cn: 这份新报告比早先那份对问题采取了更广阔的视角。

examples.en: A broader range of countries took part in the second survey.
examples.cn: 第二次调查有更广泛的国家参与。

examples.en: We need to consider the broader context before making a decision.
examples.cn: 在做决定之前，我们需要考虑更大的背景。

dict_mnemonic.text: “布若德”——把布（broad）再往两边拉一点，比原来更宽 → broader 更宽的

root: broad（古英语 brād“宽的”，原始日耳曼语 *braidi-，来源不明）+ -er（本土比较级词尾，古英语 -ra，日耳曼语 *-izô）；broader 是 broad 的比较级屈折形式，不是独立词根或新派生词。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of broader are nine senses of broad under comparison: physical width, range, generality, inclusion, outlook, framing, and two boundaries. The comparative ending never adds a new meaning of its own.
sensesIntro.cn: broader 的九个义项就是 broad 的九个义项被放进比较：物理宽度、范围、概括度、包容性、眼界、取景，以及两个边界。比较级词尾本身从不添加新意义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one width is set beside another, and this one reaches farther at both edges.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个宽度与另一个并置，而这一个在两条边上都伸得更远。

branches.en: PHYSICAL: two objects are compared, and one measures more from side to side.
branches.cn: 物理：两个物体被比较，其中一个从一侧到另一侧量得更多。

branches.en: SCOPE: the compared thing covers more cases, sources, or activities at both ends.
branches.cn: 范围：被比较者覆盖更多案例、资料或活动，两端都伸得更远。

branches.en: GENERALITY: the broader category sits one level above the narrower one.
branches.cn: 概括度：较宽的类别位于较窄类别之上的一层。

branches.en: PEOPLE AND MIND: a wider circle admits more people, and a wider outlook admits more views.
branches.cn: 人群与心智：更宽的圈容纳更多人，更宽的眼界容纳更多观点。

branches.en: FRAME AND BOUNDARIES: the comparative frames a scene, then meets wider, larger, greater, and the grammar of comparison.
branches.cn: 取景与边界：这个比较级为场景取景，再与 wider、larger、greater 以及比较语法划界。

intro.en: Broader has one live suffix, the comparative -er, attached to the adjective broad. There is no prefix and no derivational suffix; the ending marks a grammatical degree, not a new word.
intro.cn: broader 在形容词 broad 上只有一个活后缀，即比较级 -er。它没有前缀，也没有派生后缀；这个词尾标记语法程度，而不是构成新词。

latinIntro.en: Broader has no Latin ancestry. Latin latus 'wide' and amplus 'large' are separate roots, and extendere is a separate verb; the entries below are counterparts that English also uses, not ancestors of broader.
latinIntro.cn: broader 没有拉丁语血统。拉丁语 latus“宽的”与 amplus“大的”是另外的词根，extendere 是另一个动词；下面的条目是英语同时使用的对应词，不是 broader 的祖先。

items.meaning: more broad; the adjective placed in a comparison, with no change of lexical meaning
items.meaningCN: 更宽的；形容词被放进比较，词汇意义不变
items.example: The river is broader at its mouth.
items.exampleCN: 这条河在入海口更宽。

items.meaning: wide in space or large in range; the base that supplies all the content of broader
items.meaningCN: 空间上宽的，或范围广的；为 broader 提供全部内容的基础词
items.example: A broad plain lies beyond the hills.
items.exampleCN: 山丘之外是一片广阔的平原。

items.meaning: most broad of a group; the superlative counterpart of broader
items.meaningCN: 一群中最宽的；broader 的最高级对应形式
items.example: This is the broadest part of the valley.
items.exampleCN: 这是山谷最宽的部分。

items.meaning: in general terms or widely; the adjective becomes an adverb
items.meaningCN: 大体上或广泛地；形容词变成副词
items.example: Broadly, the two plans agree.
items.exampleCN: 大体而言，两个方案是一致的。

items.structure: broad + -th (noun of a quality), with a vowel change
items.meaning: width or range; the noun of the quality that broader compares
items.meaningCN: 宽度或广度；broader 所比较的性质的名词形式
items.example: The breadth of the shelf is two metres.
items.exampleCN: 这个架子的宽度是两米。

items.meaning: to make or become broad; the action that produces a broader state
items.meaningCN: 使变宽或变宽；产生更宽状态的动作
items.example: They broadened the road last year.
items.exampleCN: 他们去年把路加宽了。

items.meaning: the quality of being broad; a regular alternative to breadth
items.meaningCN: 宽的性质；breadth 的规则替代形式
items.example: The broadness of the proposal worried the board.
items.exampleCN: 提案的宽泛让董事会担忧。

items.meaning: measuring much from side to side; a separate adjective whose comparative is wider
items.meaningCN: 两侧之间量得多的；另一个形容词，其比较级是 wider
items.example: The gap is too wide to jump.
items.exampleCN: 缺口太宽，跳不过去。

items.meaning: to make or become wide; the physical-width counterpart of broaden
items.meaningCN: 使变宽或变宽；broaden 在物理宽度上的对应动词
items.example: They widened the doorway for the wheelchair.
items.exampleCN: 他们为轮椅把门洞加宽了。

latinEntries.meaning: wide, broad; a separate Latin root, not the source of broad
latinEntries.meaningCN: 宽的；另一个拉丁词根，并非 broad 的来源

latinEntries.meaning: large, spacious, abundant; the source of amplify and ampler, not of broader
latinEntries.meaningCN: 大的、宽敞的、丰富的；amplify 与 ampler 的来源，不是 broader 的来源

latinEntries.meaning: to stretch out or lengthen; a Latin counterpart stressing length
latinEntries.meaningCN: 向外伸展或延长；强调长度的拉丁对应词

definition_zh: 宽阔地；广泛地；大体而言；笼统地
definition_en: in a wide manner, over a large scope, or in general terms without detail
core_image: 一只手掌在地图上画出一个大圈，而不是用针尖点住一个位置
scene: Broadly speaking, the two explanations describe the same process, though they differ in detail.
sceneCN: 这里 broadly 是「大体而言」（第 3 个义项：说话者给结论划出大致范围）；句意：大体而言，这两种解释描述的是同一个过程，尽管细节不同。场景要点：手掌在地图上画出一个大圈，把两种解释都圈进去，而不点住其中一种。

pos.zh: 宽阔地；广泛地；大体而言；笼统地

derivatives.zh: 宽度；广度；（知识、兴趣的）范围

senses.title: Across a wide physical space
senses.titleCN: 空间上宽阔地：向两侧铺开
senses.definition: over a wide area or with a wide opening
senses.definitionCN: 以大范围或大开口的方式；宽阔地
senses.example: The valley opens broadly toward the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 山谷朝海的一面开阔地展开。
senses.why: Broad began as a word for physical width. The -ly suffix turns that width into the manner of a process, so the first sense simply lets something extend sideways.
senses.whyCN: broad 最初就是表示物理“横向宽”的词。-ly 把这个宽度变成过程进行的方式，所以最基本的义项就是让某物向两侧铺开。

senses.title: With a large, open movement
senses.titleCN: 动作幅度大地：咧嘴、张开地
senses.definition: with a large, open movement of the body or face
senses.definitionCN: 以身体或面部大幅度、张开的方式
senses.example: She smiled broadly and shook his hand.
senses.exampleCN: 她咧嘴大笑，和他握了握手。
senses.why: A wide mouth or wide gesture covers more space than a narrow one. The same spatial width is applied to the body, and -ly marks how the action is performed.
senses.whyCN: 张大的嘴或张开的手势比收紧时占据更多空间。同一个空间宽度被移到身体动作上，-ly 标记的正是动作进行的方式。

senses.title: In general terms
senses.titleCN: 大体而言：不落到细节
senses.definition: in general terms, without going into detail
senses.definitionCN: 以概括的方式；不涉及细节地
senses.example: Broadly speaking, the two explanations describe the same process.
senses.exampleCN: 大体而言，这两种解释描述的是同一个过程。
senses.why: When the scope of a statement is widened, details fall outside its edge. Speaking broadly means drawing the boundary far out so the main claim fits, while exceptions stay outside.
senses.whyCN: 当一个陈述的范围被放宽，细节就落到边界之外。broadly speaking 就是把边界画得很远，让主要结论装得进去，而例外留在圈外。

senses.title: Over a wide range
senses.titleCN: 广泛地：覆盖许多对象
senses.definition: across a large range of people, things, or cases
senses.definitionCN: 在许多人、事物或情形的大范围内
senses.example: The policy is broadly supported by both parties.
senses.exampleCN: 这项政策得到两党的广泛支持。
senses.why: The spatial circle becomes a set of cases. If the circle is drawn wide, it contains many members, so broadly comes to mean 'by a large part of the group'.
senses.whyCN: 空间的圆圈变成了事例的集合。圈画得大，装进去的成员就多，于是 broadly 表示“由群体中很大一部分”。

senses.title: Roughly, by approximation
senses.titleCN: 大致地：留出误差带
senses.definition: approximately, without exact figures
senses.definitionCN: 近似地；不用精确数字地
senses.example: The two cities are broadly comparable in size.
senses.exampleCN: 这两座城市在规模上大致相当。
senses.why: A wide boundary cannot fix a point. If the statement covers a band rather than a line, the value is approximate, and the adverb signals tolerance.
senses.whyCN: 宽的边界定不住一个点。如果陈述覆盖的是一条带而不是一条线，数值就是近似的，副词标记的正是这种容差。

senses.title: In the broad sense of a definition
senses.titleCN: 广义上：把定义的边界推远
senses.definition: using a wide rather than a strict definition
senses.definitionCN: 采用宽泛而非严格的定义
senses.example: Broadly defined, intelligence includes the ability to adapt.
senses.exampleCN: 从广义上界定，智力包括适应环境的能力。
senses.why: Definitions also have edges. To define broadly is to push the edge outward so that more cases count, as opposed to a narrow definition that draws it close.
senses.whyCN: 定义也有边界。广义定义是把边界往外推，让更多情形算进来；狭义定义则把边界收近。

senses.title: Looking at the whole picture
senses.titleCN: 整体地：把整片场地收进视线
senses.definition: considering the whole of something rather than isolated parts
senses.definitionCN: 考虑整体而非孤立部分地
senses.example: We need to look broadly at the causes of the decline.
senses.exampleCN: 我们需要从整体上审视下滑的原因。
senses.why: This sense keeps the spatial image but moves it to attention: a wide gaze takes in the whole field instead of one detail.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项保留空间意象，但把它移到注意力上：宽的视线收进整片场地，而不是只盯一个细节。

senses.title: Sweeping, without distinction
senses.titleCN: 笼统地：一概而论
senses.definition: in an undiscriminating way that treats different cases as one
senses.definitionCN: 不加区分地把不同情形当作一种
senses.example: To say that all teenagers are lazy generalizes too broadly.
senses.exampleCN: 说所有青少年都懒惰，这个概括太笼统了。
senses.why: A circle that is too wide swallows cases that should have stayed apart. The adverb then carries a critical tone: the scope has been widened past what the evidence supports.
senses.whyCN: 圈画得太大，会把本该分开的情形一并吞进去。此时副词带批评语气：范围被放宽到证据撑不住的地步。

senses.title: With a solid, wide build
senses.titleCN: 体格宽厚地：肩膀占宽度
senses.definition: with a wide, strongly built body
senses.definitionCN: 以体格宽厚、结实的方式
senses.example: He was broadly built and moved slowly through the door.
senses.exampleCN: 他体格宽厚，慢慢地穿过门口。
senses.why: The original physical sense returns in a fixed pattern. Broadly built describes shoulders that occupy width, not a manner of thinking.
senses.whyCN: 最初的空间义在固定搭配里回归。broadly built 描述的是占宽度的肩膀，而不是思考方式。

intro.en: Broadly is not a borrowed word but an English derivative: the Old English adjective broad takes the adverbial suffix -ly. Dates for the adverb's first appearance are uncertain.
intro.cn: broadly 不是借来的词，而是英语内部派生词：古英语形容词 broad 加上副词后缀 -ly。该副词最早出现的年代不确定。

items.en: brad meant 'wide, not narrow', and also 'flat, open, extended'. It described the physical spread of a thing, not a quality of thinking.
items.cn: brad 意为“宽的、不窄的”，也表示“平的、敞开的、延展开的”。它描述事物在空间上的铺开，而不是思维品质。

items.en: The ancestor is reconstructed as *braidi-, with cognates in Old Frisian bred, Old Norse breidr, Dutch breed and German breit. Its deeper origin is unknown, and the word is not found outside Germanic.
items.cn: 其祖词被重构为原始日耳曼语 *braidi-，同源词见于古弗里斯语 bred、古诺斯语 breidr、荷兰语 breed 和德语 breit。更早的来源不明，这个词也不见于日耳曼语族之外。

items.en: The adverbial suffix came from Old English -lice, from Proto-Germanic *-liko-, related to a word for 'body, form' and cognate with like. Middle English shortened it to -li, giving modern -ly.
items.cn: 副词后缀来自古英语 -lice，再往上为原始日耳曼语 *-liko-，与表示“身体、外形”的词有关，并与 like 同源。中古英语把它缩为 -li，形成现代 -ly。

items.en: broad + -ly produced the adverb 'in a broad manner'. The suffix does not change the meaning of broad; it changes the job the word does, from naming a property to naming how an action is carried out.
items.cn: broad + -ly 构成了副词“以宽的方式”。后缀并不改变 broad 的意义，而是改变这个词的职能：从命名一种属性，变成说明动作怎样进行。

items.en: Physical width became scope, and scope became generality. If a statement's circle is drawn wide, detail and exceptions fall outside it, so 'in a broad manner' turns into 'in general terms'.
items.cn: 物理宽度变成范围，范围又变成概括性。如果一个陈述的圈画得很宽，细节和例外就落在圈外，于是“以宽的方式”转为“大体而言”。

items.en: Modern academic and journalistic English relies on broadly speaking, broadly defined and broadly similar to hedge a claim. Broad's origin is Old English; the adverb was formed inside English rather than borrowed, but its exact first record is uncertain.
items.cn: 现代学术与新闻英语常用 broadly speaking、broadly defined、broadly similar 来给论断留余地。broad 源自日耳曼语，副词是在英语内部构成的，并非借词；但它最早的确切记录年代存疑。

note.en: The first group contains the adjective, verb and nouns of the same broad family; the second contains adverbs that also soften or widen a claim.
note.cn: 第一组是同一 broad 词族的形容词、动词和名词；第二组是同样能放宽或弱化陈述的副词。

entries.definition: wide, not narrow; also general in scope. It is the adjective that broadly is built on, so it names a property rather than a manner.
entries.definitionCN: 宽的、不窄的；也指范围广泛的。它是 broadly 所依附的形容词，因此命名的是属性而不是方式。

entries.definition: to make or become wider or more inclusive. The -en suffix makes a verb, so it names a change rather than a way of acting.
entries.definitionCN: 加宽；扩大；使更具包容性。-en 后缀构成动词，因此它命名的是变化，而不是做事的方式。

entries.definition: the quality of being wide or general. The -ness suffix turns the adjective into an abstract noun, not an adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 宽阔；宽泛。 -ness 后缀把形容词变成抽象名词，而不是副词。

entries.definition: width, or the range of someone's knowledge and interest. It belongs to the same family but is not formed by adding -th to modern broad, and its vowel is /e/, not /ɔː/.
entries.definitionCN: 宽度；也指知识或兴趣的范围。它属于同一词族，但并非由现代 broad 加 -th 构成，且元音是 /e/，不是 /ɔː/。

entries.definition: in most cases or usually. It points to frequency and typicality, while broadly points to the width of a statement's scope.
entries.definitionCN: 通常；在多数情况下。它指向频率和典型性，而 broadly 指向陈述范围之宽。

entries.definition: over a large area or among many people. It stresses how far something is distributed, not how general a claim is.
entries.definitionCN: 在大范围或许多人之中。它强调分布得有多广，而不是论断有多概括。

entries.definition: mostly, to a great extent. It measures the degree of a claim, whereas broadly measures the scope within which the claim is meant to hold.
entries.definitionCN: 主要地；在很大程度上。它衡量论断的程度，而 broadly 衡量论断意在成立的范围。

entries.definition: without strict definition or precision. It stresses looseness of wording, while broadly stresses the wide extent of what is covered.
entries.definitionCN: 不严格地；不精确地。它强调措辞松散，而 broadly 强调所覆盖的范围之宽。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real adjective, the real suffix and the real phrases in which broadly appears.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的形容词、真实的后缀，以及 broadly 真实出现的短语。

normal.en: broad + -ly: the adjective names width, and the suffix asks 'in what manner?' The answer is 'in a broad manner'.
normal.cn: broad + -ly：形容词命名宽度，后缀问“以什么方式？”答案就是“以宽的方式”。

normal.en: -ly here is the adverbial -ly from Old English -lice, not the adjective-forming -ly in manly or friendly.
normal.cn: 这里的 -ly 是来自古英语 -lice 的副词后缀，不是 manly、friendly 里构成形容词的那个 -ly。

normal.en: The fixed phrase broadly speaking is the clearest signal of the 'in general' sense.
normal.cn: 固定短语 broadly speaking 是“大体而言”这一义项最清楚的信号。

normal.en: Broadly similar and broadly consistent are the common academic collocations: the adverb says the match is close but not exact.
normal.cn: broadly similar 和 broadly consistent 是常见学术搭配：副词表示吻合得接近，但并不精确。

normal.en: broad, broaden, broadness and breadth form one visible family; only broadly is the adverb.
normal.cn: broad、broaden、broadness、breadth 构成一个看得见的词族；其中只有 broadly 是副词。

abstract.en: Picture a finger drawing a large circle on a map instead of pinning one spot: that circle is broadly.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指在地图上画出一个大圈，而不是钉住一个点：那个大圈就是 broadly。

abstract.en: Picture a wide-angle lens: it captures the whole room at once, but no single face in detail.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚广角镜头：它一次收进整个房间，却不细究任何一张脸。

abstract.en: Picture a fence moved far out so that almost every house is inside the same yard: the boundary is wide, so the statement is general.
abstract.cn: 想象把栅栏挪得很远，几乎每栋房子都落在同一个院子里：边界宽了，陈述也就概括了。

examples.en: Broadly speaking, the two theories agree about the cause of the ice ages.
examples.cn: 大体而言，这两种理论对冰期成因的看法是一致的。

examples.en: The new rule was broadly welcomed by smaller companies.
examples.cn: 这项新规定受到小型企业的广泛欢迎。

examples.en: The two samples are broadly comparable in age.
examples.cn: 这两个样本在年代上大致相当。

dict_mnemonic.text: “布罗德利”——布（broad）铺得宽，德（d）利（ly）落地，范围一大就成“大体而言” → broadly 大体而言、广泛地

root: 古英语 brad“宽、平、展开”，源自原始日耳曼语 *braidi-（更早来源不明，仅见于日耳曼语族）；broad + -ly（古英语副词后缀 -lice）构成方式副词。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses share one gesture: a boundary is drawn wide, so more space, more cases, or less detail fall inside it.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项共享同一个动作：把边界画宽，于是更多空间、更多情形或更少的细节被装进圈内。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wide circle drawn around many things, not a pin stuck into one point.
core.cn: 核心意象：画一个套住许多事物的大圈，而不是把针扎在一个点上。

branches.en: BODY AND SPACE: physical width, a large open gesture, and a broad build all keep the original spatial meaning.
branches.cn: 身体与空间：物理宽度、张开的大动作和宽厚的体格，都保留着最初的空间意义。

branches.en: GENERAL VIEW: speaking in general terms and looking at the whole picture both widen the boundary of attention.
branches.cn: 整体视角：大体而言和整体审视，都是把注意力的边界放宽。

branches.en: WIDE COVERAGE: a wide range of supporters and a broad definition both push the edge outward so more cases count.
branches.cn: 广泛覆盖：广泛的支持者和宽泛的定义，都把边界往外推，让更多情形算数。

branches.en: APPROXIMATION: a wide boundary cannot fix a point, so the claim becomes approximate.
branches.cn: 近似：宽的边界定不住一个点，因此论断变成近似值。

branches.en: TOO WIDE: when the circle swallows cases that should stay apart, broadly turns critical and means 'sweepingly'.
branches.cn: 过宽：当圈把本该分开的情形一并吞下，broadly 就带批评意味，表示“笼统地”。

intro.en: Broadly is a live English derivative: an Old English adjective plus an Old English adverbial suffix. The suffix is productive; the base broad is a native word, not a Latin stem.
intro.cn: broadly 是活的英语派生词：古英语形容词加古英语副词后缀。后缀有能产性，而词基 broad 是本土词，不是拉丁词干。

latinIntro.en: Broad has no Latin cognate: it is a Germanic word with no relatives outside that family. Latin does supply several borrowed adjectives for width and flatness, which are useful contrasts but not sources of broad.
latinIntro.cn: broad 没有拉丁同源词：它是日耳曼语词，在该语族之外没有亲属。拉丁语确实提供了几个表示“宽、平”的借词形容词，可作对照，但它们不是 broad 的来源。

items.meaning: in a broad manner; in general terms
items.meaningCN: 宽阔地；大体而言（-ly 构成方式副词）
items.example: Broadly, the plan has three stages.
items.exampleCN: 大体而言，这个计划分为三个阶段。

items.meaning: wide, not narrow; general in scope
items.meaningCN: 宽的；广泛的（基础形容词）
items.example: The river is broad at this point.
items.exampleCN: 这条河在这里很宽。

items.meaning: to make or become broad
items.meaningCN: 加宽；扩大（-en 构成动词）
items.example: Travel can broaden your view of the world.
items.exampleCN: 旅行能拓宽你对世界的看法。

items.meaning: width; range of knowledge or interest
items.meaningCN: 宽度；广度（-th 构成抽象名词，与 broad 同族但并非现代构词）
items.example: The breadth of her reading surprised the panel.
items.exampleCN: 她阅读范围之广让评审小组感到意外。

items.meaning: the quality of being broad
items.meaningCN: 宽阔；宽泛（-ness 构成性质名词）
items.example: The broadness of the definition caused disagreement.
items.exampleCN: 定义过于宽泛，引起了分歧。

items.meaning: a wide band of frequencies; high-speed data connection
items.meaningCN: 宽带（宽频带；高速数据连接）
items.example: The village finally has broadband.
items.exampleCN: 这个村子终于有了宽带。

items.meaning: the whole side of a ship; a strong written or verbal attack
items.meaningCN: 舷侧；（长篇的）猛烈抨击
items.example: The paper launched a broadside against the plan.
items.exampleCN: 这家报纸对该计划发起了猛烈抨击。

items.meaning: willing to accept views different from one's own
items.meaningCN: 心胸开阔的；能容纳不同观点的
items.example: Her broad-minded parents let her choose her own path.
items.exampleCN: 她心胸开阔的父母让她自己选择道路。

items.meaning: a large-format newspaper, historically associated with serious journalism
items.meaningCN: 大报（大幅面报纸，历史上与严肃新闻相关）
items.example: The story ran in every broadsheet the next morning.
items.exampleCN: 第二天早晨，每家大报都刊登了这则消息。

latinEntries.meaning: wide, broad; the source of English latitude in its geographical sense
latinEntries.meaningCN: 宽的、广的；英语 latitude 的地理义由此而来（语义对照，非同源）

latinEntries.meaning: large, spacious, abundant; source of amplitude and amplify
latinEntries.meaningCN: 大的、宽敞的、充足的；amplitude、amplify 的来源（语义对照，非同源）

latinEntries.meaning: flat, level; source of plain and plane
latinEntries.meaningCN: 平的、平坦的；plain、plane 的来源（对应 broad 的“平、展开”义，但非同源）

definition_en: the act or result of working with numbers, or a careful estimate made in advance
core_image: 木板上摆着一颗颗小石子，一颗代表一个数，摆完就能报出总数
scene: By my calculation, the bridge will be finished about two weeks late.
sceneCN: 这里 calculation 是「估算」（第 3 个义项：依据数字做出的预估判断）；句意：按我的估算，这座桥会晚完工大约两周。场景要点：木板上的小石子被挪动、分组，最后得出一个时间估计。

forms.label: 复数（多次计算或多个得数）

senses.title: Working with numbers
senses.titleCN: 计算过程：把数摆开来算
senses.definition: the act or process of computing with numbers
senses.definitionCN: 用数字进行运算的行为或过程
senses.example: The calculation took less than a second.
senses.exampleCN: 这次计算用了不到一秒。
senses.why: Latin calculus was a pebble used for counting. The -ion suffix names the action built on that practice, so calculation is first the activity of moving the pebbles.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 calculus 就是计数用的小石子。-ion 后缀命名建立在这种做法上的行为，所以 calculation 首先是挪动石子的活动。

senses.title: The result of a reckoning
senses.titleCN: 得数：石子摆完后留下的总数
senses.definition: the result obtained by computing; the answer to a problem
senses.definitionCN: 运算得到的结果；问题的答案
senses.example: My calculation was off by ten percent.
senses.exampleCN: 我的得数差了百分之十。
senses.why: Latin -ion names both an action and its result. Once the pebbles are placed, the total stays as a thing, so the same noun also means the answer.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 -ion 既命名行为，也命名结果。石子摆好之后，总数作为一个结果留了下来，因此同一个名词也可指答案。

senses.title: A rough estimate
senses.titleCN: 估算：用近似数作预测
senses.definition: an estimate or forecast based on available figures
senses.definitionCN: 根据现有数字作出的估计或预测
senses.example: By my calculation, we will arrive before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 照我估算，我们中午前会到。
senses.why: If the pebbles are few or approximate, the outcome is a forecast rather than an exact answer. The noun moves from arithmetic to prediction.
senses.whyCN: 如果石子很少或只是近似，得出的就不是精确答案，而是预测。名词于是从算术领域移到预测领域。

senses.title: One operation in a machine or proof
senses.titleCN: 一次运算：计算链条上的一步
senses.definition: a single step or operation performed by a person, machine, or formula
senses.definitionCN: 由人、机器或公式执行的单步运算
senses.example: The chip performs billions of calculations per second.
senses.exampleCN: 这块芯片每秒执行数十亿次运算。
senses.why: A long computation is a row of small pebble-moves. English counts each move as a calculation, so the noun also names the unit rather than the whole.
senses.whyCN: 一长串计算就是一连串挪动石子的动作。英语把每一步都算作一次 calculation，因此这个名词也指单位动作，而不是整体。

senses.title: A model computation
senses.titleCN: 科学演算：用模型推演
senses.definition: a set of numerical operations used to model a scientific or technical problem
senses.definitionCN: 用于模拟科学或技术问题的一组数值运算
senses.example: Climate calculations suggest a warmer century.
senses.exampleCN: 气候演算表明本世纪会更暖。
senses.why: Science replaces pebbles with variables but keeps the same structure: inputs are placed, rules applied, and an output read off.
senses.whyCN: 科学用变量替代石子，但结构不变：先放入输入，再套用规则，最后读出结果。

senses.title: Casting a horoscope
senses.titleCN: 占星推算：把石子数到天上
senses.definition: the old practice of computing a horoscope from the positions of the stars
senses.definitionCN: 根据星体位置推算星盘的古老做法
senses.example: Medieval almanacs included calculations for each month.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪的历书包含每个月的占星推算。
senses.why: The word's early record includes astrology: the same counting procedure was applied to the heavens, and the noun named that art.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的早期记录包括占星：同一套计数程序被用到天上，名词命名的就是那门技艺。

senses.title: Self-interested reckoning
senses.titleCN: 精打细算：把人情也拿来数
senses.definition: a cold or self-interested weighing of advantage
senses.definitionCN: 冷静或自私地权衡利益
senses.example: His offer was pure calculation, not kindness.
senses.exampleCN: 他的提议纯属精打细算，并非善意。
senses.why: Counting can be applied to people and favors. When advantage is counted, the noun shifts from mathematics to motive, and it carries a cold tone.
senses.whyCN: 计数也能用在人身上和人情上。当被数的是利益时，名词就从数学转向动机，并带上冷冰冰的语气。

senses.title: Deliberate, premeditated planning
senses.titleCN: 策略性预谋：先算后果再行动
senses.definition: careful, often premeditated planning of an action
senses.definitionCN: 对行动进行仔细、常带预谋的谋划
senses.example: There was calculation in every move she made.
senses.exampleCN: 她每一步都经过盘算。
senses.why: Before acting, one reckons the likely responses. The mental pebbles now stand for consequences, so calculation means planned rather than spontaneous behavior.
senses.whyCN: 行动之前，人要先推算对方可能的反应。此时心里的石子代表后果，于是 calculation 指有计划的、而非即兴的行为。

senses.title: Weighing risks and costs
senses.titleCN: 利弊权衡：把得失放上秤
senses.definition: the weighing of risks, costs, and benefits before a decision
senses.definitionCN: 决策前对风险、成本与收益的权衡
senses.example: The withdrawal was a political calculation before the election.
senses.exampleCN: 这次撤军是选举前的一次政治权衡。
senses.why: The counting board becomes a scale of gains and losses. What is counted is no longer units but costs and benefits.
senses.whyCN: 计数板变成了得失的秤。被数的已不再是单位，而是成本与收益。

intro.en: Calculation is a Latin-derived noun: a pebble word became a verb of reckoning, and -ion made the action into a noun. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: calculation 是拉丁来源的名词：一个“石子”词先变成计算动词，再由 -ion 构成名词。以下年代为大致估计。

items.en: calx (genitive calcis) meant 'limestone, lime'. Its diminutive calculus first meant 'small stone', then specifically a pebble moved on a counting board.
items.cn: calx（属格 calcis）意为“石灰岩、石灰”。它的指小形式 calculus 最初表示“小石头”，后来特指计数板上挪动的小石子。

items.en: calculus also came to mean 'reckoning, account' because pebbles were the actual counters. The thing used to count gave its name to the count itself.
items.cn: calculus 也因此表示“计算、账目”，因为小石子就是实际的计数器。用来计数的东西，把自己的名字给了计数这件事。

items.en: calculare meant 'to reckon, compute'. Its noun of action calculationem (nominative calculatio) named a computation or reckoning, built on the past-participle stem.
items.cn: calculare 意为“计算、核算”。其行为名词 calculationem（主格 calculatio）表示计算或核算，由过去分词词干构成。

items.en: English took calculacioun in the late 14th century for 'the art or practice of computing by numbers'. The same early record also names the making of a horoscope.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪后期借入 calculacioun，表示“用数字计算的技艺或做法”。同一早期记录还指推算星盘。

items.en: The Latin -ion suffix can name an action or its result. English therefore uses calculation for the process and, from the early 15th century, for the solution obtained.
items.cn: 拉丁 -ion 后缀既可命名行为，也可命名结果。因此英语用 calculation 指过程，并从 15 世纪初起也指得到的解。

items.en: The word widened from arithmetic to estimates, model computations, and cold self-interested planning. The pebble image is no longer felt, and calculus was borrowed separately as the name of a branch of mathematics.
items.cn: 这个词从算术扩展到估算、模型演算和冷静的私利盘算。石子意象已不再被感知；calculus 则是另一次独立借入，成为数学分支的名称。

note.en: The look-alikes share the calcul- stem but differ in suffix and word class; the near-meaning group contains words for counting, judging, and estimating.
note.cn: 形近词共享 calcul- 词干，但后缀和词性不同；近义词组则包含计数、判断和估算类的词。

entries.definition: to work out a result with numbers. It is the verb behind calculation; the noun adds -ion and names the act or its result.
entries.definitionCN: 用数字算出结果。它是 calculation 背后的动词；名词加 -ion，表示行为或结果。

entries.definition: a device or person that calculates. The -or suffix marks the doer, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 计算器；计算的人。-or 后缀标记施动者，而不是行为。

entries.definition: a branch of mathematics, or a hard mass formed in the body. It is borrowed directly from Latin calculus 'pebble', not formed from calculate.
entries.definitionCN: 微积分；也可指体内结石。它直接借自拉丁 calculus“石子”，并非由 calculate 派生。

entries.definition: a wrong calculation or misjudgment. The mis- prefix marks error, so it is a faulty instance rather than a separate kind of reckoning.
entries.definitionCN: 计算错误或误判。mis- 前缀标记错误，因此它是计算的一种出错情形，而不是另一类计算。

entries.definition: the act of computing, especially a long or machine-performed process. It is more technical than calculation and often implies many steps.
entries.definitionCN: 计算，尤指冗长或由机器执行的过程。它比 calculation 更技术化，常暗示许多步骤。

entries.definition: an informal count or one's own judgment of a situation; also a settling of accounts. It is more personal and less numerical than calculation.
entries.definitionCN: 非正式的计数或对情况的判断；也指结账。它比 calculation 更个人化，数字性更弱。

entries.definition: an approximate judgment of size, cost, or value, not necessarily reached by exact arithmetic. Calculation can be exact; an estimate is openly approximate.
entries.definitionCN: 对大小、成本或价值的近似判断，未必经过精确运算。calculation 可以是精确的，而 estimate 明确是近似的。

entries.definition: an evaluation of quality, condition, or value. It judges what something is worth rather than working out a number.
entries.definitionCN: 对质量、状况或价值的评估。它判断某物值多少，而不是算出一个数。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin pebble, the real suffix and the real collocations of calculation.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁“石子”、真实的后缀，以及 calculation 的真实搭配。

normal.en: calculus = a pebble used for counting. Every calculation began as a stone moved across a board.
normal.cn: calculus 就是计数用的小石子。每一次 calculation 最初都是在一块板上挪动石子。

normal.en: calculate + -ion: -ion turns the verb into either the act of calculating or the result it produces.
normal.cn: calculate + -ion：-ion 把动词变成“计算的行为”或“算出的结果”。

normal.en: By my calculation is the standard phrase for a reasoned estimate.
normal.cn: by my calculation 是表达“据我估算”的标准说法。

normal.en: Mental calculation is arithmetic done in the head; the collocation keeps the counting sense visible.
normal.cn: mental calculation 是心算；这个搭配让“计数”义保持可见。

normal.en: calculate, calculator, calculable and calculation share one stem, so the family reinforces the meaning.
normal.cn: calculate、calculator、calculable、calculation 共享一个词干，这个词族彼此强化。

abstract.en: Picture a wooden counting board with pebbles lined up in columns: each pebble is a unit, and the pattern is the number.
abstract.cn: 想象一块木制计数板，小石子按列排好：每颗石子是一个单位，排列的形状就是数。

abstract.en: Picture an abacus: the beads are pushed, the rows change, and a total appears at the end.
abstract.cn: 想象一把算盘：珠子被推动，横档变化，最后出现一个总数。

abstract.en: Picture a calculator screen: the long process disappears, and only the result remains — which is why calculation means both process and answer.
abstract.cn: 想象计算器的屏幕：漫长的过程消失了，只剩下结果——这正是 calculation 既指过程又指答案的原因。

examples.en: The engineers made a rough calculation of the load before testing the bridge.
examples.cn: 工程师在测试桥梁之前对荷载做了粗略估算。

examples.en: A single calculation error can invalidate the whole experiment.
examples.cn: 一个计算错误就可能让整个实验失效。

examples.en: Her decision to help him was not kindness but calculation.
examples.cn: 她决定帮他不是出于善意，而是精打细算。

dict_mnemonic.text: “卡了Q雷神”——卡（cal）了（cu）Q（la）雷（tion），石子卡在格子里一颗颗数 → calculation 计算

root: 拉丁 calculus“计数用的小石子”，是 calx“石灰岩”的指小词；calculare“计算、核算”+ -ion 名词后缀，表示行为或结果。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one counting board: pebbles are moved, a total appears, the total is used to forecast, and then the same counting is applied to motives and risks.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿着同一块计数板展开：石子被挪动，总数出现，总数被用来预测，随后同一套计数又被用到动机和风险上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: pebbles placed on a counting board until a total can be read off.
core.cn: 核心意象：把小石子摆到计数板上，直到能读出一个总数。

branches.en: THE COUNTING ACT: the whole process and each single step are both named by the same noun.
branches.cn: 计数行为：整个过程和其中每一步，都由同一个名词命名。

branches.en: THE TOTAL: an arithmetic answer and a horoscope are both results read off from a procedure.
branches.cn: 总数：算术答案和星盘推演，都是从一套程序中读出的结果。

branches.en: FORECAST AND WEIGHING: an estimate and a cost-benefit judgment both apply counting to the future.
branches.cn: 预测与权衡：估算和成本收益判断，都把计数用到未来。

branches.en: THE MODEL: scientific computation keeps the board but replaces pebbles with variables.
branches.cn: 模型：科学演算保留计数板，却用变量替代了石子。

branches.en: THE MOTIVE: counting advantage and counting consequences turn arithmetic into cold planning.
branches.cn: 动机：数利益、数后果，把算术变成了冷静的谋划。

intro.en: Calculation is built on a Latin stem with a live English suffix: calcul- + -ion. The -ion suffix is productive; calcul- is a fossilized Latin stem.
intro.cn: calculation 建立在拉丁词干加活的英语后缀上：calcul- + -ion。-ion 有能产性；calcul- 是凝固的拉丁词干。

latinIntro.en: Latin calculus 'pebble' is the source of a small family: calculate, calculation, calculator, calculable, and the separately borrowed calculus. English also borrowed calx 'limestone' only indirectly, through chalk.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 calculus“小石子”是一个小词族的源头：calculate、calculation、calculator、calculable，以及另行借入的 calculus。英语也间接通过 chalk 借入了 calx“石灰岩”。

items.structure: calcul- (stem of calculare) + -ion (noun of action or result)
items.meaning: the act or result of computing
items.meaningCN: 计算；得数（-ion 表示行为或结果）
items.example: The calculation takes only a few seconds.
items.exampleCN: 这项计算只需几秒钟。

items.meaning: to reckon or compute
items.meaningCN: 计算；核算（-ate 构成动词）
items.example: We calculate the cost before signing.
items.exampleCN: 签字前我们先核算成本。

items.meaning: a device or person that calculates
items.meaningCN: 计算器；计算者（-or 表示施动者）
items.example: The calculator ran out of battery.
items.exampleCN: 计算器没电了。

items.meaning: able to be calculated or estimated
items.meaningCN: 可计算的；可估计的（-able 表示“能被……的”）
items.example: The risk is calculable, though not small.
items.exampleCN: 风险是可以计算的，虽然并不小。

items.meaning: too great or uncertain to be calculated
items.meaningCN: 无法计算的；不可估量的（in- 表示否定）
items.example: The war caused incalculable damage.
items.exampleCN: 这场战争造成了无法估量的损失。

items.meaning: a wrong calculation or misjudgment
items.meaningCN: 计算错误；误判（mis- 表示“错误”）
items.example: The delay was caused by a miscalculation.
items.exampleCN: 延误是由一次计算错误造成的。

items.meaning: a mathematical method; also a stone-like mass in the body
items.meaningCN: 微积分；结石（直接借自拉丁语，仍保留“石子”形象）
items.example: She studied calculus in her first year.
items.exampleCN: 她第一年学了微积分。

items.meaning: tending to calculate; shrewdly self-interested
items.meaningCN: 精于计算的；精打细算的（-ive 表示“具有……性质的”）
items.example: He approached the offer in a calculative mood.
items.exampleCN: 他带着精打细算的心态看待这个提议。

items.meaning: scheming; acting with cold forethought
items.meaningCN: 工于心计的；精于盘算的（-ing 构成分词形容词）
items.example: She gave him a calculating look.
items.exampleCN: 她用一种盘算的眼神看了他一眼。

items.meaning: relating to calculation
items.meaningCN: 与计算有关的（-al 表示“与……有关的”）
items.example: The error is calculational, not theoretical.
items.exampleCN: 这个错误属于计算层面，而不是理论层面。

latinEntries.meaning: limestone; the base of the diminutive calculus
latinEntries.meaningCN: 石灰岩；指小词 calculus 的词基

latinEntries.meaning: small stone; a pebble used in counting; a reckoning
latinEntries.meaningCN: 小石头；计数用的小石子；计算、账目

latinEntries.meaning: to reckon, compute
latinEntries.meaningCN: 计算；核算

latinEntries.meaning: a computation, reckoning
latinEntries.meaningCN: 计算；核算（行为名词）

definition_zh: 校准；标定；刻度设定；（判断）校准
definition_en: the act or process of adjusting an instrument or scale so that its readings match a known standard
core_image: 一把标准尺贴在仪器刻度旁，把每一格推到正确的位置
scene: Before each experiment, the team runs a full calibration of the spectrometer against a known sample.
sceneCN: 这里 calibration 是「校准」（第 1 个义项：用已知标准调整仪器）；句意：每次实验前，团队都用已知样本对光谱仪做一次完整校准。场景要点：标准样本、仪器刻度盘、记录笔，每一格被对齐到已知值。

pos.zh: 校准；标定；刻度设定；（判断）校准

forms.label: 复数（多次校准或多项校准值）

senses.title: Adjusting an instrument to a standard
senses.titleCN: 仪器校准：把读数对齐已知标准
senses.definition: the act of checking and adjusting an instrument so that its readings agree with a known standard
senses.definitionCN: 检查并调整仪器，使其读数与已知标准一致的行为
senses.example: The calibration of the thermometer is repeated every year.
senses.exampleCN: 这支温度计每年都要重新校准。
senses.why: Caliber named the bore of a gun. Calibrate first meant to measure that bore, then to fix any scale against a standard, and -ion names the process.
senses.whyCN: caliber 原本指炮管口径。calibrate 最初表示测定这个口径，后来表示让任何刻度对齐标准，-ion 命名这个过程。

senses.title: The state of being in adjustment
senses.titleCN: 校准状态：已经对准
senses.definition: the condition of an instrument whose readings are known to be accurate
senses.definitionCN: 仪器读数已知准确的状态
senses.example: The gauge is out of calibration and must not be used.
senses.exampleCN: 这只仪表已经失准，不能使用。
senses.why: The result of the act is a state. English uses the same -ion noun for both the process and the standing condition it leaves behind.
senses.whyCN: 动作的结果是一种状态。英语用同一个 -ion 名词既指过程，也指过程留下的持续状态。

senses.title: Setting the divisions of a scale
senses.titleCN: 刻度设定：决定每一格站在哪里
senses.definition: the marking or fixing of the divisions of a scale
senses.definitionCN: 标记或确定刻度上各分格的位置
senses.example: The calibration of the axis places zero at the freezing point.
senses.exampleCN: 这条轴的刻度设定把零点放在冰点。
senses.why: A scale is a row of marks. Calibration decides where each mark sits, so the noun also names the layout of the divisions rather than the instrument.
senses.whyCN: 刻度是一排标记。校准决定每个标记的位置，所以名词也指分格的排布，而不只是仪器。

senses.title: The reference relationship
senses.titleCN: 校准曲线：把信号与真值绑在一起
senses.definition: the established relationship between an instrument's signal and the true value
senses.definitionCN: 仪器信号与真实值之间建立起来的关系
senses.example: The concentration was read from the calibration curve.
senses.exampleCN: 浓度是从校准曲线上读出的。
senses.why: Once each mark is tied to a standard, the whole set of marks forms a curve or table. The noun is transferred from the act to the reference object produced by it.
senses.whyCN: 每个标记一旦绑定到一个标准，整套标记就构成一条曲线或一张表。名词于是从动作转到动作产生的参照物。

senses.title: Fine adjustment of a device
senses.titleCN: 设备调校：让参数回到工作区间
senses.definition: the tuning of a device or system so that it performs within its intended range
senses.definitionCN: 调整设备或系统，使其在预期范围内工作的过程
senses.example: Sensor calibration improved the camera's low-light performance.
senses.exampleCN: 传感器校准改善了相机的弱光表现。
senses.why: Modern devices have many parameters, not one scale. The word widens from a single needle to any setting that must be brought into line.
senses.whyCN: 现代设备有许多参数，而不只是一根指针。这个词从单根刻度扩展到任何需要被对齐的设置。

senses.title: Checking a model against data
senses.titleCN: 模型校准：让模型输出贴合观测
senses.definition: the process of testing and adjusting a model so that its output matches observations
senses.definitionCN: 检验并调整模型，使其输出与观测相符的过程
senses.example: Model calibration against field data reduced the error.
senses.exampleCN: 依据野外数据进行的模型校准降低了误差。
senses.why: A model is treated like an instrument: it produces readings, so it can be calibrated. The standard is now observed data rather than a physical gauge.
senses.whyCN: 模型被当作仪器：它会产生读数，因此可以被校准。此时的标准是观测数据，而不是物理量具。

senses.title: Calibration of confidence
senses.titleCN: 判断校准：自信程度与实际水平对得上吗
senses.definition: the accuracy with which a person's stated confidence matches actual performance
senses.definitionCN: 一个人表达的自信程度与其实际表现相符的准确度
senses.example: Forecasters studied the calibration of their confidence.
senses.exampleCN: 预报员研究了自己信心的校准程度。
senses.why: This is the metaphor at its most abstract: confidence is a scale, and calibration measures whether its marks match reality.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个隐喻最抽象的用法：自信是一条刻度，校准衡量的是刻度是否与真实相符。

senses.title: Measuring a bore
senses.titleCN: 口径测定：最早的字面义
senses.definition: the original sense: determining the caliber, or inside diameter, of a gun barrel
senses.definitionCN: 最初的字面义：测定炮管口径，即内直径
senses.example: The calibration of the barrel decided which shot would fit.
senses.exampleCN: 炮管的口径测定决定了哪种炮弹能装进去。
senses.why: The oldest literal sense measured a bore. Later senses keep the shape of measuring against a fixed width, which is why the word can still mean 'set to a standard'.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的字面义是测量孔径。后来的义项保留了“对着固定宽度测量”的形状，因此这个词仍能表示“对准标准”。

senses.title: Bringing standards into line
senses.titleCN: 标准对齐：让两套规范可比
senses.definition: the adjustment of standards, expectations, or policies so that they agree
senses.definitionCN: 调整标准、预期或政策，使其一致
senses.example: The two agencies agreed on a calibration of their safety standards.
senses.exampleCN: 两个机构就安全标准的对齐达成一致。
senses.why: Institutions also have scales. When separate standards must be made comparable, the instrument image is applied to rules and expectations.
senses.whyCN: 机构也有自己的刻度。当不同的标准需要变得可比时，仪器的意象就被用到规则和预期上。

intro.en: Calibration is a 19th-century derivative of calibrate, which was formed from caliber. The history of caliber itself is disputed, and the often-repeated Arabic-Greek chain is not established.
intro.cn: calibration 是 19 世纪由 calibrate 派生的名词，而 calibrate 又由 caliber 构成。caliber 本身的历史存在争议，常被转述的“阿拉伯—希腊”链条并未得到确证。

items.en: French calibre, recorded by the mid-16th century and perhaps in the late 15th, named the inside diameter of a gun barrel. English borrowed it as caliber in the 1580s.
items.cn: 法语 calibre 在 16 世纪中期有记录，也许可早到 15 世纪晚期，指炮管的内直径。英语在 16 世纪 80 年代把它借入为 caliber。

items.en: It is often said that calibre goes back to Arabic qalib 'a mold for casting'. Standard references repeat this with caution: Barnhart notes that Spanish and Italian forms appear too late to serve as intermediate links, and no documentary evidence supports the Arabic route.
items.cn: 常有人说 calibre 可追溯到阿拉伯语 qalib“铸造用的模具”。通行词源资料转述时都带保留：Barnhart 指出西班牙语和意大利语形式出现太晚，无法充当中间环节；也没有文献证据支持这条阿拉伯路径。

items.en: A still deeper link to Greek kalapous 'wooden shoe' is sometimes proposed. It is speculative and not accepted in standard etymological references, so it should be treated as uncertain rather than as fact.
items.cn: 偶尔还有人把它更往上联系到希腊语 kalapous“木鞋”。这属于推测，通行词源资料并不接受，因此应当作存疑处理，不能当作事实。

items.en: A rival 19th-century explanation derives calibre from Medieval Latin qua libra 'of what weight', from quis 'which' and libra 'balance'. This is also a hypothesis, not a settled fact.
items.cn: 19 世纪还有一种竞争性解释，认为 calibre 来自中古拉丁语 qua libra“按什么重量”，由 quis“哪一个”和 libra“天平”构成。这同样只是假说，并非定论。

items.en: Calibrate was formed in English in 1839 from caliber + -ate, meaning 'determine the caliber of'. By 1869 it also meant 'determine the relative value of the parts of an arbitrary scale'.
items.cn: calibrate 于 1839 年在英语中由 caliber + -ate 构成，意为“测定……的口径”。到 1869 年，它也指“确定任意刻度上各部分的相对数值”。

items.en: Calibration is recorded in 1854 as the noun of action of calibrate. The sense moved from measuring a bore to setting any scale, then to adjusting instruments, models, and even human confidence. The deeper origin of caliber remains uncertain.
items.cn: calibration 于 1854 年作为 calibrate 的行为名词出现。词义从测量口径扩展到设定任何刻度，再扩展到调整仪器、模型，甚至人的信心。caliber 的更早来源仍然存疑。

note.en: The look-alikes are the measuring and counting words that share the cal- shape; the near-meaning group contains words for adjustment and checking against a standard.
note.cn: 形近词是共享 cal- 外形的测量与计数词；近义词组则包含调整和对照标准检查类的词。

entries.definition: the inside diameter of a gun barrel, or the level of someone's ability. It is the noun from which calibrate was formed, not the act of adjusting.
entries.definitionCN: 炮管口径，或某人的能力水准。它是 calibrate 所由构成的名词，不是调整行为本身。

entries.definition: an instrument for measuring external or internal diameters. It is a measuring device, while calibration is the adjustment of a scale.
entries.definitionCN: 测量外径或内径的量具。它是测量工具，而 calibration 是对刻度的调整。

entries.definition: the act or result of computing with numbers. It shares the cal- beginning but comes from calculus 'pebble', not from caliber.
entries.definitionCN: 用数字计算的行为或结果。它共享 cal- 开头，但来自 calculus“石子”，并非来自 caliber。

entries.definition: to adjust an instrument against a standard. It is the verb; calibration adds -ion and names the act or its result.
entries.definitionCN: 对照标准调整仪器。它是动词；calibration 加 -ion，表示行为或结果。

entries.definition: a change made to fit a condition or purpose. It is broader than calibration and does not require a known standard.
entries.definitionCN: 为适应某条件或目的而作的改变。它比 calibration 宽泛，不要求有已知标准。

entries.definition: the adjustment of an instrument or system for best performance, especially by changing frequency. Calibration aims at accurate readings rather than optimal performance.
entries.definitionCN: 为获得最佳性能而调整仪器或系统，尤指改变频率。calibration 追求读数准确，而不是性能最优。

entries.definition: making things conform to one shared standard, often across an industry. It is a collective process; calibration is usually a local measurement adjustment.
entries.definitionCN: 使事物符合一个共同标准，常跨行业进行。它是集体过程；calibration 通常是局部的测量调整。

entries.definition: the act of checking that something is true or accurate. It tests the reading but does not necessarily adjust the instrument.
entries.definitionCN: 检查某事物是否真实或准确的行为。它检验读数，但未必调整仪器。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real gun-bore origin, the real suffix and the real laboratory collocations of calibration.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的炮口径来源、真实的后缀，以及 calibration 真实的实验室搭配。

normal.en: caliber = the bore of a gun. Calibration began as measuring that fixed width, then became setting any scale to a standard.
normal.cn: caliber 就是炮管口径。calibration 从测量这个固定宽度开始，后来变成把任何刻度对准标准。

normal.en: calibrate + -ion: the verb names the adjusting, and the noun names the act or the state it produces.
normal.cn: calibrate + -ion：动词命名调整动作，名词命名行为或它产生的状态。

normal.en: Out of calibration is the standard warning that an instrument's readings can no longer be trusted.
normal.cn: out of calibration 是标准警示语：仪器的读数不再可信。

normal.en: A calibration curve is the visible result of calibration: a line tying signal to true value.
normal.cn: calibration curve 是校准的可视结果：一条把信号与真值绑在一起的线。

normal.en: Calibration and calculation look alike but have different roots: caliber is a bore, calculus is a pebble.
normal.cn: calibration 与 calculation 形似，但词根不同：caliber 是口径，calculus 是石子。

abstract.en: Picture a standard ruler laid beside a dial: every mark on the dial is pushed until it lines up.
abstract.cn: 想象一把标准尺贴在刻度盘旁：盘上的每个标记都被推到对齐的位置。

abstract.en: Picture a scale with a known weight on one side: the needle is moved until it reads that weight.
abstract.cn: 想象一台秤的一边放着已知重量的砝码：指针被调到能读出这个重量。

abstract.en: Picture a metronome set to 100 beats: the setting is not the music, but it makes the music trustworthy.
abstract.cn: 想象把节拍器设到每分钟 100 拍：这个设定不是音乐，却让音乐变得可信。

examples.en: The laboratory keeps a log of every calibration performed on its balances.
examples.cn: 实验室为天平所做的每一次校准都保留记录。

examples.en: Without regular calibration, the sensor's readings drift away from the true value.
examples.cn: 如果不定期校准，传感器的读数就会偏离真实值。

examples.en: The forecasters measured the calibration of their confidence over a full year.
examples.cn: 预报员用整整一年时间测量自己信心的校准程度。

dict_mnemonic.text: “卡里布瑞申”——卡（ca）里（li）布（bra）瑞（tion），用卡尺卡住标准布一量，刻度就准了 → calibration 校准

root: 英语 caliber/calibre“炮口径”（16 世纪经法语 calibre 借入），calibrate“测定口径、校准”+ -ion；calibre 更深来源存疑：阿拉伯 qalib“模具”说缺乏证据，另有中古拉丁 qua libra“按何重量”说。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all repeat one gesture: a reading is brought into line with a fixed reference, whether the scale belongs to an instrument, a model, a standard, or a person's confidence.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都在重复同一个动作：让读数与一个固定参照对齐——无论这条刻度属于仪器、模型、标准，还是人的信心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a standard laid against a scale, with every mark pushed into line.
core.cn: 核心意象：把标准贴到刻度上，把每个标记推到对齐的位置。

branches.en: ACT AND STATE: the adjustment and the trustworthy condition it leaves behind are the same noun.
branches.cn: 行为与状态：调整动作和它留下的可信状态，由同一个名词表示。

branches.en: THE SCALE ITSELF: fixing where the divisions sit produces the reference curve used for later readings.
branches.cn: 刻度本身：确定分格的位置，就产生了供后续读数使用的参照曲线。

branches.en: SYSTEMS AND STANDARDS: device parameters and institutional rules are both brought into line.
branches.cn: 系统与标准：设备参数和机构规则，都被调到一致。

branches.en: MODELS AND MINDS: a model's output and a person's confidence can both be checked against reality.
branches.cn: 模型与心智：模型的输出和人的信心，都可以对照现实来检验。

branches.en: THE ORIGINAL BORE: the oldest sense measured a gun barrel, and its shape survives in every later use.
branches.cn: 最初的口径：最古老的义项测量炮管，这个形状留在后来每一种用法里。

intro.en: Calibration is built from an English verb and a Latin suffix: calibrate + -ion. The productive step is -ion; the base calibr- is frozen inside caliber, whose own origin is disputed.
intro.cn: calibration 由英语动词加拉丁后缀构成：calibrate + -ion。有能产性的一步是 -ion；词基 calibr- 凝固在 caliber 内部，而 caliber 本身的来源存在争议。

latinIntro.en: There is no certain Latin ancestor for calibr-. The two rival explanations are Arabic qalib 'mold' and Medieval Latin qua libra 'of what weight'. The Latin side of the second hypothesis is listed below; it is a hypothesis, not an established root.
latinIntro.cn: calibr- 没有确证的拉丁祖先。两种竞争性解释是阿拉伯语 qalib“模具”和中古拉丁语 qua libra“按什么重量”。下面列出第二种假说中的拉丁成分；它只是假说，不是已确立的词根。

items.meaning: the act or result of calibrating
items.meaningCN: 校准；标定（-ion 表示行为）
items.example: The calibration of the instrument is complete.
items.exampleCN: 仪器的校准已经完成。

items.meaning: to determine a caliber; to adjust a scale against a standard
items.meaningCN: 测定口径；校准（-ate 构成动词）
items.example: They calibrated the sensor before the test.
items.exampleCN: 测试前他们对传感器做了校准。

items.meaning: the inside diameter of a barrel; degree of quality
items.meaningCN: 口径；（人的）水准、才干
items.example: The rifle is of a small caliber.
items.exampleCN: 这支步枪口径较小。

items.meaning: same as caliber; also used figuratively for quality
items.meaningCN: caliber 的英式拼写；也用于比喻“水准”
items.example: The committee is looking for someone of her calibre.
items.exampleCN: 委员会正在找像她这种水准的人。

items.structure: probably from caliber, with a variant ending
items.meaning: an instrument for measuring diameters
items.meaningCN: 卡尺；测径器（可能由 caliber 变体而来）
items.example: Use the caliper to measure the pipe's diameter.
items.exampleCN: 用卡尺测量管子的直径。

items.meaning: to calibrate again
items.meaningCN: 重新校准（re- 表示“再次”）
items.example: The machine recalibrates itself after each restart.
items.exampleCN: 每次重启后机器都会自动重新校准。

items.meaning: a second or fresh calibration
items.meaningCN: 重新校准（再次进行的校准）
items.example: A recalibration was needed after the move.
items.exampleCN: 搬动之后需要重新校准。

items.meaning: a device or person that calibrates
items.meaningCN: 校准器；校准员（-or 表示施动者）
items.example: The calibrator generates a known signal.
items.exampleCN: 校准器会生成一个已知信号。

items.meaning: adjusted against a standard
items.meaningCN: 已校准的；标定过的（-ed 构成分词形容词）
items.example: All calibrated instruments are stored separately.
items.exampleCN: 所有已校准的仪器都单独存放。

items.meaning: of a smaller caliber than the standard
items.meaningCN: 次口径的；小于标准口径的（sub- 表示“低于”）
items.example: The training round uses a subcaliber insert.
items.exampleCN: 训练弹使用一个次口径内衬。

latinEntries.structure: libra (Latin noun: balance, pair of scales; pound)
latinEntries.meaning: a balance or unit of weight; the weight element in the rival qua libra hypothesis
latinEntries.meaningCN: 天平；重量单位；竞争性 qua libra 假说中的“重量”成分

latinEntries.meaning: 'of what weight'; Mahn's 19th-century alternative source for caliber, not proven
latinEntries.meaningCN: “按什么重量”；Mahn 在 19 世纪提出的 caliber 替代来源，未获确证

latinEntries.meaning: a standard measure; related measuring vocabulary, but not the source of caliber
latinEntries.meaningCN: 标准量度；属于测量词汇的对照项，但不是 caliber 的来源

definition_zh: 候选人；申请人；考生；候选对象
definition_en: a person who seeks a position, or a thing being considered for a particular role
core_image: 一个穿雪白长袍的人站在罗马广场的石阶上，等人叫他的名字
scene: Each candidate for the doctoral program must present a research proposal at the interview.
sceneCN: 这里 candidate 是「博士候选人／学位申请人」（第 9 个义项：进入学位候选阶段的人）；句意：每位博士项目申请人都必须在面试时陈述研究计划。场景要点：白袍意象退到背景，留下一个站在评审面前、等待被选中的人。

pos.zh: 候选人；申请人；考生；候选对象

senses.title: A person competing for elected office
senses.titleCN: 选举候选人：等选民投票的人
senses.definition: a person who is competing for an elected office
senses.definitionCN: 竞选公职的人
senses.example: The party nominated a young candidate for mayor.
senses.exampleCN: 该党提名了一位年轻人为市长候选人。
senses.why: Candidatus named the white-robed office-seeker in Rome. The -ate noun keeps that role: someone put forward and waiting for a vote.
senses.whyCN: candidatus 在罗马指穿白袍的求官者。-ate 名词保留了这个角色：一个被推出来、等待投票的人。

senses.title: A person applying for a job
senses.titleCN: 职位申请人：把名字交到雇主手里
senses.definition: a person who applies for a job or appointment
senses.definitionCN: 申请工作或职位的人
senses.example: We interviewed five candidates for the post.
senses.exampleCN: 我们面试了五位职位申请人。
senses.why: Election by vote widened to selection by an employer. The white robe is gone, but the structure remains: a person formally put forward for a place.
senses.whyCN: 由投票选举扩展到由雇主挑选。白袍没有了，但结构还在：一个人被正式推到某个位置前面。

senses.title: A person taking an examination
senses.titleCN: 考生：站在考试这道门前的人
senses.definition: a person taking an examination
senses.definitionCN: 参加考试的人
senses.example: Candidates must bring photo identification.
senses.exampleCN: 考生必须携带带照片的身份证明。
senses.why: An exam is a gate to a place, so the person at the gate is called a candidate. British usage keeps this school and exam sense strongly.
senses.whyCN: 考试是通往某个位置的关口，站在关口上的人就叫 candidate。英式英语很强地保留了这个学校与考试义。

senses.title: A person nominated or considered
senses.titleCN: 被提名者：进入考虑名单
senses.definition: a person nominated or considered for an honor or role
senses.definitionCN: 被提名或考虑授予荣誉、担任角色的人
senses.example: She is a candidate for the chair of the committee.
senses.exampleCN: 她是委员会主席的候选人。
senses.why: The word does not require an election; anyone formally considered for a role fits the slot.
senses.whyCN: 这个词不要求真有选举；任何被正式考虑担任某角色的人都符合这个位置。

senses.title: The person likely to fit
senses.titleCN: 可能合适的人选：最像那个位置的人
senses.definition: a person likely to be suitable for something
senses.definitionCN: 很可能适合某事的人
senses.example: He is the likeliest candidate for the task.
senses.exampleCN: 他是这项任务最可能的人选。
senses.why: Once 'considered for' is loosened, the noun means 'the one that fits'. The selection frame stays; the formal process may disappear.
senses.whyCN: 一旦“被考虑”这层放松，名词就表示“最合适的那一个”。选择的框架还在，正式程序却可能消失。

senses.title: An option being considered
senses.titleCN: 候选方案：地点、计划也可参选
senses.definition: a plan, place, or option being considered for selection
senses.definitionCN: 被考虑选用的计划、地点或选项
senses.example: Three candidate sites were compared for the new library.
senses.exampleCN: 新图书馆比较了三个候选地点。
senses.why: The role of 'thing waiting to be chosen' is transferred from people to options. This is the productive modern extension.
senses.whyCN: “等待被选中的东西”这一角色从人转到了选项。这是这个词能产的现代扩展。

senses.title: A substance singled out for testing
senses.titleCN: 候选基因／候选药物：被推出来待验证
senses.definition: in science, a gene, drug, or substance singled out for testing
senses.definitionCN: 科学研究中被挑出来待检验的基因、药物或物质
senses.example: The team identified a candidate gene for the disorder.
senses.exampleCN: 团队找到了与这种疾病相关的候选基因。
senses.why: Research also selects. A candidate gene is not yet confirmed; it is the one put forward for testing, exactly the Roman role applied to molecules.
senses.whyCN: 科研也要挑选。候选基因尚未被确认；它是被推出来接受检验的那一个，正是罗马角色被用到分子上。

senses.title: The leading explanation under investigation
senses.titleCN: 最可能的病因：解释也在竞争
senses.definition: the most likely cause or explanation under investigation
senses.definitionCN: 调查中最可能的病因或解释
senses.example: Poor drainage is the leading candidate for the collapse.
senses.exampleCN: 排水不良是这次坍塌最可能的原因。
senses.why: In diagnosis and investigation, explanations compete. The likely one is the candidate, still awaiting confirmation.
senses.whyCN: 在诊断和调查中，各种解释会相互竞争。最可能的那个就是 candidate，仍然等待确认。

senses.title: A doctoral candidate
senses.titleCN: 博士候选人：进入学位最后阶段
senses.definition: a student who has completed coursework and is writing a dissertation
senses.definitionCN: 已完成课程、正在撰写学位论文的学生
senses.example: She became a candidate after passing the qualifying exam.
senses.exampleCN: 她通过资格考核后成为博士候选人。
senses.why: The degree has stages, and the final stage is a supervised piece of work. The student is now formally put forward for the degree, so the old word marks status.
senses.whyCN: 学位分阶段，最后阶段是一项受指导的研究工作。此时学生被正式推到学位面前，这个古老的词就用来标记身份。

intro.en: Candidate is a Latin borrowing, not an English derivative: the white-robed Roman office-seeker gave the word its first meaning, and the color is the key to the whole family.
intro.cn: candidate 是拉丁借词，不是英语派生词：罗马穿白袍的求官者给了它最初的意义，而“白”是理解整个词族的关键。

items.en: candere meant 'to shine'. From it came candidus 'white, bright', and by extension 'pure, sincere'. The root is PIE *kand- 'to shine'.
items.cn: candere 意为“发光”。由它产生 candidus“白色的、明亮的”，并引申为“纯净、真诚”。词根是原始印欧语 *kand-“发光”。

items.en: candidatus was the past participle of candidare 'to make white', used as a noun for 'one aspiring to office'. Literally it meant 'whitened, white-robed'.
items.cn: candidatus 是 candidare“使变白”的过去分词，作名词指“谋求公职的人”。字面义是“被漂白的、穿白袍的”。

items.en: Office-seekers in Rome wore the toga candida, a gleaming white toga probably whitened with fine chalk. The white was a public display; the later idea that it advertised pure intentions is an inference, not the word's meaning.
items.cn: 罗马的求官者穿 toga candida，一种很可能用细白垩漂白的闪亮白袍。白色是一种公开展示；后来“表示动机纯洁”的说法只是推断，并不是这个词本身的意思。

items.en: English candidate is recorded from about 1600, meaning 'person who seeks or is put forward for an office by election or appointment'. The Latin noun came in whole, without an English verb step.
items.cn: 英语 candidate 约在 1600 年有记录，意为“通过选举或任命谋求、被推举担任公职的人”。拉丁名词整体借入，没有经过英语动词阶段。

items.en: The white robe became a general 'person put forward': first for office, then for any job or exam, then for anything awaiting selection, including sites and genes.
items.cn: 白袍变成了泛指的“被推出来的人”：先指公职，再指任何工作或考试，最后指任何等待挑选的对象，包括地点和基因。

items.en: Modern English uses candidate for elections, employment, exams, research substances, and doctoral status. The same PIE root also gives candid, candle, candor and incandescent; candy is unrelated and comes through Arabic qandi 'crystallized sugar'.
items.cn: 现代英语用 candidate 指选举、求职、考试、科研对象和博士身份。同一原始印欧词根还产生 candid、candle、candor、incandescent；candy 则无关，它经阿拉伯语 qandi“结晶糖”传入。

note.en: The look-alikes share the cand- shape but not always the same history; the near-meaning group contains words for people seeking or proposed for a position.
note.cn: 形近词共享 cand- 外形，但历史未必相同；近义词组则包含谋求或被人提名某个位置的人。

entries.definition: frank and honest; literally 'white, bright'. It comes from the same Latin root as candidate, but it describes openness of speech, not a person seeking office.
entries.definitionCN: 坦率、诚实的；字面义“白、亮”。它与 candidate 同出拉丁词根，但描述的是说话的开放，而不是谋求职位的人。

entries.definition: the state or period of being a candidate. The -cy suffix makes an abstract noun of status, while candidate names the person.
entries.definitionCN: 候选资格或候选人身份、任期。-cy 后缀构成身份抽象名词，而 candidate 指人本身。

entries.definition: a sweet food made with sugar. It looks like candid but has no connection: it comes through Old French from Arabic qandi 'crystallized sugar'.
entries.definitionCN: 用糖制成的甜食。它看起来像 candid，却毫无关联：它经古法语来自阿拉伯语 qandi“结晶糖”。

entries.definition: the quality of being frank and open. It belongs with candid, not with candidate, although all three share the Latin root for 'shining white'.
entries.definitionCN: 坦率、直言的性质。它与 candid 同族，而不与 candidate 同义，尽管三者共享拉丁语“发白光”的词根。

entries.definition: a person who applies for a job, place, or benefit. It stresses the act of applying, while candidate stresses being put forward for selection.
entries.definitionCN: 申请工作、名额或福利的人。它强调“申请”这个动作，而 candidate 强调“被推出来接受挑选”。

entries.definition: a person formally proposed for an office or honor. The naming is done by someone else, which is often clearer than candidate.
entries.definitionCN: 被正式提名担任公职或获得荣誉的人。提名由他人完成，这一点常比 candidate 更明确。

entries.definition: a person competing to win a prize or position. It stresses rivalry and struggle, not the formal selection process.
entries.definitionCN: 竞争奖项或位置的人。它强调竞争和争夺，而不是正式的选拔程序。

entries.definition: a person who hopes to attain a position or honor. It is formal and stresses ambition rather than nomination.
entries.definitionCN: 希望获得某个位置或荣誉的人。它较书面，强调抱负，而不是被提名。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real white toga, the real suffixes and the real modern uses of candidate.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的白袍、真实的后缀，以及 candidate 真实的现代用法。

normal.en: candidatus = white-robed. The Roman office-seeker wore a chalk-whitened toga, and the word followed the person into English.
normal.cn: candidatus 就是“穿白袍的”。罗马求官者穿用白垩漂白的长袍，这个词跟着这个人进入英语。

normal.en: candidate + -cy = candidacy: the person becomes the status.
normal.cn: candidate + -cy = candidacy：人变成了身份状态。

normal.en: Candidate for is the key pattern: the word always opens a slot that someone or something is trying to fill.
normal.cn: candidate for 是关键句式：这个词总是打开一个位置，等人或物去填。

normal.en: Candidate gene and candidate site show the modern extension from people to things under consideration.
normal.cn: candidate gene 和 candidate site 展示了从人扩展到“被考虑之物”的现代用法。

normal.en: Candy looks like candid but is unrelated; keeping that pair apart prevents a false 'sweet' association.
normal.cn: candy 看起来像 candid，但毫无关联；把这对词分开，可以避免错误的“甜”联想。

abstract.en: Picture a line of white-robed men on the steps of a Roman forum, each waiting for the crowd to call a name.
abstract.cn: 想象罗马广场石阶上站着一排穿白袍的人，每个人都在等人群叫出一个名字。

abstract.en: Picture a form with one empty slot and several name cards laid beside it: only one card will be inserted.
abstract.cn: 想象一张表格上有一个空位，旁边摆着几张姓名卡：最终只有一张会被插进去。

abstract.en: Picture a laboratory shelf of labeled samples, each marked 'test me': those are candidate genes.
abstract.cn: 想象实验室架子上摆着一排贴了标签的样本，每个都写着“待检验”：那些就是 candidate genes。

examples.en: Voters compare the candidates' positions on health care and taxes.
examples.cn: 选民比较各位候选人在医疗和税收上的立场。

examples.en: The committee will shortlist three candidates for the position by Friday.
examples.cn: 委员会将在周五前筛出三位职位候选人。

examples.en: The enzyme is a strong candidate for the cause of the disease.
examples.cn: 这种酶是导致该疾病的一个很有力的候选原因。

dict_mnemonic.text: “看迪得特”——看（can）迪（di）得（da）特（te），一群人站成一排等投票，白袍最显眼 → candidate 候选人

root: 拉丁 candidatus“穿白袍的人”，来自 candidus“白色、明亮的”，再溯 candere“发光”（原始印欧语 *kand-“发光”）。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one Roman image: a person in white is put forward and waits to be chosen; later the same slot is filled by jobs, exam places, options, genes, and a degree.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个罗马意象展开：一个穿白袍的人被推出来，等待被选中；后来这个位置又被职位、考试名额、选项、基因和学位填上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white-robed person standing forward, waiting to be chosen.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个穿白袍的人站到前面，等待被选中。

branches.en: ELECTION AND NOMINATION: the original office-seeker and anyone formally considered for a role.
branches.cn: 选举与提名：最初的求官者，以及任何被正式考虑担任某角色的人。

branches.en: GATES TO A PLACE: a job application and an examination both put a person before a selection gate.
branches.cn: 通往位置的关口：求职和考试，都把一个人放到选拔的门前。

branches.en: THE LIKELY ONE: the person who fits and the explanation that fits are both the leading candidate.
branches.cn: 最可能的那个：合适的人与合适的解释，都是 leading candidate。

branches.en: THINGS THAT COMPETE: sites, plans, genes and drugs are all put forward for selection or testing.
branches.cn: 参与竞争的事物：地点、计划、基因、药物，都被推出来接受挑选或检验。

branches.en: DEGREE STATUS: a doctoral candidate is formally put forward for a degree.
branches.cn: 学位身份：博士候选人被正式推到学位面前。

intro.en: Candidate is a borrowed Latin noun, not a live English derivative. Its ending -ate belongs to the Latin participle, and English later adds -cy to make candidacy. The base cand- is fossilized.
intro.cn: candidate 是借入的拉丁名词，不是活的英语派生词。词尾 -ate 属于拉丁分词，英语后来又加 -cy 构成 candidacy。词基 cand- 已经凝固。

latinIntro.en: Latin candere 'to shine' is the source of a family that includes candidus, candidatus, candid, candor and candle. English borrowed the words at different times, so the root appears as cand- or as the whole stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 candere“发光”是一个词族的源头，包括 candidus、candidatus、candid、candor 和 candle。英语在不同时期借入这些词，因此词根有时以 cand- 出现，有时以完整词干出现。

items.meaning: a person put forward for office or selection
items.meaningCN: 候选人；申请人（-ate 构成指人名词）
items.example: Two candidates are running for the seat.
items.exampleCN: 两人正在竞选这个席位。

items.meaning: the state of being a candidate
items.meaningCN: 候选资格；候选人身份（-cy 构成状态抽象名词）
items.example: She announced her candidacy in March.
items.exampleCN: 她在三月宣布参选。

items.meaning: frank, open, honest
items.meaningCN: 坦率的；直言不讳的
items.example: He gave a candid account of his mistakes.
items.exampleCN: 他坦率地讲述了自己的错误。

items.meaning: in a frank way
items.meaningCN: 坦率地（-ly 构成方式副词）
items.example: She spoke candidly about her doubts.
items.exampleCN: 她坦率地谈了自己的疑虑。

items.meaning: the quality of being frank
items.meaningCN: 坦率（-ness 构成性质名词）
items.example: The candidness of the report surprised readers.
items.exampleCN: 报告的坦率让读者吃惊。

items.meaning: frankness; open honesty
items.meaningCN: 坦率；光明磊落（-or 构成性质名词）
items.example: He answered with unexpected candor.
items.exampleCN: 他以出人意料的坦率回答。

items.structure: same PIE root *kand-, not derived from candidate
items.meaning: a stick of wax with a wick that gives light
items.meaningCN: 蜡烛（同出 *kand-“发光”词根，但不是由 candidate 派生）
items.example: A candle burned on the table.
items.exampleCN: 桌上点着一支蜡烛。

items.meaning: the SI unit of luminous intensity
items.meaningCN: 坎德拉（发光强度的国际单位；同出“发光”词根）
items.example: Luminous intensity is measured in candelas.
items.exampleCN: 发光强度以坎德拉计量。

items.meaning: glowing with heat; brilliantly bright
items.meaningCN: 白炽的；发亮光的（in- + candescere“变亮”+ -ent）
items.example: The old bulb used an incandescent filament.
items.exampleCN: 那只旧灯泡使用白炽灯丝。

items.meaning: a large hanging light with branches for several bulbs or candles
items.meaningCN: 枝形吊灯（同出“发光”词根，经法语借入）
items.example: A chandelier hung above the dining table.
items.exampleCN: 餐桌上方挂着一盏枝形吊灯。

latinEntries.meaning: to shine, to be bright
latinEntries.meaningCN: 发光；发亮

latinEntries.meaning: white, bright; pure, sincere
latinEntries.meaningCN: 白色的、明亮的；纯净的、真诚的

latinEntries.meaning: whitened, white-robed; one seeking office
latinEntries.meaningCN: 被漂白的、穿白袍的；谋求公职的人

latinEntries.meaning: brightness; frankness
latinEntries.meaningCN: 明亮；坦率

definition_en: the power or ability to do something, or the range of things a person or system can do
core_image: 一双手伸进箱子，够到最里面的东西并把它拿出来
scene: The new telescope has the capability to detect light from the earliest galaxies.
sceneCN: 这里 capability 是「功能／性能」（第 3 个义项：设备能做到的事）；句意：这台新望远镜具备探测最早星系光线的能力。场景要点：镜头深入夜空，把极暗的光收进来，强调“能做到”而非“能装多少”。

senses.title: The power to do something
senses.titleCN: 一般能力：手够得到，也拿得动
senses.definition: the power or ability to do something
senses.definitionCN: 做某事的力量或能力
senses.example: She has the capability to lead a large team.
senses.exampleCN: 她有能力领导一支大团队。
senses.why: Capabilis meant 'able to grasp or hold'. The -ity suffix turns that adjective into the quality, so the holding hand becomes the power to carry a task through.
senses.whyCN: capabilis 意为“能抓住、能容纳的”。-ity 后缀把这个形容词变成性质，于是“握住的手”变成“把任务做到底的力量”。

senses.title: Undeveloped ability
senses.titleCN: 潜力：手还能拿更多
senses.definition: an undeveloped ability that may be realized later
senses.definitionCN: 尚未发展、但以后可能实现的能力
senses.example: The program helps students discover capabilities they did not know they had.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目帮助学生发现他们不知道自己拥有的能力。
senses.why: A hand can hold more than it is currently holding. The noun therefore names capacity not yet used, which is why the plural often means latent powers.
senses.whyCN: 一只手能拿的东西比它现在拿着的更多。因此这个名词指尚未被使用的能力，这也是复数常表示“潜在才能”的原因。

senses.title: What a device can do
senses.titleCN: 功能／性能：机器能做的事
senses.definition: the range of things a device or system is able to do
senses.definitionCN: 设备或系统能够做到的事情的范围
senses.example: The telescope has the capability to detect very faint light.
senses.exampleCN: 这台望远镜有能力探测非常微弱的光。
senses.why: Tools are treated as hands: what they can reach and hold defines them. The noun moves from a person's power to a machine's functions.
senses.whyCN: 工具被当作手：它们能伸到、能拿住什么，就定义了它们。名词于是从人的力量转到机器的功能。

senses.title: Developed professional skill
senses.titleCN: 专业本领：训练出来的够取范围
senses.definition: a person's developed skill or competence in a field
senses.definitionCN: 某人在某一领域已发展的技能或胜任力
senses.example: Her capabilities as a translator are well known.
senses.exampleCN: 她作为译者的本领广为人知。
senses.why: Training turns a general power into a specific reach. The plural names the set of things a person can actually do well.
senses.whyCN: 训练把一般的力量变成具体的够取范围。复数命名的是一个人真正能做好的那一组事情。

senses.title: Military power to act
senses.titleCN: 军事能力：国家的手能伸多远
senses.definition: the military power to carry out an operation
senses.definitionCN: 执行军事行动的能力
senses.example: The country announced a new long-range strike capability.
senses.exampleCN: 该国宣布具备新的远程打击能力。
senses.why: States are treated as agents with hands. What they can reach across distance is their capability, so the word becomes a measure of strategic reach.
senses.whyCN: 国家被当作有手的行动者。它们能跨越距离够到什么，就是它们的 capability，因此这个词成为战略触达的度量。

senses.title: The power to produce at all
senses.titleCN: 生产能力：能不能做，而非能做多少
senses.definition: the power to produce goods or results, as distinct from the maximum amount
senses.definitionCN: 生产商品或成果的能力，区别于最大产量
senses.example: The factory has the capability to switch to electric parts.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂有能力转产电动部件。
senses.why: Here capability answers 'can it do this at all', not 'how many can it hold'. That is the line between capability and capacity.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 capability 回答的是“它到底能不能做”，而不是“它能装多少”。这正是 capability 与 capacity 的分界线。

senses.title: The range of operations a system offers
senses.titleCN: 技术能力：可执行操作的清单
senses.definition: the set of operations a technique or instrument can perform
senses.definitionCN: 某项技术或仪器能够执行的一组操作
senses.example: The software's capabilities include voice search and offline maps.
senses.exampleCN: 这款软件的功能包括语音搜索和离线地图。
senses.why: Each operation is something the system can reach. The plural lists the reachable actions, turning an abstract power into a checklist.
senses.whyCN: 每一项操作都是系统能够够到的东西。复数把这些可达动作列成清单，把抽象的能力变成可勾选的条目。

senses.title: An organization's power to carry out its mandate
senses.titleCN: 机构执行力：能不能真正办到
senses.definition: an organization's power to respond and carry out its mandate
senses.definitionCN: 组织作出反应并完成其职责的能力
senses.example: The agency lacks the capability to inspect every site.
senses.exampleCN: 该机构没有能力检查每一个场地。
senses.why: An institution is also an agent. Its reach is measured by what it can actually carry out, so the word names operational power rather than intention.
senses.whyCN: 机构也是行动者。它的触达由它实际能办成的事来衡量，因此这个词命名的是执行力量，而不是意图。

senses.title: A right held by a computing process
senses.titleCN: 计算机能力／权限：把“能力”做成可传递的令牌
senses.definition: in computing, a right or token that allows a process to perform an action
senses.definitionCN: 计算机中允许某个进程执行某项操作的权利或令牌
senses.example: The sandbox grants only the capabilities the program needs.
senses.exampleCN: 沙盒只授予程序所需的能力权限。
senses.why: In capability-based security, an abstract ability is made into a concrete object that can be held and passed. The old 'hold' image becomes literal again.
senses.whyCN: 在基于能力的安全模型中，抽象的能力被做成一个可以持有、可以传递的具体对象。古老的“握住”意象又变回了字面意义。

intro.en: Capability is an English derivative of capable, which came from Late Latin capabilis. Its Latin base differs from the base of capacity, and that difference explains the modern division of work between the two words.
intro.cn: capability 是 capable 的英语派生词，而 capable 来自晚期拉丁语 capabilis。它的拉丁词基与 capacity 的词基不同，这个差异解释了现代英语中两个词的分工。

items.en: capere meant 'to grasp, lay hold of, take, catch; take in, hold; be large enough for; comprehend'. The root is PIE *kap- 'to grasp'.
items.cn: capere 意为“抓住、握住、拿取、接住；收进、容纳；大到足以装下；理解”。词根是原始印欧语 *kap-“抓”。

items.en: capax (genitive capacis) meant 'able to hold much, broad, roomy', also 'receptive, fit for'. Its noun capacitas produced English capacity in the early 15th century.
items.cn: capax（属格 capacis）意为“能装很多的、宽的、宽敞的”，也表示“能接受的、适合的”。其名词 capacitas 在 15 世纪初产生英语 capacity。

items.en: Late Latin capabilis meant 'receptive; able to grasp or hold' and was used especially by theologians. It passed through French capable into English capable in the 1590s.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 capabilis 意为“能接受的；能抓住或容纳的”，尤其为神学家使用。它经法语 capable 于 16 世纪 90 年代进入英语。

items.en: English added -ity, from Latin -itatem, to capable, producing capability in the 1580s with the sense 'quality of being capable, power to do'. The suffix names a state or quality.
items.cn: 英语给 capable 加上来自拉丁 -itatem 的 -ity，于 16 世纪 80 年代构成 capability，意为“有能力的状态、做事的力量”。这个后缀命名状态或性质。

items.en: Capax and capacitas answer 'how much fits'; capabilis and capability answer 'what one can do'. Because the Latin bases differ, English capacity specializes in volume and containment, while capability specializes in performance.
items.cn: capax 和 capacitas 回答“能装多少”；capabilis 和 capability 回答“能做什么”。由于拉丁词基不同，英语 capacity 专管容量与容纳，而 capability 专管做事与表现。

items.en: Capabilities in the sense 'undeveloped faculty or property' is recorded from 1778. Modern English extends the word to devices, organizations, the military, and computing permissions, while keeping the 'can do' core.
